265.s:
puṣkara uvāca
vināyakopasṛṣṭānāṃ snānaṃ sarvakaraṃ vade /
vināyakaḥ karmavighnasiddhyarthaṃ viniyojitaḥ //
265.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
विनायकोपसृष्टानां स्नानं सर्वकरं वदे /
विनायकः कर्मविघ्नसिद्ध्यर्थं विनियोजितः //
265.m: Puṣkara said: / I shall state the bath that accomplishes everything for those afflicted by Vināyaka. / Vināyaka was appointed for the achievement of obstacles to actions

265.s:
gaṇānāmādhipatye ca keśaveśapitāmahaiḥ /
svapnevagāhate 'tyarthaṃ jalaṃ muṇḍāṃś ca paśyati //
:p 469
265.d:
गणानामाधिपत्ये च केशवेशपितामहैः /
स्वप्नेवगाहते ऽत्यर्थं जलं मुण्डांश् च पश्यति //
:प् 469
265.m:
and to the overlordship of the gaṇas by Keśava, Īśa, and the Grandfather [Brahmā]. / [One so afflicted] plunges exceedingly into water in dreams and sees shaven-headed men;
[Page 469]

265.s:
vināyakopasṛṣṭastu kravyādānadhirohati /
vrajamānas tathātmānaṃ manyate 'nugatamparaiḥ //
265.d:
विनायकोपसृष्टस्तु क्रव्यादानधिरोहति /
व्रजमानस् तथात्मानं मन्यते ऽनुगतम्परैः //
265.m: afflicted by Vināyaka, he mounts carnivorous animals, / and while walking, he imagines himself pursued by others;

265.s:
vimanā viphalārambhaḥ saṃsīdatyanimittataḥ /
kanyā varaṃ na cāpnoti na cāpatyaṃ varāṅganā //
265.d:
विमना विफलारम्भः संसीदत्यनिमित्ततः /
कन्या वरं न चाप्नोति न चापत्यं वराङ्गना //
265.m: he is dejected, his undertakings are fruitless, and he falters without cause; / an unmarried woman finds no groom, and a noble woman bears no child;

265.s:
ācāryatvaṃ śrotriyaś ca na śiṣyo 'dhyayanaṃ labhet /
dhanī na lābhamāpnoti na kṛṣiñca kṛṣībalaḥ //
265.d:
आचार्यत्वं श्रोत्रियश् च न शिष्यो ऽध्ययनं लभेत् /
धनी न लाभमाप्नोति न कृषिञ्च कृषीबलः //
265.m: the learned Brahmin does not attain the rank of teacher, and the pupil does not gain study; / the wealthy man obtains no gain, and the cultivator reaps no harvest;

265.s:
rājā rājyaṃ na cāpnoti snapanantasya kārayet /
hastapuṣyāśvayuksaumye vaiṣṇave bhadrapīṭhake(1) //
265.d:
राजा राज्यं न चाप्नोति स्नपनन्तस्य कारयेत् /
हस्तपुष्याश्वयुक्सौम्ये वैष्णवे भद्रपीठके(1) //
265.m: the king does not attain kingship. One should cause his bath to be performed / under the asterisms Hasta, Puṣya, Aśvayuj, Saumya, or Vaiṣṇava, on an auspicious seat.

265.s:
gaurasarṣapakalkena sājyenotsāditasya ca(2) /
sarvauṣadhaiḥ sarvagandhaiḥ praliptaśirasas tathā //
265.d:
गौरसर्षपकल्केन साज्येनोत्सादितस्य च(2) /
सर्वौषधैः सर्वगन्धैः प्रलिप्तशिरसस् तथा //
265.m: Having rubbed him with a paste of white mustard together with ghee, / and likewise smeared his head with all medicinal herbs and all fragrant substances,

265.s:
caturbhiḥ kalasaiḥ snānanteṣu sarvauṣādhau kṣipet /
aśvasthānādgajasthānādvalmīkāt saṅgamāddhradāt //
265.d:
चतुर्भिः कलसैः स्नानन्तेषु सर्वौषाधौ क्षिपेत् /
अश्वस्थानाद्गजस्थानाद्वल्मीकात् सङ्गमाद्ध्रदात् //
265.m: the bath is performed with four jars; into them he should put all herbs, / and earth from a horse-stable, from an elephant-stable, from an anthill, from a confluence, and from a deep pool.

265.s:
mṛttikāṃ rocanāṅgandhaṅguggulunteṣu nikṣipet /
sahasrākṣaṃ śatadhāramṛṣibhiḥ pāvanaṃ kṛtam //
265.d:
मृत्तिकां रोचनाङ्गन्धङ्गुग्गुलुन्तेषु निक्षिपेत् /
सहस्राक्षं शतधारमृषिभिः पावनं कृतम् //
265.m: He should put earth, rocanā, fragrant perfume, and guggulu into them: / "The thousand-eyed, hundred-streamed [bath], made purifying by the sages:

265.s:
tena tvāmabhiṣiñcāmi pāvamānyaḥ(3) punantu te /
bhagavante varuṇo rājā bhagaṃ sūryo vṛhaspatiḥ //
265.d:
तेन त्वामभिषिञ्चामि पावमान्यः(3) पुनन्तु ते /
भगवन्ते वरुणो राजा भगं सूर्यो वृहस्पतिः //
265.m: with that I consecrate you; may the purifying verses purify you! / May King Varuṇa give you fortune; may Sūrya and Bṛhaspati give you fortune;

265.s:
bhagamindraś ca vāyuś ca bhagaṃ saptarṣayo daduḥ /
yatte keśeṣu daurbhāgyaṃ sīmante yacca mūrdhani //
265.d:
भगमिन्द्रश् च वायुश् च भगं सप्तर्षयो ददुः /
यत्ते केशेषु दौर्भाग्यं सीमन्ते यच्च मूर्धनि //
265.m: may Indra and Vāyu give you fortune; may the Seven Sages give you fortune! / Whatever ill-fortune is in your hair, in your parting, and on your head,

265.s:
lalāṭe karṇayorakṣṇorāpastadghnantu sarvadā /
darbhapiñjalimādāya vāmahaste tato guruḥ //
:n
1 hastapuṣyāśvayuksaumyavaiṣṇaveṣu śubheṣu ceti gha.. , ña..
ca
2 sājyenāsāditasya ceti ka.. , cha.. ca
3 imā āpa iti cha.. , ña..
:p 470
265.d:
ललाटे कर्णयोरक्ष्णोरापस्तद्घ्नन्तु सर्वदा /
दर्भपिञ्जलिमादाय वामहस्ते ततो गुरुः //
:न्
1 हस्तपुष्याश्वयुक्सौम्यवैष्णवेषु शुभेषु चेति घ.. , ञ..
च
2 साज्येनासादितस्य चेति क.. , छ.. च
3 इमा आप इति छ.. , ञ..
:प् 470
265.m:
on your forehead, your ears, and your eyes, may the waters always destroy that!" / Then the guru, taking a bunch of darbha grass in his left hand,
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "under Hasta, Puṣya, Aśvayuj, Saumya, and Vaiṣṇava, and on auspicious [occasions]" in manuscripts gha and ña.]
[Footnote 2: "approached with ghee" in manuscripts ka and cha.]
[Footnote 3: "these waters" in manuscripts cha and ña. Page 470]

265.s:
snātasya sārṣapantailaṃ śruveṇauḍumbareṇa ca /
juhuyānmūrdhani kuśān savyena parigṛhya ca //
265.d:
स्नातस्य सार्षपन्तैलं श्रुवेणौडुम्बरेण च /
जुहुयान्मूर्धनि कुशान् सव्येन परिगृह्य च //
265.m: should offer mustard oil upon the head of the bathed person with a ladle of udumbara wood, / holding the kuśa grasses with the right hand, [saying:]

265.s:
mitaś ca sammitaś caiva tathā śālakakaṇṭakau /
kuṣmāṇḍo rājaputraś ca etaiḥ svāhāsamanvitaiḥ //
265.d:
मितश् च सम्मितश् चैव तथा शालककण्टकौ /
कुष्माण्डो राजपुत्रश् च एतैः स्वाहासमन्वितैः //
265.m: "Mita, Sammita, Śālaka, Kaṇṭaka, / Kuṣmāṇḍa, and Rājaputra"—with these [names] accompanied by "svāhā",

265.s:
nāmabhirbalimantraiś ca namaskārasamanvitaiḥ(1) /
dadyāccatuṣpathe śūrpe kuśānāstīrya sarvataḥ //
265.d:
नामभिर्बलिमन्त्रैश् च नमस्कारसमन्वितैः(1) /
दद्याच्चतुष्पथे शूर्पे कुशानास्तीर्य सर्वतः //
265.m: with the names and offering mantras accompanied by obeisance, / having strewn kuśa grass all around in a winnowing basket at a crossroads, he should offer

265.s:
kṛtākṛtāṃstaṇḍulāṃś ca palalaudanameva ca /
matsyānpaṅkāṃstathaivāmān puṣpaṃ citraṃ surāṃ tridhā //
265.d:
कृताकृतांस्तण्डुलांश् च पललौदनमेव च /
मत्स्यान्पङ्कांस्तथैवामान् पुष्पं चित्रं सुरां त्रिधा //
265.m: cooked and uncooked grains of rice, boiled rice with ground sesamum, / fish from mud as well as raw, flowers of variegated colors, liquor of three kinds,

265.s:
mūlakaṃ pūrikāṃ pūpāṃstathaivaiṇḍavikāsrajaḥ /
dadhyannaṃ pāyasaṃ piṣṭaṃ modakaṃ guḍamarpayet //
265.d:
मूलकं पूरिकां पूपांस्तथैवैण्डविकास्रजः /
दध्यन्नं पायसं पिष्टं मोदकं गुडमर्पयेत् //
265.m: radish, fried cakes, sweet breads, garlands of buns, / curd-rice, milk-rice, flour cakes, sweetmeats, and molasses.

265.s:
vināyakasya jananīmupatiṣṭhettato 'mbikāṃ /
dūrvāsarṣapapuṣpāṇāṃ datvārghyaṃ pūrṇamañjaliṃ //
265.d:
विनायकस्य जननीमुपतिष्ठेत्ततो ऽम्बिकां /
दूर्वासर्षपपुष्पाणां दत्वार्घ्यं पूर्णमञ्जलिं //
265.m: Then he should approach Ambikā, the mother of Vināyaka, / offering a full handful as water offering with dūrvā grass, mustard, and flowers:

265.s:
rūpaṃ dehi yaśo dehi saubhāgyaṃ subhage mama /
putraṃ dehi dhanaṃ dehi sarvān kāmāṃś ca dehi me //
265.d:
रूपं देहि यशो देहि सौभाग्यं सुभगे मम /
पुत्रं देहि धनं देहि सर्वान् कामांश् च देहि मे //
265.m: "Grant beauty, grant fame, grant fortune to me, O fortunate goddess! / Grant a son, grant wealth, and grant all desires to me!"

265.s:
bhojayedbrāhmaṇāndadyādvastrayugmaṃ gurorapi /
vināyakaṃ grahānprārcya śriyaṃ karmaphalaṃ labhet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vināyakasnānaṃ nāma
pañcaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 vaṣaṭkārasamanvitair iti gha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 471
:ś atha ṣaṭṣaṣṭhyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
māheśvarasnānalakṣakoṭihomādayaḥ
265.d:
भोजयेद्ब्राह्मणान्दद्याद्वस्त्रयुग्मं गुरोरपि /
विनायकं ग्रहान्प्रार्च्य श्रियं कर्मफलं लभेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे विनायकस्नानं नाम
पञ्चषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 वषट्कारसमन्वितैर् इति घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 471
:श् अथ षट्षष्ठ्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
माहेश्वरस्नानलक्षकोटिहोमादयः
265.m:
He should feed Brahmins and give a pair of garments also to the guru. / Having thoroughly worshipped Vināyaka and the planets, he obtains prosperity and the fruit of his deeds.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and sixty-fifth chapter, entitled "The Bath for Vināyaka."
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: "accompanied by the exclamation vaṣaṭ" in manuscripts gha, ja, ña, and ṭa. Page 471]
Now, the two hundred and sixty-sixth chapter:
The Bath for Maheśvara, the Hundred-Thousand and Ten-Million Fire Oblations, and Others.

266.s:
puṣkara uvāca
snānaṃ māheśvaraṃ vakṣye rājāderjayavardhanam /
dānavendrāya balaye yajjagādośanāḥ purā //
266.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
स्नानं माहेश्वरं वक्ष्ये राजादेर्जयवर्धनम् /
दानवेन्द्राय बलये यज्जगादोशनाः पुरा //
266.m: Puṣkara said: / I shall declare the bath for Maheśvara, which increases victory for kings and others, / which Uśanas taught in ancient times to Bali, the king of the Dānavas.

266.s:
bhāskare 'nudite pīṭhe prātaḥ saṃsnāpayed ghaṭaiḥ /
oṃ namo bhagavate rudrāya ca balāya ca
pāṇḍarocitabhasmānuliptagātrāya / tadyathā jaya jaya sarvān
śatrūnmūkasya kalahavigrahavivādeṣu bhañjaya / oṃ matha matha
sarvapathikānyosau yugāntakāle didhakṣati imāṃ pūjāṃ
raudramūrtiḥ sahasrāṃśuḥ śukraḥ sa te rakṣatu jīvitaṃ /
sambartakāgnitulyaś ca tripurāntakaraḥ śivaḥ / sarvadevamayaḥ sopi
tava rakṣatu jīvitaṃ likhi likhi khili svāhā ||
evaṃ snatastu mantreṇa juhuyāttilataṇḍulam //
266.d:
भास्करे ऽनुदिते पीठे प्रातः संस्नापयेद् घटैः /
ओं नमो भगवते रुद्राय च बलाय च
पाण्डरोचितभस्मानुलिप्तगात्राय / तद्यथा जय जय सर्वान्
शत्रून्मूकस्य कलहविग्रहविवादेषु भञ्जय / ओं मथ मथ
सर्वपथिकान्योसौ युगान्तकाले दिधक्षति इमां पूजां
रौद्रमूर्तिः सहस्रांशुः शुक्रः स ते रक्षतु जीवितं /
सम्बर्तकाग्नितुल्यश् च त्रिपुरान्तकरः शिवः / सर्वदेवमयः सोपि
तव रक्षतु जीवितं लिखि लिखि खिलि स्वाहा ||
एवं स्नतस्तु मन्त्रेण जुहुयात्तिलतण्डुलम् //
266.m:
Before the sun has risen, in the morning, one should bathe [him] on the seat with jars:
"Oṃ, obeisance to the Blessed Rudra and to Bala, whose body is smeared with white, fitting ashes! Thus: conquer, conquer all enemies of so-and-so; smash [them] in quarrels, conflicts, and disputes! Oṃ, crush, crush all travelers! He who at the time of the end of the aeon desires to burn, of terrible form, thousand-rayed, the bright one: may he protect your life! And Śiva, equal to the fire of universal destruction, the destroyer of Tripura, consisting of all gods: may he also protect your life! Likhi likhi khili svāhā!"
Thus bathed with the mantra, he should offer sesamum and unbroken rice into the fire.

266.s:
pañcāmṛtaistu saṃsnāpya pūjayecchūlapāṇinaṃ /
snānānyanyāni vakṣyāmi sarvadā vijayāya te //
266.d:
पञ्चामृतैस्तु संस्नाप्य पूजयेच्छूलपाणिनं /
स्नानान्यन्यानि वक्ष्यामि सर्वदा विजयाय ते //
266.m: Having bathed [him] with the five nectars, one should worship the Trident-Holder. / I shall state other baths for your constant victory.

266.s:
snānaṃ ghṛtena kathitamāyuṣyavardhanaṃ param /
gomayena ca lakṣmīḥ syādgomūtreṇāghamardanam //
266.d:
स्नानं घृतेन कथितमायुष्यवर्धनं परम् /
गोमयेन च लक्ष्मीः स्याद्गोमूत्रेणाघमर्दनम् //
266.m: Bathing with ghee is declared to be the best increaser of longevity. / By cow dung fortune is obtained, and by cow urine the destruction of sins.

266.s:
kṣīreṇa balabuddhiḥ syāddadhnā lakṣmīvivardhanaṃ /
kuśodakena pāpāntaḥ pañcagavyena sarvabhāk //
266.d:
क्षीरेण बलबुद्धिः स्याद्दध्ना लक्ष्मीविवर्धनं /
कुशोदकेन पापान्तः पञ्चगव्येन सर्वभाक् //
266.m: By milk there is strength and intellect; by curds, the increase of fortune. / By water with kuśa grass there is an end to sin; by the five products of the cow one possesses all.

266.s:
śatamūlena sarvāptirgośṛṅgodakato 'ghajit /
:p 472
palāśabilvakamalakuśasnānantu sarvadaṃ //
266.d:
शतमूलेन सर्वाप्तिर्गोशृङ्गोदकतो ऽघजित् /
:प् 472
पलाशबिल्वकमलकुशस्नानन्तु सर्वदं //
266.m:
By śatamūlā all is attained; through water [poured over] a cow's horn sins are conquered.
[Page 472]
A bath with palāśa, bilva, lotus, and kuśa bestows everything.

266.s:
vacā haridre dve mustaṃ snānaṃ rakṣohaṇaṃ paraṃ /
āyuṣyañca yaśasyañca dharmamedhāvivardhanam //
266.d:
वचा हरिद्रे द्वे मुस्तं स्नानं रक्षोहणं परं /
आयुष्यञ्च यशस्यञ्च धर्ममेधाविवर्धनम् //
266.m: Vacā, the two turmerics, and mustā make the best bath that slays demons, / increasing longevity, renown, righteousness, and intellect.

266.s:
haimādbhiś caiva māṅgalyaṃ rūpyatāmrodakais tathā /
ratnodakaistu vijayaḥ saubhāgyaṃ sarvagandhakaiḥ //
266.d:
हैमाद्भिश् चैव माङ्गल्यं रूप्यताम्रोदकैस् तथा /
रत्नोदकैस्तु विजयः सौभाग्यं सर्वगन्धकैः //
266.m: Auspiciousness comes from water [infused with] gold, and likewise with silver- and copper-water; / victory comes through gem-infused water, and good fortune through all fragrant substances.

266.s:
phalādbhiś ca tathārogyaṃ dhātryadbhiḥ paramāṃ śriyam /
tilasiddhārthakair lakṣmīḥ saubhāgyañca priyaṅguṇā //
266.d:
फलाद्भिश् च तथारोग्यं धात्र्यद्भिः परमां श्रियम् /
तिलसिद्धार्थकैर् लक्ष्मीः सौभाग्यञ्च प्रियङ्गुणा //
266.m: Likewise, freedom from disease comes from water [steeped with] fruits, and supreme fortune from emblic myrobalan water; / prosperity comes through sesamum and white mustard seeds, and good fortune through priyaṅgu.

266.s:
padmotpalakadambaiś ca śrīrbalaṃ balādrumodakaiḥ /
viṣṇupādodakasnānaṃ sarvasnānebhya uttamam //
266.d:
पद्मोत्पलकदम्बैश् च श्रीर्बलं बलाद्रुमोदकैः /
विष्णुपादोदकस्नानं सर्वस्नानेभ्य उत्तमम् //
266.m: Through lotus, water lily, and kadamba comes prosperity; strength comes from waters [infused with] the balādruma tree. / A bath with water [that has washed] Viṣṇu's feet is the best of all baths.

266.s:
ekākī ekakāmāyetyekorkaṃ(1) vidhivaccaret /
akrandayatisūktena prabadhnīyānmaṇiṃ kare //
266.d:
एकाकी एककामायेत्येकोर्कं(1) विधिवच्चरेत् /
अक्रन्दयतिसूक्तेन प्रबध्नीयान्मणिं करे //
266.m: Alone, for a single desire, one should offer an arka plant according to rule; / with the Akrandayati hymn one should bind an amulet on the hand.

266.s:
kuṣṭhapāṭhā vācā śuṇṭhī śaṅkhalohādiko maṇiḥ /
sarveṣāmevakāmānāmīśvaro bhagavān hariḥ //
266.d:
कुष्ठपाठा वाचा शुण्ठी शङ्खलोहादिको मणिः /
सर्वेषामेवकामानामीश्वरो भगवान् हरिः //
266.m: Kuṣṭha, pāṭhā, vacā, dry ginger, an amulet of conch, iron, and the like [are used]. / The Blessed Lord Hari is indeed the lord of all desires.

266.s:
tasya saṃpūjanādeva sarvānkāmānsamaśnute /
snāpayitvā ghṛtakṣīraiḥ pūjayitvā ca pittahā //
266.d:
तस्य संपूजनादेव सर्वान्कामान्समश्नुते /
स्नापयित्वा घृतक्षीरैः पूजयित्वा च पित्तहा //
266.m: From his worship alone one attains all desires. / Having bathed [him] with ghee and milk and worshipped him, one destroys bile disorders.

266.s:
pañcamudgabalindatvā atisārāt pramucyate /
pañcagavyena saṃsnāpya vātavyādhiṃ vināśayet //
266.d:
पञ्चमुद्गबलिन्दत्वा अतिसारात् प्रमुच्यते /
पञ्चगव्येन संस्नाप्य वातव्याधिं विनाशयेत् //
266.m: Having offered the oblation of five varieties of kidney beans, one is freed from diarrhea; / having bathed him with the five products of the cow, one destroys disorders of wind.

266.s:
dvisnehasnapanāt śleṣmarogahā cātipūjayā /
ghṛtaṃ tailaṃ tathā kṣaudraṃ snānantu trirasaṃ paraṃ //
266.d:
द्विस्नेहस्नपनात् श्लेष्मरोगहा चातिपूजया /
घृतं तैलं तथा क्षौद्रं स्नानन्तु त्रिरसं परं //
266.m: From bathing [him] with two unctuous substances and through intense worship, one destroys phlegm disorders. / Ghee, oil, and honey—this bath of three fluids is supreme.

266.s:
snānaṃ ghṛtāmbu dvisnehaṃ samalaṃ ghṛtatailakam /
kṣaudramikṣurasaṃ kṣīraṃ snānaṃ trimadhuraṃ smṛtam //
266.d:
स्नानं घृताम्बु द्विस्नेहं समलं घृततैलकम् /
क्षौद्रमिक्षुरसं क्षीरं स्नानं त्रिमधुरं स्मृतम् //
266.m: A bath of ghee and water is the two unctuous substances; ghee and oil mixed is [another] two unctuous substances. / Honey, sugarcane juice, and milk—this bath is known as the three sweets.

266.s:
ghṛtamiśurasaṃ tailaṃ kṣaudrañca trirasaṃ śriye /
:n
1 yavakāmāyetyekorkamiti ka.. , cha.. ca
:p 473
anulepastriśukrastu karpūrośīracandanaiḥ //
266.d:
घृतमिशुरसं तैलं क्षौद्रञ्च त्रिरसं श्रिये /
:न्
1 यवकामायेत्येकोर्कमिति क.. , छ.. च
:प् 473
अनुलेपस्त्रिशुक्रस्तु कर्पूरोशीरचन्दनैः //
266.m:
Ghee, sugarcane juice, oil, and honey—the bath of three fluids is for prosperity.
[Footnote 1: 'yavakāmāyetyekorkam' in manuscripts ka and cha] / [Page 473]
The three-white unguent consists of camphor, uśīra, and sandalwood.

266.s:
candanāgurukarpūramṛgadarpaiḥ sakuṅkumaiḥ /
pañcānulepanaṃ viṣṇoḥ sarvakāmaphalapradaṃ //
266.d:
चन्दनागुरुकर्पूरमृगदर्पैः सकुङ्कुमैः /
पञ्चानुलेपनं विष्णोः सर्वकामफलप्रदं //
266.m: With sandalwood, agallochum, camphor, musk, and saffron, / the fivefold unguent of Viṣṇu bestows the fruit of all desires.

266.s:
trisugandhañca karpūraṃ tathā candanakuṅkumaiḥ /
mṛgadarpaṃ sakarpūraṃ malayaṃ sarvakāmadam //
266.d:
त्रिसुगन्धञ्च कर्पूरं तथा चन्दनकुङ्कुमैः /
मृगदर्पं सकर्पूरं मलयं सर्वकामदम् //
266.m: The triple-fragrant one is camphor with sandalwood and saffron; / musk along with camphor and sandalwood grants all desires.

266.s:
jātīphalaṃ sakarpūraṃ candanañca triśītakam /
pītāni śuklavarṇāni tathā śuklāni bhārgava //
266.d:
जातीफलं सकर्पूरं चन्दनञ्च त्रिशीतकम् /
पीतानि शुक्लवर्णानि तथा शुक्लानि भार्गव //
266.m: Nutmeg with camphor and sandalwood is the triple-cooling one. / Yellow and white colors, and likewise white ones, O descendant of Bhṛgu,

266.s:
kṛṣṇāni caiva raktāni pañcavarṇāni nirdiśet /
utpalaṃ padmajātī ca triśītaṃ haripūjane //
266.d:
कृष्णानि चैव रक्तानि पञ्चवर्णानि निर्दिशेत् /
उत्पलं पद्मजाती च त्रिशीतं हरिपूजने //
266.m: and black and red—one should designate these five colors. / The blue water lily, the lotus, and jasmine are the three cool flowers in the worship of Hari.

266.s:
kuṅkumaṃ raktapadmāni triraktamutpalaṃ /
dhūpadīpādibhiḥ prārcya viṣṇuṃ śāntirbhavennṛṇāṃ //
266.d:
कुङ्कुमं रक्तपद्मानि त्रिरक्तमुत्पलं /
धूपदीपादिभिः प्रार्च्य विष्णुं शान्तिर्भवेन्नृणां //
266.m: Saffron, red lotuses, and red water lilies are the triple-red offering. / Having worshipped Viṣṇu with incense, lamps, and so forth, peace comes to men.

266.s:
caturasrakare kuṇḍe brāhmaṇāścāṣṭa śoḍaśa /
lakṣahomaṅkoṭihomantilājyayavadhānyakaiḥ //
266.d:
चतुरस्रकरे कुण्डे ब्राह्मणाश्चाष्ट शोडश /
लक्षहोमङ्कोटिहोमन्तिलाज्ययवधान्यकैः //
266.m: In a square cubit-sized fire-pit, eight or sixteen brāhmaṇas [perform] / the fire oblation of one hundred thousand or ten million [offerings] with sesamum, clarified butter, barley, and grains.

266.s:
grahānabhyarcya gāyatryā sarvaśāntiḥ kramādbhavet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe maheśvarasnānalakṣakoṭihomādayo nāma
ṣaṭṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś atha saptaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nīrājanavidhiḥ
266.d:
ग्रहानभ्यर्च्य गायत्र्या सर्वशान्तिः क्रमाद्भवेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे महेश्वरस्नानलक्षकोटिहोमादयो नाम
षट्षष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथ सप्तषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
नीराजनविधिः
266.m:
Having worshipped the planets with the Gāyatrī, all pacification shall occur in order.
Thus ends the two hundred sixty-sixth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'The Bath of the Great Lord, the Fire Oblations of One Hundred Thousand and Ten Million Offerings, and Others.'
Now, the two hundred sixty-seventh chapter:
The Rite of Lustration.

267.s:
puṣkara uvāca
karma sāṃvatsaraṃ rājñāṃ janmarkṣe pūjayecca taṃ /
māsi māsi ca saṃkrāntau sūryasomādidevatāḥ //
:p 474
267.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
कर्म सांवत्सरं राज्ञां जन्मर्क्षे पूजयेच्च तं /
मासि मासि च संक्रान्तौ सूर्यसोमादिदेवताः //
:प् 474
267.m:
Puṣkara said: / [Regarding] the annual ritual of kings, one should worship on their natal asterism, / and month by month at the planetary transit, one should worship the deities beginning with the sun and the moon.
[Page 474]

267.s:
agastyasyodaye 'gastyañcāturmāsyaṃ hariṃ yajet /
śayanotthāpane pañcadinaṃ kuryātsamutsavam //
267.d:
अगस्त्यस्योदये ऽगस्त्यञ्चातुर्मास्यं हरिं यजेत् /
शयनोत्थापने पञ्चदिनं कुर्यात्समुत्सवम् //
267.m: At the rising of Agastya one should worship Agastya; during the four-month period of rain one should worship Hari. / At [his] lying down and rising up, one should celebrate a great festival for five days.

267.s:
proṣṭhapāde site pakṣe pratipatprabhṛtikramāt /
śivirāt pūrvadigbhāge śakrārthaṃ bhavanañcaret //
267.d:
प्रोष्ठपादे सिते पक्षे प्रतिपत्प्रभृतिक्रमात् /
शिविरात् पूर्वदिग्भागे शक्रार्थं भवनञ्चरेत् //
267.m: In the month of Bhādrapada, in the bright fortnight, beginning in order from the first lunar day, / one should construct a pavilion in the eastern direction from the camp for Śakra.

267.s:
tatra śakradhvajaṃ sthāpya śacī śakrañca pūjayet /
aṣṭamyāṃ vādyaghoṣeṇa tāntu yaṣṭiṃ praveśayet //
267.d:
तत्र शक्रध्वजं स्थाप्य शची शक्रञ्च पूजयेत् /
अष्टम्यां वाद्यघोषेण तान्तु यष्टिं प्रवेशयेत् //
267.m: Having raised the banner of Śakra there, one should worship Śacī and Śakra; / on the eighth lunar day, one should bring that staff inside to the sound of musical instruments.

267.s:
ekādaśyāṃ sopavāso dvādaśyāṃ ketumutthitam /
yajedvastrādisaṃvītaṃ ghaṭasthaṃ(1) surapaṃ śacīṃ //
267.d:
एकादश्यां सोपवासो द्वादश्यां केतुमुत्थितम् /
यजेद्वस्त्रादिसंवीतं घटस्थं(1) सुरपं शचीं //
267.m: Fasting on the eleventh lunar day, on the twelfth lunar day one should worship / the lord of the gods [placed] in a jar [or on a cloth] and covered with garments and the like, and Śacī, beside the raised banner:

267.s:
vardhasvendra jitāmitra vṛtrahan pākaśāsana /
deva deva mahābhāga tvaṃ hi bhūmiṣṭhatāṃ gataḥ //
267.d:
वर्धस्वेन्द्र जितामित्र वृत्रहन् पाकशासन /
देव देव महाभाग त्वं हि भूमिष्ठतां गतः //
267.m: 'Grow, O Indra, conqueror of enemies, slayer of Vṛtra, subduer of Pāka! / O god of gods, O highly fortunate one, you have indeed come to reside on earth!

267.s:
tvaṃ prabhuḥ śāśvataś caiva sarvabhūtahite rataḥ /
anantatejā vai rājo yaśojayavivardhanaḥ //
267.d:
त्वं प्रभुः शाश्वतश् चैव सर्वभूतहिते रतः /
अनन्ततेजा वै राजो यशोजयविवर्धनः //
267.m: You are the sovereign lord, eternal and devoted to the welfare of all beings, / of boundless splendor, a king who increases fame and victory!

267.s:
tejaste vardhayantvete devāḥ śakraḥ suvṛṣṭikṛt /
brahmaviṣṇumaheśāś ca kārttikeyo vināyakaḥ //
267.d:
तेजस्ते वर्धयन्त्वेते देवाः शक्रः सुवृष्टिकृत् /
ब्रह्मविष्णुमहेशाश् च कार्त्तिकेयो विनायकः //
267.m: May these gods increase your splendor, O Śakra, maker of good rain! / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Maheśa, Kārttikeya, Vināyaka,

267.s:
ādityā vasavo rudrāḥ sādhyāś ca bhṛgavo diśaḥ /
marudguṇā lokapālā grahā yakṣādrinimnagāḥ //
267.d:
आदित्या वसवो रुद्राः साध्याश् च भृगवो दिशः /
मरुद्गुणा लोकपाला ग्रहा यक्षाद्रिनिम्नगाः //
267.m: the Ādityas, Vasus, Rudras, Sādhyas, Bhṛgus, the directions, / the hosts of Maruts, the world guardians, planets, yakṣas, mountains, and rivers,

267.s:
samudrā śrīrmahī gaurī caṇḍikā ca sarasvatī /
pravartayantu te tejo jaya śakra śacīpate //
267.d:
समुद्रा श्रीर्मही गौरी चण्डिका च सरस्वती /
प्रवर्तयन्तु ते तेजो जय शक्र शचीपते //
267.m: the oceans, Śrī, the Earth, Gaurī, Caṇḍikā, and Sarasvatī! / May they arouse your splendor! Be victorious, O Śakra, consort of Śacī!

267.s:
tava cāpi jayānnityaṃ mama sampaṭhyatāṃ śubhaṃ /
prasīda rājñāṃ viprāṇāṃ prajānāmapi sarvaśaḥ //
267.d:
तव चापि जयान्नित्यं मम सम्पठ्यतां शुभं /
प्रसीद राज्ञां विप्राणां प्रजानामपि सर्वशः //
267.m: And through your constant victory, let auspiciousness be proclaimed for me! / Be gracious to kings, brāhmaṇas, and to the subjects everywhere!

267.s:
bhavatprasādāt pṛthivī nityaṃ śasyavatī bhavet /
śivaṃ bhavatu nirvighnaṃ śāmyantāmītayo bhṛśaṃ //
:n
1 paṭasthamiti ka.. , ga.. , cha.. , ja.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 475
267.d:
भवत्प्रसादात् पृथिवी नित्यं शस्यवती भवेत् /
शिवं भवतु निर्विघ्नं शाम्यन्तामीतयो भृशं //
:न्
1 पटस्थमिति क.. , ग.. , छ.. , ज.. , ट.. च
:प् 475
267.m:
By your grace, may the earth ever abound with crops! / May there be auspiciousness without obstacles! May calamities be entirely pacified!'
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: 'paṭastham' in manuscripts ka, ga, cha, ja, and ṭa] / [Page 475]

267.s:
mantreṇendraṃ samabhyarcya jitabhūḥ svargamāpnuyāt /
bhadrakālīṃ paṭe likhya pūjayedāśvine jaye //
267.d:
मन्त्रेणेन्द्रं समभ्यर्च्य जितभूः स्वर्गमाप्नुयात् /
भद्रकालीं पटे लिख्य पूजयेदाश्विने जये //
267.m: Having worshipped Indra with the mantra, having conquered the earth, one attains heaven. / Having drawn Bhadrakālī on a cloth, one should worship her in the month of Āśvina for victory,

267.s:
śuklapakṣe tathāṣṭamyāmāyudhaṃ kārmukaṃ dhvajam /
chatrañca rājaliṅgāni śastrādyaṃ kusumādibhiḥ //
267.d:
शुक्लपक्षे तथाष्टम्यामायुधं कार्मुकं ध्वजम् /
छत्रञ्च राजलिङ्गानि शस्त्राद्यं कुसुमादिभिः //
267.m: in the bright fortnight, likewise on the eighth lunar day, [worshipping] the weapon, bow, banner, / umbrella, and royal insignia, weapons and the like, with flowers and other offerings.

267.s:
jāgranniśi balindadyāddvitīye 'hni punaryajet /
bhadrakāli mahākāli durge durgārtihāriṇi //
267.d:
जाग्रन्निशि बलिन्दद्याद्द्वितीये ऽह्नि पुनर्यजेत् /
भद्रकालि महाकालि दुर्गे दुर्गार्तिहारिणि //
267.m: Remaining awake at night, one should offer oblation; on the second day one should worship again: / 'O Bhadrakālī, Mahākālī, Durgā, remover of distress at fortress gates,

267.s:
trailokyavijaye caṇḍi mama śāntau jaye bhava /
nīrājanavidhiṃ vakṣye aiśānyānmandiraṃ caret //
267.d:
त्रैलोक्यविजये चण्डि मम शान्तौ जये भव /
नीराजनविधिं वक्ष्ये ऐशान्यान्मन्दिरं चरेत् //
267.m: victor in the three worlds, O Caṇḍī, be present for my peace and victory!' / I shall declare the rite of lustration: one should build a pavilion in the north-east.

267.s:
toraṇatritayaṃ tatra gṛhe devānyajet sadā /
citrāntyaktvā yadā svātiṃ savitā pratipadyate //
267.d:
तोरणत्रितयं तत्र गृहे देवान्यजेत् सदा /
चित्रान्त्यक्त्वा यदा स्वातिं सविता प्रतिपद्यते //
267.m: There are three arched gateways there; in that house one should constantly worship the gods. / When the sun, leaving Citrā, enters Svātī,

267.s:
tataḥ prabhṛti kartavyaṃ yāvat svātau raviḥ sthitaḥ /
brahmā viṣṇuś ca śambhuś ca śakraś caivānalānilau //
267.d:
ततः प्रभृति कर्तव्यं यावत् स्वातौ रविः स्थितः /
ब्रह्मा विष्णुश् च शम्भुश् च शक्रश् चैवानलानिलौ //
267.m: from that time forth [the rite] is to be performed as long as the sun remains in Svātī. / Brahmā, Viṣṇu, Śambhu, Śakra, Fire and Wind,

267.s:
vināyakaḥ kumāraś ca varuṇo dhanado yamaḥ /
viśvedevā vaiśravaso gajāścāṣṭau ca tānyajet //
267.d:
विनायकः कुमारश् च वरुणो धनदो यमः /
विश्वेदेवा वैश्रवसो गजाश्चाष्टौ च तान्यजेत् //
267.m: Vināyaka, Kumāra, Varuṇa, Kubera, Yama, / the Viśvedevas, Kubera, and the eight elephants—one should worship them:

267.s:
kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadantaś ca vāmanaḥ /
supratīko 'ñjano nīlaḥ pūjā kāryā gṛhādike //
267.d:
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदन्तश् च वामनः /
सुप्रतीको ऽञ्जनो नीलः पूजा कार्या गृहादिके //
267.m: Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla; the worship is to be performed in the pavilion and other places.

267.s:
purodhā juhuyādājyaṃ samitsiddhārthakaṃ tilāḥ /
kumbhā aṣṭau pūjitāś ca taiḥ snāpyāśvagajottamāḥ //
267.d:
पुरोधा जुहुयादाज्यं समित्सिद्धार्थकं तिलाः /
कुम्भा अष्टौ पूजिताश् च तैः स्नाप्याश्वगजोत्तमाः //
267.m: The royal chaplain should offer ghee, fuel sticks, white mustard, and sesamum seeds into the fire. / Eight jars are worshipped, and with them the excellent horses and elephants should be bathed.

267.s:
aśvāḥ snāpyā dadet piṇḍān tato hi prathamaṃ gajān /
niṣkrāmayettoraṇaistu gopurādi(1) na laṅghayet //
267.d:
अश्वाः स्नाप्या ददेत् पिण्डान् ततो हि प्रथमं गजान् /
निष्क्रामयेत्तोरणैस्तु गोपुरादि(1) न लङ्घयेत् //
267.m: Having bathed the horses, he should offer food balls, and then first of all [the horses and] elephants / he should lead out through the arches; he should not step over the town gate and the like.

267.s:
vikrameyustataḥ sarve rājaliṅgaṃ gṛhe yajet /
:n
1 śekharādīti ka..
:p 476
vāruṇe varuṇaṃ prārcya rātrau bhūtabaliṃ dadet //
267.d:
विक्रमेयुस्ततः सर्वे राजलिङ्गं गृहे यजेत् /
:न्
1 शेखरादीति क..
:प् 476
वारुणे वरुणं प्रार्च्य रात्रौ भूतबलिं ददेत् //
267.m:
Then they all should march out; in the house, one should worship the royal insignia.
[Footnote]
[Footnote 1: 'śekharādī' in manuscript ka] / [Page 476]
Having worshipped Varuṇa in the west, one should offer an oblation to the spirits at night.

267.s:
viśākhāyāṃ(1) gate sūrye āśrame nivasennṛpaḥ /
alaṅkuryāddine tasmin vāhanantu viśeṣataḥ //
267.d:
विशाखायां(1) गते सूर्ये आश्रमे निवसेन्नृपः /
अलङ्कुर्याद्दिने तस्मिन् वाहनन्तु विशेषतः //
267.m: When the sun has entered the asterism Viśākhā, the king should reside in the hermitage; / and on that day he should especially adorn the mounts.

267.s:
pūjitā rājaliṅgāś ca kartavyā narahastagāḥ /
hastinanturagaṃ chatraṃ khaḍgaṃ cāpañca dundubhim //
267.d:
पूजिता राजलिङ्गाश् च कर्तव्या नरहस्तगाः /
हस्तिनन्तुरगं छत्रं खड्गं चापञ्च दुन्दुभिम् //
267.m: The royal insignia, having been worshipped, should be placed in the hands of men: / the elephant, horse, parasol, sword, bow, drum,

267.s:
dhvajaṃ patākāṃ dharmajña kālajñastvabhimantrayet /
abhimantrya tataḥ sarvān kuryāt kuñjaradhūrgatān //
267.d:
ध्वजं पताकां धर्मज्ञ कालज्ञस्त्वभिमन्त्रयेत् /
अभिमन्त्र्य ततः सर्वान् कुर्यात् कुञ्जरधूर्गतान् //
267.m: standard, and banner, O knower of duty; the knower of time should consecrate them with mantras. / Having consecrated all of them, he should place them before the elephant.

267.s:
kuñjaroparigau syātāṃ sāṃvatsarapurohitau /
mantritāṃś ca samāruhya toraṇena vinirgamet //
267.d:
कुञ्जरोपरिगौ स्यातां सांवत्सरपुरोहितौ /
मन्त्रितांश् च समारुह्य तोरणेन विनिर्गमेत् //
267.m: The astrologer and the family priest should mount upon the elephant. / Having mounted the consecrated ones, he should depart through the ceremonial archway.

267.s:
niṣkramya nāgamāruhya toraṇenātha nirgamet /
baliṃ vibhajya vidhivadrājā kuñjaradhūrgataḥ //
267.d:
निष्क्रम्य नागमारुह्य तोरणेनाथ निर्गमेत् /
बलिं विभज्य विधिवद्राजा कुञ्जरधूर्गतः //
267.m: Having come out and mounted the elephant, he should then depart through the ceremonial archway. / Having distributed the bali according to rule, the king, stationed at the forefront of the elephant,

267.s:
unmūkānāntu nicayamādīpitadigantaraṃ /
rājā pradakṣiṇaṃ kuryāttrīn vārān susamāhitaḥ //
267.d:
उन्मूकानान्तु निचयमादीपितदिगन्तरं /
राजा प्रदक्षिणं कुर्यात्त्रीन् वारान् सुसमाहितः //
267.m: should attentively perform circumambulation three times / around a heap of burning brands that illuminates the quarters.

267.s:
caturaṅgabalopetaḥ sarvasainyena nādayan /
evaṃ kṛtvā gṛhaṃ gacchedvisarjitajalāñjaliḥ //
267.d:
चतुरङ्गबलोपेतः सर्वसैन्येन नादयन् /
एवं कृत्वा गृहं गच्छेद्विसर्जितजलाञ्जलिः //
267.m: Accompanied by the fourfold army, making sound with the entire host, / having done so and having poured out a handful of water, he should return to his palace.

267.s:
śāntir nīrājanākhyeyaṃ vṛddhaye ripumardanī //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nīrājanāvidhirnāma
saptaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 viśākhāntviti ka.. , cha.. ca
:p 477
:ś athāṣṭaṣaṣṭyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
chatrādimantrādayaḥ
267.d:
शान्तिर् नीराजनाख्येयं वृद्धये रिपुमर्दनी //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नीराजनाविधिर्नाम
सप्तषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 विशाखान्त्विति क.. , छ.. च
:प् 477
:श् अथाष्टषष्ट्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
छत्रादिमन्त्रादयः
267.m:
This pacification rite called Nīrājanā is for prosperity and crushes enemies.
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-seventh chapter, entitled “The Rule of Nīrājanā,” in the great Āgneya Purāṇa.
[Footnote]
1. "viśākhāṃ tu" thus in manuscripts ka and cha. / [Page 477]
Now, the two hundred and sixty-eighth chapter:
Mantras for the Parasol and Other Items.

268.s:
puṣkara uvāca
chatrādimantrānvakṣyāmi yaistat pūjya jayādikam /
brahmaṇaḥ satyavākyena somasya varuṇasya ca //
268.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
छत्रादिमन्त्रान्वक्ष्यामि यैस्तत् पूज्य जयादिकम् /
ब्रह्मणः सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य वरुणस्य च //
268.m: Puṣkara said: / I will proclaim the mantras for the parasol and other items, by which, when worshipped, victory and other blessings [are attained]. / By the true word of Brahmā, and of Soma and Varuṇa,

268.s:
sūryasya ca prabhāvena vardhasva tvaṃ mahāmate /
pāṇḍarābhapratīkāśa himakundendusuprabha //
268.d:
सूर्यस्य च प्रभावेन वर्धस्व त्वं महामते /
पाण्डराभप्रतीकाश हिमकुन्देन्दुसुप्रभ //
268.m: and by the splendor of the Sun, prosper, O intelligent one, / O you who resemble white radiance, brilliant like snow, the kunda flower, and the moon!

268.s:
yathāmbudaśchādayate śivāyaināṃ vasundharāṃ /
tathācchādaya rājānaṃ vijayārogyavṛddhaye //
268.d:
यथाम्बुदश्छादयते शिवायैनां वसुन्धरां /
तथाच्छादय राजानं विजयारोग्यवृद्धये //
268.m: Just as a cloud covers this earth for its welfare, / so cover the king for victory, health, and prosperity.

268.s:
gandharvakulajātastvaṃ mābhūyāḥ kuladūṣakaḥ /
brahmaṇaḥ satyavākyena somasya varuṇasya ca //
268.d:
गन्धर्वकुलजातस्त्वं माभूयाः कुलदूषकः /
ब्रह्मणः सत्यवाक्येन सोमस्य वरुणस्य च //
268.m: You are born of the Gandharva lineage; do not bring disgrace to your lineage! / By the true word of Brahmā, and of Soma and Varuṇa,

268.s:
prabhāvācca hutāśasya vardhasva tvaṃ turaṅgama /
tejasā caiva sūryasya munīnāṃ tapasā tathā //
268.d:
प्रभावाच्च हुताशस्य वर्धस्व त्वं तुरङ्गम /
तेजसा चैव सूर्यस्य मुनीनां तपसा तथा //
268.m: and by the power of the consumer of oblations, grow strong, O horse! / And by the brilliance of the Sun, and by the ascetic austerity of the sages,

268.s:
rudrasya brahmacaryeṇa pavanasya balena ca /
smara tvaṃ rājaputro 'si kaustubhantu maṇiṃ smara //
268.d:
रुद्रस्य ब्रह्मचर्येण पवनस्य बलेन च /
स्मर त्वं राजपुत्रो ऽसि कौस्तुभन्तु मणिं स्मर //
268.m: by the celibacy of Rudra, and by the strength of the Wind, / remember that you are a prince! Remember the Kaustubha gem!

268.s:
yāṃ gatiṃ brahmahā gacchet pitṛhā mātṛhā tathā /
bhūmyarthe 'nṛtavādī ca kṣatriyaś ca parāṅmukhaḥ //
268.d:
यां गतिं ब्रह्महा गच्छेत् पितृहा मातृहा तथा /
भूम्यर्थे ऽनृतवादी च क्षत्रियश् च पराङ्मुखः //
268.m: The destination to which a killer of a brāhmaṇa, a father, or a mother goes, / or a speaker of falsehood for the sake of land, or a warrior who turns his back on battle—

268.s:
vrajestvantāṃ gatiṃ kṣipraṃ mā tat pāpaṃ bhavettava /
vikṛtiṃ māpagacchestvaṃ yuddhe 'dhvani turaṅgama //
268.d:
व्रजेस्त्वन्तां गतिं क्षिप्रं मा तत् पापं भवेत्तव /
विकृतिं मापगच्छेस्त्वं युद्धे ऽध्वनि तुरङ्गम //
268.m: may you swiftly go to that destination! May that sin not be yours! / May you not become disfigured in battle or on the road, O horse!

268.s:
ripūn vinighnansamare saha bhartrā sukhī bhava /
śakraketo mahāvīryaḥ suvarṇastvāmupāśritaḥ //
268.d:
रिपून् विनिघ्नन्समरे सह भर्त्रा सुखी भव /
शक्रकेतो महावीर्यः सुवर्णस्त्वामुपाश्रितः //
268.m: Slaying enemies in battle, be happy along with your master! / O banner of Indra, the mighty, golden-winged one has resorted to you,

268.s:
patatrirāḍvainateyas tathā nārāyaṇadhvajaḥ /
:p 478
kāśyapeyo 'mṛtāhartā nāgārirviṣṇuvāhanaḥ //
268.d:
पतत्रिराड्वैनतेयस् तथा नारायणध्वजः /
:प् 478
काश्यपेयो ऽमृताहर्ता नागारिर्विष्णुवाहनः //
268.m:
the king of birds, the son of Vinatā, and the emblem of Nārāyaṇa,
[Page 478]
the son of Kaśyapa, the bringer of nectar, the enemy of serpents, the vehicle of Viṣṇu,

268.s:
aprameyo durādharṣo raṇe devārisūdanaḥ /
mahābalo māvego mahākāyo 'mṛtāśanaḥ //
268.d:
अप्रमेयो दुराधर्षो रणे देवारिसूदनः /
महाबलो मावेगो महाकायो ऽमृताशनः //
268.m: immeasurable, invincible, the slayer of the foes of the gods in battle, / of great strength, great speed, huge body, the consumer of nectar,

268.s:
garutmānmārutagatistvayi sannihitaḥ sthitaḥ /
viṣṇunā devadevena śakrārthaṃ sthāpito hy asi //
268.d:
गरुत्मान्मारुतगतिस्त्वयि सन्निहितः स्थितः /
विष्णुना देवदेवेन शक्रार्थं स्थापितो ह्य् असि //
268.m: Garutmān, who moves like the wind, is stationed present within you. / For you were established by Viṣṇu, the god of gods, for Indra's sake.

268.s:
jayāya bhava me nityaṃ vṛddhaye 'tha balasya ca /
sāśvavarmāyudhānyodhānrakṣāsmākaṃ ripūndaha //
268.d:
जयाय भव मे नित्यं वृद्धये ऽथ बलस्य च /
साश्ववर्मायुधान्योधान्रक्षास्माकं रिपून्दह //
268.m: Be ever for my victory, and for the increase of my army! / Protect our warriors with their horses, armor, and weapons, and burn up the enemies!

268.s:
kumudairāvaṇau padmaḥ puṣpadanto 'tha vāmanaḥ /
supratīko 'ñjano nīla ete 'ṣṭau devayonayaḥ //
268.d:
कुमुदैरावणौ पद्मः पुष्पदन्तो ऽथ वामनः /
सुप्रतीको ऽञ्जनो नील एते ऽष्टौ देवयोनयः //
268.m: Kumuda, Airāvaṇa, Padma, Puṣpadanta, then Vāmana, / Supratīka, Añjana, and Nīla—these eight are born of divine origin.

268.s:
teṣāṃ putrāś ca pautrāś ca balānyaṣṭau samāśritāḥ /
bhadro mando mṛgaś caiva gajaḥ saṃkīrṇa eva ca //
268.d:
तेषां पुत्राश् च पौत्राश् च बलान्यष्टौ समाश्रिताः /
भद्रो मन्दो मृगश् चैव गजः संकीर्ण एव च //
268.m: Their sons and grandsons resort to the eight forces; / [the classes of elephants are:] bhadra, manda, mṛga, and saṃkīrṇa.

268.s:
vane vane prasūtāste smarayoniṃ mahāgajāḥ /
pāntu tvāṃ vasavo rudrā ādityāḥ samarudgaṇāḥ //
268.d:
वने वने प्रसूतास्ते स्मरयोनिं महागजाः /
पान्तु त्वां वसवो रुद्रा आदित्याः समरुद्गणाः //
268.m: Born in forest after forest, remember your origin, O great elephants! / May the Vasus, Rudras, and Ādityas, along with the hosts of Maruts, protect you.

268.s:
bhartāraṃ rakṣa nāgendra samayaḥ paripālyatāṃ /
airāvatādhirūḍhastu vajrahastaḥ śatakratuḥ //
268.d:
भर्तारं रक्ष नागेन्द्र समयः परिपाल्यतां /
ऐरावताधिरूढस्तु वज्रहस्तः शतक्रतुः //
268.m: Protect your master, O lord of elephants; let your duty be preserved! / Mounted on Airāvata, holding the thunderbolt, Śatakratu,

268.s:
pṛṣṭhato 'nugatastveṣa rakṣatu tvāṃ sa devarāṭ /
avāpnuhi jayaṃ yuddhe susthaś caiva sadā vraja //
268.d:
पृष्ठतो ऽनुगतस्त्वेष रक्षतु त्वां स देवराट् /
अवाप्नुहि जयं युद्धे सुस्थश् चैव सदा व्रज //
268.m: following behind you—may that king of the gods protect you! / Attain victory in battle, and always march in sound condition!

268.s:
avāpnuhi balañcaiva airāvatasamaṃ yudhi /
śrīste somādbalaṃ viṣṇostejaḥ sūryājjavo 'nilāt //
268.d:
अवाप्नुहि बलञ्चैव ऐरावतसमं युधि /
श्रीस्ते सोमाद्बलं विष्णोस्तेजः सूर्याज्जवो ऽनिलात् //
268.m: Attain strength in battle equal to Airāvata! / May your fortune come from Soma, strength from Viṣṇu, brilliance from the Sun, speed from the Wind,

268.s:
sthairyaṃ girerjayaṃ rudrādyaśo devāt purandarāt /
yuddhe rakṣantu nāgāstvāṃ diśaś ca saha daivataiḥ //
268.d:
स्थैर्यं गिरेर्जयं रुद्राद्यशो देवात् पुरन्दरात् /
युद्धे रक्षन्तु नागास्त्वां दिशश् च सह दैवतैः //
268.m: steadfastness from the mountain, victory from Rudra, and renown from the divine Purandara! / May the elephants protect you in battle, and the directions along with their deities!

268.s:
aśvinau saha gandharvaiḥ pāntu tvāṃ sarvato diśaḥ /
manvo vasavo rudrā vāyuḥ somo maharṣayaḥ //
:p 479
268.d:
अश्विनौ सह गन्धर्वैः पान्तु त्वां सर्वतो दिशः /
मन्वो वसवो रुद्रा वायुः सोमो महर्षयः //
:प् 479
268.m:
May the Aśvins together with the Gandharvas protect you from all quarters! / The Manus, Vasus, Rudras, Vāyu, Soma, the great sages,
[Page 479]

268.s:
nāgakinnaragandharvayakṣabhūtagaṇā grahāḥ /
pramathāstu sahādityair bhūteśo mātṛbhiḥ saha //
268.d:
नागकिन्नरगन्धर्वयक्षभूतगणा ग्रहाः /
प्रमथास्तु सहादित्यैर् भूतेशो मातृभिः सह //
268.m: the hosts of nāgas, kinnaras, gandharvas, yakṣas, and bhūtas, the planets, / the Pramathas along with the Ādityas, the Lord of spirits with the Mothers,

268.s:
śakraḥ senāpatiḥ skando varuṇaścāśritastvayi /
pradahantu ripūn sarvān rājā vijayamṛcchatu //
268.d:
शक्रः सेनापतिः स्कन्दो वरुणश्चाश्रितस्त्वयि /
प्रदहन्तु रिपून् सर्वान् राजा विजयमृच्छतु //
268.m: Indra, Skanda the general of the army, and Varuṇa have resorted to you. / Let them burn all enemies, and let the king attain victory!

268.s:
yāni prayuktānyaribhirbhūṣaṇāni samantataḥ /
patantu tava śatrūṇāṃ hatāni tava tejasā //
268.d:
यानि प्रयुक्तान्यरिभिर्भूषणानि समन्ततः /
पतन्तु तव शत्रूणां हतानि तव तेजसा //
268.m: Whatever ornaments are employed all around by enemies, / may they fall, destroyed by your brilliance, upon your enemies!

268.s:
kālanemibadhe yadvat yuddhe tripuraghātane /
hiraṇyakaśiporyuddhe badhe sarvāsureṣu ca //
268.d:
कालनेमिबधे यद्वत् युद्धे त्रिपुरघातने /
हिरण्यकशिपोर्युद्धे बधे सर्वासुरेषु च //
268.m: Just as in the slaying of Kālanemi, in the battle of the destruction of Tripura, / in the battle of Hiraṇyakaśipu, and in the slaughter of all the asuras,

268.s:
śobhitāsi tathaivādya śobhasva samayaṃ smara /
nīlasvetāmimāndṛṣṭvā naśyantvāśu nṛpārayaḥ //
268.d:
शोभितासि तथैवाद्य शोभस्व समयं स्मर /
नीलस्वेतामिमान्दृष्ट्वा नश्यन्त्वाशु नृपारयः //
268.m: you shone, just so shine today! Remember your duty! / Seeing this black and white [banner], may the king's enemies quickly perish,

268.s:
vyādhibhirvividhair ghoraiḥ śastraiś ca yudhi nirjitāḥ /
pūtanā revatī lekhā kālarātrīti paṭhyate //
268.d:
व्याधिभिर्विविधैर् घोरैः शस्त्रैश् च युधि निर्जिताः /
पूतना रेवती लेखा कालरात्रीति पठ्यते //
268.m: overcome in battle by diverse, terrible diseases and by weapons! / Pūtanā, Revatī, Lekhā, and the one called Kālarātrī—

268.s:
dahantvāśu ripūn sarvānpatāke tvāmupāśritāḥ /
sarvamedhe mahāyajñe devadevena śūlinā //
268.d:
दहन्त्वाशु रिपून् सर्वान्पताके त्वामुपाश्रिताः /
सर्वमेधे महायज्ञे देवदेवेन शूलिना //
268.m: having resorted to you, O banner, let them quickly consume all foes! / In the Sarvamedha great sacrifice, by the god of gods who holds the trident,

268.s:
śarveṇa jagataś caiva sāreṇa tvaṃ vinirmitaḥ /
nandakasyāparāṃ mūrtiṃ smara śatrunivarhaṇa //
268.d:
शर्वेण जगतश् चैव सारेण त्वं विनिर्मितः /
नन्दकस्यापरां मूर्तिं स्मर शत्रुनिवर्हण //
268.m: by Śarva, you were created out of the essence of the entire universe. / Remember the other form of Nandaka, O destroyer of foes!

268.s:
nīlotpaladalaśyāma kṛṣṇa duḥsvapnanāśana /
asirviśasanaḥ khaḍgastīkṣṇadhāro durāsadaḥ //
268.d:
नीलोत्पलदलश्याम कृष्ण दुःस्वप्ननाशन /
असिर्विशसनः खड्गस्तीक्ष्णधारो दुरासदः //
268.m: Dark as a blue lotus petal, black, destroyer of bad dreams! / Asi, Viśasana, Khaḍga, Tīkṣṇadhāra, Durāsada,

268.s:
augarbho vijayaś caiva dharmapālastathaiva ca /
ityaṣṭau tava nāmāni puroktāni svayambhuvā //
268.d:
औगर्भो विजयश् चैव धर्मपालस्तथैव च /
इत्यष्टौ तव नामानि पुरोक्तानि स्वयम्भुवा //
268.m: Āugarbha, Vijaya, and Dharmapāla— / these are your eight names spoken formerly by the Self-born One.

268.s:
nakṣatraṃ kṛttikā tubhyaṃ gururdevo maheśvaraḥ /
hiraṇyañca śarīrante daivatante janārdanaḥ //
268.d:
नक्षत्रं कृत्तिका तुभ्यं गुरुर्देवो महेश्वरः /
हिरण्यञ्च शरीरन्ते दैवतन्ते जनार्दनः //
268.m: Your asterism is Kṛttikā, your guru is the god Maheśvara, / your body is gold, and your deity is Janārdana.

268.s:
rājānaṃ rakṣa nistriṃśa sabalaṃ sapurantathā /
:p 480
pitā pitāmaho devaḥ sa tvaṃ pālaya sarvadā //
268.d:
राजानं रक्ष निस्त्रिंश सबलं सपुरन्तथा /
:प् 480
पिता पितामहो देवः स त्वं पालय सर्वदा //
268.m:
Protect the king, O pitiless sword, along with his army and his city!
[Page 480]
The god is your father and grandfather; as such, protect him always!

268.s:
śarmapradastvaṃ samare varman sainye yaśo 'dya me /
rakṣa māṃ rakṣaṇīyo 'hantavānagha namo 'stu te //
268.d:
शर्मप्रदस्त्वं समरे वर्मन् सैन्ये यशो ऽद्य मे /
रक्ष मां रक्षणीयो ऽहन्तवानघ नमो ऽस्तु ते //
268.m: You bestow comfort in battle, O armor, and renown today in my army. / Protect me, for I am to be protected by you, O sinless one! Homage be to you!

268.s:
dundubhe tvaṃ sapatnānāṃ ghoṣāddhṛdayakampanaḥ /
bhava bhūmisainyānāṃ yathā vijayavardhanaḥ //
268.d:
दुन्दुभे त्वं सपत्नानां घोषाद्धृदयकम्पनः /
भव भूमिसैन्यानां यथा विजयवर्धनः //
268.m: O drum, you cause the hearts of adversaries to tremble by your sound; / become the increaser of victory for the armies on earth!

268.s:
yathā jīmūtaghoṣeṇa hṛṣyanti varavāraṇāḥ /
tathāstu tava śabdena harṣo 'smākaṃ mudāvaha //
268.d:
यथा जीमूतघोषेण हृष्यन्ति वरवारणाः /
तथास्तु तव शब्देन हर्षो ऽस्माकं मुदावह //
268.m: Just as excellent elephants rejoice at the sound of a cloud, / so by your sound let there be joy bringing gladness unto us!

268.s:
yathā jīmūtaśabdena strīṇāṃ trāso 'bhijāyate /
tathā tu tava śabdena trasyantvasmaddviṣo raṇe //
268.d:
यथा जीमूतशब्देन स्त्रीणां त्रासो ऽभिजायते /
तथा तु तव शब्देन त्रस्यन्त्वस्मद्द्विषो रणे //
268.m: Just as terror arises in women by the sound of a thundercloud, / even so by your sound let our enemies tremble in battle!

268.s:
mantraiḥ sadārcanīyāste yojanīyā jayādiṣu /
ghṛtakambalaviṣṇādestvabhiṣekañca vatsare //
268.d:
मन्त्रैः सदार्चनीयास्ते योजनीया जयादिषु /
घृतकम्बलविष्णादेस्त्वभिषेकञ्च वत्सरे //
268.m: These should always be worshipped with mantras and employed for victory and the like. / And consecration by aspersion with a blanket of clarified butter, Viṣṇu, and the rest [should be performed] each year.

268.s:
rājño 'bhiṣekaḥ kartavyo daivajñena purodhasā //39//
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe chatrādimantrādayaḥ
nāmāṣṭaṣaṣṭhyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 481
agnipurāṇam
maharṣiśrīmadvedavyāsena praṇītam
śrīlaśrī vaṅgadeśīyāsiyātik-samājānujñayā
śrīrājendralālamitreṇa pariśodhitam
kalikātārājadhānyāṃ gaṇeśayantre mudritañca
saṃvat 1933
agnipurāṇam
:ś athonasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
viṣṇupañjaraṃ
puṣkara uvaca
268.d:
राज्ञो ऽभिषेकः कर्तव्यो दैवज्ञेन पुरोधसा //39//
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे छत्रादिमन्त्रादयः
नामाष्टषष्ठ्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 481
अग्निपुराणम्
महर्षिश्रीमद्वेदव्यासेन प्रणीतम्
श्रीलश्री वङ्गदेशीयासियातिक्-समाजानुज्ञया
श्रीराजेन्द्रलालमित्रेण परिशोधितम्
कलिकाताराजधान्यां गणेशयन्त्रे मुद्रितञ्च
संवत् 1933
अग्निपुराणम्
:श् अथोनसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
विष्णुपञ्जरं
पुष्कर उवच
268.m:
The consecration by aspersion of the king should be performed by the astrologer and the family priest. //39
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-eighth chapter, entitled "The Mantras for the Royal Umbrella and Other Regalia", in the great Agni Purāṇa.
[Page 481]
Agni Purāṇa.
Composed by the great sage, the venerable Vedavyāsa.

Agni Purāṇa.
Now, the two hundred and sixty-ninth chapter:
The Viṣṇu-Armour.
Puṣkara said:

269.s:
tripurañjaghnuṣaḥ pūrvaṃ brahmaṇā viṣṇupañjaraṃ /
śaṅkarasya dvijaśreṣtha rakṣaṇāya nirūpitaṃ //
269.d:
त्रिपुरञ्जघ्नुषः पूर्वं ब्रह्मणा विष्णुपञ्जरं /
शङ्करस्य द्विजश्रेष्थ रक्षणाय निरूपितं //
269.m: Anciently, when Śaṅkara set out to slay Tripura, the Viṣṇu-armour was prescribed / by Brahmā, O best of the twice-born, for his protection;

269.s:
vāgīśena ca śakrasya balaṃ hantuṃ prayāsyataḥ /
tasya svarūpaṃ vakṣyāmi tattvaṃ śṛṇu jayādimat //
269.d:
वागीशेन च शक्रस्य बलं हन्तुं प्रयास्यतः /
तस्य स्वरूपं वक्ष्यामि तत्त्वं शृणु जयादिमत् //
269.m: and by the Lord of Speech [Bṛhaspati] for Indra when he set out to slay Bala. / I shall explain its nature; hear its reality, which bestows victory and other blessings.

269.s:
viṣṇuḥ prācyāṃ sthitaś cakrī harirdakṣinaṇato gadī /
pratīcyāṃ śārṅgadhṛgviṣṇurjiṣṇuḥ khaḍgī mamottare //
269.d:
विष्णुः प्राच्यां स्थितश् चक्री हरिर्दक्षिनणतो गदी /
प्रतीच्यां शार्ङ्गधृग्विष्णुर्जिष्णुः खड्गी ममोत्तरे //
269.m: May Viṣṇu, bearing the discus, stand in the east; Hari, bearing the mace, on the south; / may Viṣṇu, bearing the Śārṅga bow, stand in the west; and the victorious [Lord], bearing the sword, on my north.

269.s:
hṛṣīkeśo vikoṇeṣu tacchidreṣu janārdanaḥ /
kroḍarūpī harirbhūmau narasiṃho 'mbare mama //
269.d:
हृषीकेशो विकोणेषु तच्छिद्रेषु जनार्दनः /
क्रोडरूपी हरिर्भूमौ नरसिंहो ऽम्बरे मम //
269.m: May Hṛṣīkeśa be in the intermediate directions, and Janārdana in the intervals between them; / may Hari in the form of a boar protect me on earth, and Narasiṃha in the sky.

269.s:
kṣurāntamamalañcakraṃ bhramatyetat sudarśanaṃ /
asyāṃśumālā duṣprekṣyā hantuṃ pretaniśācarān //
269.d:
क्षुरान्तममलञ्चक्रं भ्रमत्येतत् सुदर्शनं /
अस्यांशुमाला दुष्प्रेक्ष्या हन्तुं प्रेतनिशाचरान् //
269.m: This spotless Sudarśana discus revolves with razor-sharp edges; / the garland of its rays is dazzling to behold, [set] to slay ghosts and night-wandering demons.

269.s:
gadā ceyaṃ sahasrārciḥpradīptapāvakojjvalā /
rakṣobhūtapiśācānāṃ ḍākinīnāñca nāśanī //
269.d:
गदा चेयं सहस्रार्चिःप्रदीप्तपावकोज्ज्वला /
रक्षोभूतपिशाचानां डाकिनीनाञ्च नाशनी //
269.m: And this mace, blazing with fire ignited by a thousand flames, / destroys Rākṣasas, Bhūtas, Piśācas, and Ḍākinīs.

And may the twang of Vāsudeva's Śārṅga bow utterly destroy my enemies: / animals, humans, kūṣmāṇḍa demons, ghosts, and the rest.
[Page 1]

269.s:
khaḍgadhārojjvalajjo 'tsnānirdhūtā ye samāhitāḥ /
te yāntu śāmyatāṃ sadyo garuḍeneva pannagāḥ //
269.d:
खड्गधारोज्ज्वलज्जो ऽत्स्नानिर्धूता ये समाहिताः /
ते यान्तु शाम्यतां सद्यो गरुडेनेव पन्नगाः //
269.m: Those assembled who are scattered by the bright moonlight of the sword's blade— / may they instantly be pacified, just as serpents [are subdued] by Garuḍa.

269.s:
ye kuṣmāṇḍāsthā yakṣā ye daityā ye niśācarāḥ /
pretā vināyakāḥ krūrā manuṣyā jambhagāḥ khagāḥ //
269.d:
ये कुष्माण्डास्था यक्षा ये दैत्या ये निशाचराः /
प्रेता विनायकाः क्रूरा मनुष्या जम्भगाः खगाः //
269.m: Whatever kūṣmāṇḍas, yakṣas, daityas, and night-wandering demons there are, / ghosts, cruel vināyakas, humans, jambhagas, and birds,

269.s:
siṃhādayaś ca paśavo dandaśūkāś ca pannagāḥ /
sarve bhavantu te saumyāḥ kṛṣṇaśaṅkharavāhatāḥ //
269.d:
सिंहादयश् च पशवो दन्दशूकाश् च पन्नगाः /
सर्वे भवन्तु ते सौम्याः कृष्णशङ्खरवाहताः //
269.m: beasts such as lions, biting vermin, and serpents— / struck by the sound of Kṛṣṇa's conch, may they all become gentle.

269.s:
cittavṛttiharā ye me ye janāḥ smṛtihārakāḥ /
balaujasañca hartāraśchāyāvibhraṃśakāś ca ye //
269.d:
चित्तवृत्तिहरा ये मे ये जनाः स्मृतिहारकाः /
बलौजसञ्च हर्तारश्छायाविभ्रंशकाश् च ये //
269.m: Those entities that rob my mental faculties, that steal memory, / that steal strength and vitality, and that destroy my aura,

269.s:
ye copabhogahartāro ye ca lakṣaṇanāśakāḥ /
kuṣmāṇḍāste praṇaśyantu viṣṇucakraravāhatāḥ //
269.d:
ये चोपभोगहर्तारो ये च लक्षणनाशकाः /
कुष्माण्डास्ते प्रणश्यन्तु विष्णुचक्ररवाहताः //
269.m: and those that rob enjoyments and destroy auspicious marks— / struck by the sound of Viṣṇu's discus, may those kūṣmāṇḍas perish.

269.s:
buddhisvāsthyaṃ manaḥsvāsthyaṃ svāsthyamaindriyakaṃ tathā /
mamāstu devadevasya vāsudevasya kīrtanāt //
269.d:
बुद्धिस्वास्थ्यं मनःस्वास्थ्यं स्वास्थ्यमैन्द्रियकं तथा /
ममास्तु देवदेवस्य वासुदेवस्य कीर्तनात् //
269.m: May I have health of intellect, health of mind, and likewise health of the senses, / through celebrating the God of gods, Vāsudeva.

269.s:
pṛṣṭhe purastānmama dakṣiṇottare vikoṇataścāstu janārdanohariḥ /
tamīḍyamīśānamanantamacyutaṃ janārdanaṃ praṇipatito na sīdati //
269.d:
पृष्ठे पुरस्तान्मम दक्षिणोत्तरे विकोणतश्चास्तु जनार्दनोहरिः /
तमीड्यमीशानमनन्तमच्युतं जनार्दनं प्रणिपतितो न सीदति //
269.m: May Janārdana Hari be behind me, before me, to my right and left, and in the intermediate directions; / having bowed down to that praiseworthy Lord, the endless, unchanging Janārdana, one does not perish.

269.s:
yathā paraṃ brahma haris tathā paraḥ jagatsvarūpaś ca sa eva keśavaḥ /
satyena tenācyutanāmakīrtanāt praṇāśayettu trividhaṃmamāśubhaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe viṣṇupañjaraṃ
nāmonasapratyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:p 2
:ś atha saptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vedaśākhadikīrtanaṃ
269.d:
यथा परं ब्रह्म हरिस् तथा परः जगत्स्वरूपश् च स एव केशवः /
सत्येन तेनाच्युतनामकीर्तनात् प्रणाशयेत्तु त्रिविधंममाशुभं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे विष्णुपञ्जरं
नामोनसप्रत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:प् 2
:श् अथ सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
वेदशाखदिकीर्तनं
269.m:
Just as Hari is the supreme Brahman, supreme, and Keśava himself embodies the universe, / by that truth, may he destroy my threefold misfortune through the recitation of Acyuta's name.
Thus ends the two hundred and sixty-ninth chapter, entitled "The Viṣṇu-Armour", in the great Agni Purāṇa. / [Page 2]
Now, the two hundred and seventieth chapter:
Proclamation of the Branches of the Veda and Other Subjects.

270.s:
puṣkara uvāca
sarvānugrāhakā mantrāś caturvargaprasādhakāḥ /
ṛgatharva tathā sāma yajuḥ saṃkhyā tu lakṣakaṃ //
270.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
सर्वानुग्राहका मन्त्राश् चतुर्वर्गप्रसाधकाः /
ऋगथर्व तथा साम यजुः संख्या तु लक्षकं //
270.m: Puṣkara said: / The mantras confer grace on all and accomplish the four goals of life; / the Ṛg, Atharvan, Sāman, and Yajus total one hundred thousand [verses].

270.s:
bhedaḥ sāṅkhyāyanaś caika āśvalāyano dvitīyakaḥ /
śatāni daśa mantrāṇāṃ brāhmaṇā dvisahasrakaṃ //
270.d:
भेदः साङ्ख्यायनश् चैक आश्वलायनो द्वितीयकः /
शतानि दश मन्त्राणां ब्राह्मणा द्विसहस्रकं //
270.m: One division is the Sāṅkhyāyana, and the second is the Āśvalāyana; / there are ten hundred mantras, and the Brāhmaṇa [portion] contains two thousand.

270.s:
ṛgvedo hi pramāṇena smṛto dvaipāyanādibhiḥ /
ekonidvisahasrantu mantrāṇāṃ yajuṣas tathā //
270.d:
ऋग्वेदो हि प्रमाणेन स्मृतो द्वैपायनादिभिः /
एकोनिद्विसहस्रन्तु मन्त्राणां यजुषस् तथा //
270.m: The Ṛgveda is recorded according to standard measure by Dvaipāyana and others; / and nineteen hundred are the mantras of the Yajus.

270.s:
śatāni daśa viprāṇāṃ ṣaḍaśītiś ca śākhikāḥ /
kāṇvamādhyandinī saṃjñā kaṭhī mādhyakaṭhī tathā //
270.d:
शतानि दश विप्राणां षडशीतिश् च शाखिकाः /
काण्वमाध्यन्दिनी संज्ञा कठी माध्यकठी तथा //
270.m: There are ten hundred for the brāhmaṇas and eighty-six branches: / the one called Kāṇva, the Mādhyandina, the Kaṭha, and likewise the Mādhyakaṭha,

270.s:
maitrāyaṇī ca saṃjñā ca taittirīyābhidhānikā /
vaiśampāyaniketyādyāḥ śākhā yajuṣi saṃsthitāḥ //
270.d:
मैत्रायणी च संज्ञा च तैत्तिरीयाभिधानिका /
वैशम्पायनिकेत्याद्याः शाखा यजुषि संस्थिताः //
270.m: and the one named Maitrāyaṇī, the branch called Taittirīya, / the Vaiśampāyanikā, and others established in the Yajurveda.

270.s:
sāmnaḥ kauthumasaṃjñaikā dvitīyātharvaṇāyanī /
gānānyapi ca catvāri veda āraṇyakantathā //
270.d:
साम्नः कौथुमसंज्ञैका द्वितीयाथर्वणायनी /
गानान्यपि च चत्वारि वेद आरण्यकन्तथा //
270.m: Of the Sāmaveda, one is called Kauthuma, and the second is the Ātharvaṇāyani; / there are also four song collections, the Veda, and the Āraṇyaka,

270.s:
ukthā ūhacaturthañca mantrā navasahasrakāḥ /
sacatuḥśatakāś caiva brahmasaṅghaṭakāḥ smṛtāḥ //
270.d:
उक्था ऊहचतुर्थञ्च मन्त्रा नवसहस्रकाः /
सचतुःशतकाश् चैव ब्रह्मसङ्घटकाः स्मृताः //
270.m: the ukthas, and the ūha as the fourth; nine thousand / four hundred mantras are recorded as constituting Brahman.

270.s:
pañcaviṃśatirevātra sāmamānaṃ prakīrtitaṃ /
sumanturjājaliś caiva ślokāyaniratharvake //
270.d:
पञ्चविंशतिरेवात्र साममानं प्रकीर्तितं /
सुमन्तुर्जाजलिश् चैव श्लोकायनिरथर्वके //
270.m: Twenty-five [thousand] is declared here to be the measure of the Sāmaveda. / Sumantu, Jājali, and Ślokāyani belong to the Atharvaveda,

270.s:
śaunakaḥ pippalādaś ca muñjakeśādayo 'pare /
mantrāṇāmayutaṃ ṣaṣṭiśatañcopaniṣacchataṃ //
270.d:
शौनकः पिप्पलादश् च मुञ्जकेशादयो ऽपरे /
मन्त्राणामयुतं षष्टिशतञ्चोपनिषच्छतं //
270.m: as well as Śaunaka, Pippalāda, Muñjakeśa, and others; / it contains ten thousand mantras, one hundred and sixty [hymns], and one hundred Upaniṣads.

270.s:
vyāsarūpī sa bhagavān śākhābhedadyakārayat /
:p 3
śākhābhedādayo viṣṇuritihāsaḥ purāṇakaṃ //
270.d:
व्यासरूपी स भगवान् शाखाभेदद्यकारयत् /
:प् 3
शाखाभेदादयो विष्णुरितिहासः पुराणकं //
270.m:
The Blessed One in the form of Vyāsa effected the division of the branches.
[Page 3]
Viṣṇu is the division into branches and the rest; he is the epic and the Purāṇa.

270.s:
prāpya vyāsāt purāṇādi sūto vai lomaharṣaṇaḥ /
sumatiścāgnivarcāś ca mitrayuḥśiṃśapāyanaḥ //
270.d:
प्राप्य व्यासात् पुराणादि सूतो वै लोमहर्षणः /
सुमतिश्चाग्निवर्चाश् च मित्रयुःशिंशपायनः //
270.m: Having received the Purāṇas and other works from Vyāsa, the Sūta Lomaharṣaṇa, / Sumati, Agnivarcas, Mitrayu, Śiṃśapāyana,

270.s:
kṛtavratotha sāvarṇiḥ ṣaṭśiṣyāstasya cābhavan /
śāṃśapāyanādayaś cakruḥ(1) purāṇānāntu saṃhitāḥ //
270.d:
कृतव्रतोथ सावर्णिः षट्शिष्यास्तस्य चाभवन् /
शांशपायनादयश् चक्रुः(1) पुराणानान्तु संहिताः //
270.m: Kṛtavrata, and Sāvarṇi—these six became his disciples. / Śāṃśapāyana and the others composed the collections of the Purāṇas.

270.s:
brāhmādīni purāṇāni harividyā daśāṣṭa ca /
mahāpurāṇe hy āgneye vidyārūpo hariḥ sthitaḥ //
270.d:
ब्राह्मादीनि पुराणानि हरिविद्या दशाष्ट च /
महापुराणे ह्य् आग्नेये विद्यारूपो हरिः स्थितः //
270.m: The eighteen Purāṇas, beginning with the Brāhma, are the wisdom of Hari; / and in this great Agni Purāṇa, Hari resides in the form of sacred wisdom.

270.s:
saprapañco niṣprapañco mūrtāmūrtasvarūpadhṛk /
taṃ jñātvābhyarcya saṃstūya bhuktimuktimavāpnuyāt //
270.d:
सप्रपञ्चो निष्प्रपञ्चो मूर्तामूर्तस्वरूपधृक् /
तं ज्ञात्वाभ्यर्च्य संस्तूय भुक्तिमुक्तिमवाप्नुयात् //
270.m: Possessing both cosmic differentiation and transcendence, assuming manifest and unmanifest forms, / by knowing him, worshipping him, and praising him, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation.

270.s:
viṣṇurjiṣṇurbhaviṣṇuś ca agnisūryādirūpavān /
agnirūpeṇa devādermukhaṃ viṣṇuḥ parā gatiḥ //
270.d:
विष्णुर्जिष्णुर्भविष्णुश् च अग्निसूर्यादिरूपवान् /
अग्निरूपेण देवादेर्मुखं विष्णुः परा गतिः //
270.m: Viṣṇu is victorious, continually becoming, having the form of Agni, the Sun, and others; / in the form of Agni, Viṣṇu is the mouth of the gods and the supreme goal.

270.s:
vedeṣu sapurāṇeṣu yajñamūrtiś ca gīyate /
āgneyākhyaṃ purāṇantu rūpaṃ viṣṇormahattaraṃ //
270.d:
वेदेषु सपुराणेषु यज्ञमूर्तिश् च गीयते /
आग्नेयाख्यं पुराणन्तु रूपं विष्णोर्महत्तरं //
270.m: In the Vedas and Purāṇas he is sung as the embodiment of sacrifice; / and the Purāṇa named after Agni is the superior form of Viṣṇu.

270.s:
āgneyākhyapurāṇasya kartā śrotā janārdanaḥ /
tasmātpurāṇamāgneyaṃ sarvavedamayaṃ mahat //
270.d:
आग्नेयाख्यपुराणस्य कर्ता श्रोता जनार्दनः /
तस्मात्पुराणमाग्नेयं सर्ववेदमयं महत् //
270.m: Janārdana is both the author and the listener of the Agni Purāṇa; / therefore, the great Agni Purāṇa is composed of all the Vedas.

270.s:
sarvavidyāmayaṃ puṇyaṃ sarvajñānamayaṃ varam(2) /
sarvātma harirūpaṃ hi paṭhatāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ nṛṇāṃ //
270.d:
सर्वविद्यामयं पुण्यं सर्वज्ञानमयं वरम्(2) /
सर्वात्म हरिरूपं हि पठतां शृण्वतां नृणां //
270.m: It is full of all lore, meritorious, full of all knowledge, and supreme; / for it is the very form of Hari, the Self of all, to human beings who read and listen to it.

270.s:
vidyārthināñca vidyādamarthināṃ śrīdhanapradam(3) /
rājyārthināṃ rājyadañca dharmadaṃ dharmakāminām //
270.d:
विद्यार्थिनाञ्च विद्यादमर्थिनां श्रीधनप्रदम्(3) /
राज्यार्थिनां राज्यदञ्च धर्मदं धर्मकामिनाम् //
270.m: To those who desire knowledge it gives knowledge; to seekers of wealth it grants prosperity and riches; / to those who desire kingship it gives a kingdom; and it bestows righteousness upon those who desire righteousness.

270.s:
svargārthināṃ svargadañca putradaṃ putrakāmināṃ /
gavādikāmināṅgodaṃ grāmadaṃ grāmakāmināṃ //
:n
1 śiṃśapāyanādayaś cakruriti kha ..
2 paramiti ña ..
3 śrībalapradamiti ña ..
:p 4
270.d:
स्वर्गार्थिनां स्वर्गदञ्च पुत्रदं पुत्रकामिनां /
गवादिकामिनाङ्गोदं ग्रामदं ग्रामकामिनां //
:न्
1 शिंशपायनादयश् चक्रुरिति ख ..
2 परमिति ञ ..
3 श्रीबलप्रदमिति ञ ..
:प् 4
270.m:
To those desiring heaven it gives heaven; it grants a son to those desiring a son; / to those desiring cattle and the like it grants cows; it grants a village to those desiring a village.
[Footnote]
1 Manuscript kha reads: "śiṃśapāyanādayaś cakruḥ".
2 Manuscript ña reads: "param".
3 Manuscript ña reads: "śrībalapradam". / [Page 4]

270.s:
kāmārthināṃ kāmadañca sarvasaubhāgyasampradam /
guṇakīrtipradannṝṇāṃ jayadañjayakāminām //
270.d:
कामार्थिनां कामदञ्च सर्वसौभाग्यसम्प्रदम् /
गुणकीर्तिप्रदन्नॄणां जयदञ्जयकामिनाम् //
270.m: It grants desires to those seeking their fulfillment, and bestows all good fortune; / it grants virtue and fame to men, and gives victory to those desiring victory.

270.s:
sarvepsūnāṃ sarvadantu muktidaṃ muktikāmināṃ /
pāpaghnaṃ pāpakartṝṇāmāgneyaṃ hi purāṇakam //
ityāgneye mahāpurāṇe vedaśākhādikīrtinaṃ nāma
saptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athaikasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dānādimāhatmyaṃ
270.d:
सर्वेप्सूनां सर्वदन्तु मुक्तिदं मुक्तिकामिनां /
पापघ्नं पापकर्तॄणामाग्नेयं हि पुराणकम् //
इत्याग्नेये महापुराणे वेदशाखादिकीर्तिनं नाम
सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथैकसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
दानादिमाहत्म्यं
270.m:
It grants everything to those desiring all things; it gives liberation to those desiring liberation; / the Agni Purāṇa indeed destroys the sin of those who commit sin.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventieth chapter in the Agnipurāṇa, entitled 'The Glorification of the Branches of the Veda and Related Topics'.
Now begins the two hundred and seventy-first chapter.
The Greatness of the Gift [of the Purāṇas] and Related Matters

271.s:
puṣkara uvāca
brahmaṇābhihitaṃ pūrvaṃ yāvanmātraṃ marīcaye /
lakṣārdhāddhantu tadbrāhmaṃ likhitvā sampradāpayet //
271.d:
पुष्कर उवाच
ब्रह्मणाभिहितं पूर्वं यावन्मात्रं मरीचये /
लक्षार्धाद्धन्तु तद्ब्राह्मं लिखित्वा सम्प्रदापयेत् //
271.m:
Puṣkara said:
Whatever was previously spoken by Brahmā to Marīci, / having written down that Brāhma [Purāṇa] of fifty thousand [verses], one should give it away [in gift].

271.s:
vaiśākhyāmpaurṇamāsyāñca svargārthī jaladhenumat /
pādmaṃ dvādaśasāhasraṃ dyaiṣṭhe dadyācca dhenumat //
271.d:
वैशाख्याम्पौर्णमास्याञ्च स्वर्गार्थी जलधेनुमत् /
पाद्मं द्वादशसाहस्रं द्यैष्ठे दद्याच्च धेनुमत् //
271.m: One desirous of heaven [should give it] on the full moon day of Vaiśākha along with a water-cow. / One should give the Pādma [Purāṇa] of twelve thousand [verses] in the month of Jyaiṣṭha along with a cow.

271.s:
varāhakalpavṛttāntamadhikṛtya parāśaraḥ /
trayoviṃśatisāhasraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ prāha cārpayet //
271.d:
वराहकल्पवृत्तान्तमधिकृत्य पराशरः /
त्रयोविंशतिसाहस्रं वैष्णवं प्राह चार्पयेत् //
271.m: Setting forth the events of the Varāha Kalpa, Parāśara / declared the Vaiṣṇava [Purāṇa] of twenty-three thousand [verses]; and one should present it.

271.s:
jaladhenumadāṣāḍhyāṃ viṣṇoḥ padamavāpnuyāt /
caturdaśasahasrāṇi vāyavīyaṃ haripriyaṃ //
271.d:
जलधेनुमदाषाढ्यां विष्णोः पदमवाप्नुयात् /
चतुर्दशसहस्राणि वायवीयं हरिप्रियं //
271.m: [Giving it] with a water-cow on the full moon day of Āṣāḍha, one attains Viṣṇu's realm. / The Vāyavīya [Purāṇa], dear to Hari, consists of fourteen thousand [verses].

271.s:
śvetakalpaprasaṅgena dharmān vāyurihābravīt /
dadyāllikhitvā tadvipre śrāvaṇyāṃ guḍadhenumat //
271.d:
श्वेतकल्पप्रसङ्गेन धर्मान् वायुरिहाब्रवीत् /
दद्याल्लिखित्वा तद्विप्रे श्रावण्यां गुडधेनुमत् //
271.m: In connection with the Śveta Kalpa, Vāyu proclaimed dharmas here. / Having written it down, one should give it to a Brahmin on the full moon day of Śrāvaṇa along with a jaggery-cow.

271.s:
yatrādhikṛtya gāyatrīṃ kīrtyate dharmavistaraḥ /
:p 5
vṛtrāsurabadhopetaṃ tadbhāgavatamucyate //
271.d:
यत्राधिकृत्य गायत्रीं कीर्त्यते धर्मविस्तरः /
:प् 5
वृत्रासुरबधोपेतं तद्भागवतमुच्यते //

271.s:
sārasvatasta kalpasya proṣṭhapadyāntu taddadet /
aṣṭādaśasahasrāṇi hemasiṃhasamanvitaṃ //
271.d:
सारस्वतस्त कल्पस्य प्रोष्ठपद्यान्तु तद्ददेत् /
अष्टादशसहस्राणि हेमसिंहसमन्वितं //
271.m: Relating to the Sārasvata Kalpa, one should give it on the full moon day of Proṣṭhapadā; / it contains eighteen thousand [verses], accompanied by a golden lion.

271.s:
yatrāha nārado dharmān vṛhatkalpāśritānihaṃ /
pañcaviṃśasahasrāṇi nāradīyaṃ taducyate //
271.d:
यत्राह नारदो धर्मान् वृहत्कल्पाश्रितानिहं /
पञ्चविंशसहस्राणि नारदीयं तदुच्यते //
271.m: Wherein Nārada proclaimed dharmas based upon the Bṛhat Kalpa, / containing twenty-five thousand [verses], that is called the Nāradīya [Purāṇa].

271.s:
sadhenuñcāśvine dadyātsiddhimātyantikīṃ labhet /
yatrādhikṛtya śatrūnāndharmādharmavicāraṇā //
271.d:
सधेनुञ्चाश्विने दद्यात्सिद्धिमात्यन्तिकीं लभेत् /
यत्राधिकृत्य शत्रूनान्धर्माधर्मविचारणा //
271.m: One should give it in the month of Āśvina with a cow; one obtains ultimate perfection. / Wherein, based on enemies, the deliberation on virtue and vice is held,

271.s:
kārttikyāṃ navasāhasraṃ mārkaṇḍeyamathārpayet /
agninā yadvaśiṣṭhāya proktañcāgneyameva tat //
271.d:
कार्त्तिक्यां नवसाहस्रं मार्कण्डेयमथार्पयेत् /
अग्निना यद्वशिष्ठाय प्रोक्तञ्चाग्नेयमेव तत् //
271.m: One should then present the Mārkaṇḍeya [Purāṇa] of nine thousand [verses] on the full moon day of Kārttika. / And that which was spoken by Agni to Vasiṣṭha is the Āgneya [Purāṇa].

271.s:
likhitvā pustakaṃ dadyānmārgaśīrṣyāṃ sa sarvadaḥ /
dvādaśaiva sahasrāṇi sarvavidyāvabodhanaṃ(1) //
271.d:
लिखित्वा पुस्तकं दद्यान्मार्गशीर्ष्यां स सर्वदः /
द्वादशैव सहस्राणि सर्वविद्यावबोधनं(1) //
271.m: Having written the book, he who gives it on the full moon day of Mārgaśīrṣa grants everything; / it consists of twelve thousand [verses], imparting all knowledge.

271.s:
caturdaśasahasrāṇi bhaviṣyaṃ sūryasambhavaṃ /
bhavastu manave prāha dadyāt pauṣyāṃ guḍādimat //
271.d:
चतुर्दशसहस्राणि भविष्यं सूर्यसम्भवं /
भवस्तु मनवे प्राह दद्यात् पौष्यां गुडादिमत् //
271.m: The Bhaviṣya [Purāṇa], of fourteen thousand [verses], originated from Sūrya, / which Bhava proclaimed to Manu; one should give it on the full moon day of Pauṣa along with jaggery and the like.

271.s:
sāvarṇinā nāradāya brahmavaivartamīritaṃ /
rathāntarasya vṛttāntamaṣṭādaśasahasrakaṃ //
271.d:
सावर्णिना नारदाय ब्रह्मवैवर्तमीरितं /
रथान्तरस्य वृत्तान्तमष्टादशसहस्रकं //
271.m: The Brahmavaivarta [Purāṇa] was declared by Sāvarṇi to Nārada; / it contains the account of the Rathantara [Kalpa] and consists of eighteen thousand [verses].

271.s:
māghyāndadyādvarāhasya caritaṃ brahmalokabhāk /
yatragniliṅgamadhyastho dharmānprāha maheśvaraḥ //
271.d:
माघ्यान्दद्याद्वराहस्य चरितं ब्रह्मलोकभाक् /
यत्रग्निलिङ्गमध्यस्थो धर्मान्प्राह महेश्वरः //
271.m: One should give it on the full moon day of Māgha, [together with] the deeds of Varāha, and one partakes in the world of Brahmā. / Wherein Maheśvara, situated within the fire-liṅga, proclaimed dharmas,

271.s:
āgneyakalpe talliṅgamekādaśasahasrakam /
taddatvā śivamāpnoti phālgunyāṃ tiladhenumat //
271.d:
आग्नेयकल्पे तल्लिङ्गमेकादशसहस्रकम् /
तद्दत्वा शिवमाप्नोति फाल्गुन्यां तिलधेनुमत् //
271.m: In the Āgneya Kalpa, that is the Liṅga [Purāṇa] of eleven thousand [verses]. / Giving that along with a sesame-cow on the full moon day of Phālguna, one attains Śiva.

271.s:
caturdaśasahasrāṇi vārāhaṃ viṣṇuṇeritam /
bhūmau varāhacaritaṃ mānavasya pravṛttitaḥ //
271.d:
चतुर्दशसहस्राणि वाराहं विष्णुणेरितम् /
भूमौ वराहचरितं मानवस्य प्रवृत्तितः //
271.m: The Vārāha [Purāṇa] of fourteen thousand [verses] was spoken by Viṣṇu, / [describing] the deeds of the Boar on the earth, arising from Manu.

271.s:
sahemagaruḍañcaitryāṃ padamāpnoti vaiṣṇavam /
:n
1 sarvavidyāvadhāraṇamiti ña ..
:p 6
caturaśītisāhasraṃ skāndaṃ skanderitaṃ mahat //
271.d:
सहेमगरुडञ्चैत्र्यां पदमाप्नोति वैष्णवम् /
:न्
1 सर्वविद्यावधारणमिति ञ ..
:प् 6
चतुरशीतिसाहस्रं स्कान्दं स्कन्देरितं महत् //
271.m:
[Given] on the full moon day of Caitra along with a golden Garuḍa, one attains Viṣṇu's realm.
:n
1. 'sarvavidyāvadhāraṇam' according to manuscript ña..
:p 6
The great Skānda [Purāṇa] declared by Skanda has eighty-four thousand [verses].

271.s:
adhikṛtya sadharmāṃś ca kalpe tatpuruṣe 'rpayet /
vāmanaṃ daśasāhasraṃ dhaumakalpe hareḥ kathāṃ //
271.d:
अधिकृत्य सधर्मांश् च कल्पे तत्पुरुषे ऽर्पयेत् /
वामनं दशसाहस्रं धौमकल्पे हरेः कथां //
271.m: Dealing with righteous duties, in the Tatpuruṣa Kalpa, one should present it. / The Vāmana [Purāṇa] of ten thousand [verses], the story of Hari in the Dhauma Kalpa,

271.s:
dadyāt śaradi viṣuve dharmārthādinibodhanam /
kūrmañcāṣṭasahasrañca kūrmoktañca rasātale //
271.d:
दद्यात् शरदि विषुवे धर्मार्थादिनिबोधनम् /
कूर्मञ्चाष्टसहस्रञ्च कूर्मोक्तञ्च रसातले //
271.m: One should give at the autumn equinox, imparting understanding of dharma, artha, and the rest. / And the Kūrma [Purāṇa] of eight thousand [verses], spoken by the Tortoise in Rasātala

271.s:
indradyumnaprasaṅgena dadyāttaddhemakūrmavat /
trayodaśasahasrāṇi mātsyaṃ kalpādito 'bravīt //
271.d:
इन्द्रद्युम्नप्रसङ्गेन दद्यात्तद्धेमकूर्मवत् /
त्रयोदशसहस्राणि मात्स्यं कल्पादितो ऽब्रवीत् //
271.m: In connection with Indradyumna, one should give with a golden tortoise. / The Mātsya [Purāṇa] contains thirteen thousand [verses], spoken from the beginning of the kalpa.

271.s:
matsyo hi manave dadyādviṣuve hemamatsyavat /
gāruḍañcāṣṭasāhasraṃ viṣṇūktantārkṣakalpake //
271.d:
मत्स्यो हि मनवे दद्याद्विषुवे हेममत्स्यवत् /
गारुडञ्चाष्टसाहस्रं विष्णूक्तन्तार्क्षकल्पके //
271.m: The Fish indeed [spoke it] to Manu; one should give it at the equinox with a golden fish. / The Gāruḍa [Purāṇa] has eight thousand [verses], spoken by Viṣṇu in the Tārkṣya Kalpa,

271.s:
viśvāṇḍādgaruḍotpattiṃ taddadyāddhemahaṃsavat /
brahmā brahmāṇḍamāhātmyamadhikṛtyābrabīttu yat //
271.d:
विश्वाण्डाद्गरुडोत्पत्तिं तद्दद्याद्धेमहंसवत् /
ब्रह्मा ब्रह्माण्डमाहात्म्यमधिकृत्याब्रबीत्तु यत् //
271.m: Treating the origin of Garuḍa from the universal egg; one should give that with a golden swan. / What Brahmā declared taking as its subject the greatness of the Brahmāṇḍa,

271.s:
tacca dvādaśasāhasraṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ taddvije 'rpayet /
bhārate parvasamāptau vastragandhasragādibhiḥ //
271.d:
तच्च द्वादशसाहस्रं ब्रह्माण्डं तद्द्विजे ऽर्पयेत् /
भारते पर्वसमाप्तौ वस्त्रगन्धस्रगादिभिः //
271.m: That is the Brahmāṇḍa [Purāṇa] of twelve thousand [verses]; that one should present to a Brahmin. / At the conclusion of a section of the Mahābhārata, with garments, incense, garlands, and other things,

271.s:
vācakaṃ pūjayedādau bhojayet pāyasair dvijān /
gobhūgrāmasuvarṇādi dadyātparvaṇi parvaṇi //
271.d:
वाचकं पूजयेदादौ भोजयेत् पायसैर् द्विजान् /
गोभूग्रामसुवर्णादि दद्यात्पर्वणि पर्वणि //
271.m: One should first honor the reciter and feed the Brahmins with milk-rice; / one should give cattle, land, villages, gold, and other gifts at each festival section.

271.s:
samāpte bhārate vipraṃ saṃhitāpustakānyajet /
śubhe deśe niveśyātha kṣaumavastrādināvṛtān //
271.d:
समाप्ते भारते विप्रं संहितापुस्तकान्यजेत् /
शुभे देशे निवेश्याथ क्षौमवस्त्रादिनावृतान् //
271.m: When the Bhārata is concluded, one should worship the Brahmin and the manuscript of the Saṃhitā, / having placed them in an auspicious place and covered them with linen cloth and the like.

271.s:
naranārayaṇau pūjyau pustakāḥ kusumādibhiḥ /
go 'nnabhūhema dadvātha bhojayitvā kṣamāpayet //
271.d:
नरनारयणौ पूज्यौ पुस्तकाः कुसुमादिभिः /
गो ऽन्नभूहेम दद्वाथ भोजयित्वा क्षमापयेत् //
271.m: Nara and Nārāyaṇa are to be worshipped, and the manuscripts with flowers and the like. / Having given cattle, food, land, and gold, and having fed him, one should ask his forgiveness.

271.s:
mahādānāni deyāni ratnāni vividhāni ca /
māsakau dvau trayaś caiva māse māse pradāpayet //
271.d:
महादानानि देयानि रत्नानि विविधानि च /
मासकौ द्वौ त्रयश् चैव मासे मासे प्रदापयेत् //
271.m: Great gifts are to be given, as well as various kinds of jewels. / One should have [them] given month after month, for two or three months.

271.s:
ayanādau śrābakasya dānamādau vidhīyate /
śrotṛbhiḥ sakalaiḥ kāryaṃ śrāvake pūjanaṃ dvija //
:p 7
271.d:
अयनादौ श्राबकस्य दानमादौ विधीयते /
श्रोतृभिः सकलैः कार्यं श्रावके पूजनं द्विज //
:प् 7
271.m:
At the solstice and the like, a gift is first ordained for the reciter; / all the listeners must perform the worship of the reciter, O twice-born one.
[Page 7]

271.s:
itihāsapurāṇānāṃ pustakāni prayacchati /
pūjayitvāyurārogyaṃ svargamokṣamavāpnuyāt //
ityagneye mahapuraṇe dānādimāhatmyaṃ nāmaika
saptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha dvisaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sūryavaṃśakīrtanaṃ
271.d:
इतिहासपुराणानां पुस्तकानि प्रयच्छति /
पूजयित्वायुरारोग्यं स्वर्गमोक्षमवाप्नुयात् //
इत्यग्नेये महपुरणे दानादिमाहत्म्यं नामैक
सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ द्विसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सूर्यवंशकीर्तनं
271.m:
Whoever presents manuscripts of the histories and the Purāṇas, / having worshipped [them], obtains long life, health, heaven, and liberation.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-first chapter, entitled 'The Glorification of Gifts and the Like,' in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now follows the two hundred and seventy-second chapter.
The Recitation of the Solar Dynasty.

272.s:
agnir uvāca
sūryavaṃśaṃ somavaṃśaṃ rajñāṃ vaṃśaṃ vadami te /
harerbrahmā padmago 'bhūnmarīcirbrahmaṇaḥ sutaḥ //
272.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
सूर्यवंशं सोमवंशं रज्ञां वंशं वदमि ते /
हरेर्ब्रह्मा पद्मगो ऽभून्मरीचिर्ब्रह्मणः सुतः //
272.m: Agni said: / I shall tell you of the Solar Dynasty, the Lunar Dynasty, and the dynasty of kings. / From Hari, Brahmā arose seated on a lotus; Marīci was the son of Brahmā.

272.s:
marīceḥ kaśyapastasmādvivasvāṃstasya patnyapi /
saṃjñā rājñī(1) prabhā tisro rājñī raivataputrikā //
272.d:
मरीचेः कश्यपस्तस्माद्विवस्वांस्तस्य पत्न्यपि /
संज्ञा राज्ञी(1) प्रभा तिस्रो राज्ञी रैवतपुत्रिका //
272.m: From Marīci came Kaśyapa; from him Vivasvat. His wives also were / Saṃjñā, Rājñī, and Prabhā—the three; Rājñī was the daughter of Raivata.

272.s:
revantaṃ suṣuve putraṃ prabhātañca prabhā raveḥ /
tvāṣṭrī saṃjñā manuṃ putraṃ yamalau yamunāṃ yamam //
272.d:
रेवन्तं सुषुवे पुत्रं प्रभातञ्च प्रभा रवेः /
त्वाष्ट्री संज्ञा मनुं पुत्रं यमलौ यमुनां यमम् //
272.m: Prabhā bore to the Sun a son Revanta, and Prabhāta; / Saṃjñā, daughter of Tvaṣṭṛ, bore the son Manu, and the twins Yamunā and Yama.

272.s:
chāyā saṃjñā ca sāvarṇiṃ manuṃ vaivasvataṃ sutam /
śaniñca tapatīṃ viṣṭiṃ saṃjñāyāñcāśvinau punaḥ //
272.d:
छाया संज्ञा च सावर्णिं मनुं वैवस्वतं सुतम् /
शनिञ्च तपतीं विष्टिं संज्ञायाञ्चाश्विनौ पुनः //
272.m: Chāyā-Saṃjñā bore the son Sāvarṇi Manu, [and] Vaivasvata, / and Śani, Tapatī, and Viṣṭi; and on Saṃjñā [he begot] the two Aśvins again.

272.s:
manorvaivasvatasyāsan putrā vai na ca tatsamāḥ /
ikṣvākuś caiva nābhāgo dhṛṣṭaḥśaryātireva ca //
272.d:
मनोर्वैवस्वतस्यासन् पुत्रा वै न च तत्समाः /
इक्ष्वाकुश् चैव नाभागो धृष्टःशर्यातिरेव च //
272.m: The sons of Vaivasvata Manu were indeed peerless: / Ikṣvāku, Nābhāga, Dhṛṣṭa, and Śaryāti,

272.s:
nariṣyantas tathā prāṃśurnābhāgādiṣṭasattamāḥ /
karuṣaś ca pṛṣadhraś ca ayodhyāyāṃ mahābalāḥ //
272.d:
नरिष्यन्तस् तथा प्रांशुर्नाभागादिष्टसत्तमाः /
करुषश् च पृषध्रश् च अयोध्यायां महाबलाः //
272.m: Nariṣyanta, Prāṃśu, the best of men Nābhāgādiṣṭa, / Karuṣa, and Pṛṣadhra, mighty in Ayodhyā.

272.s:
kanyelā ca manorāsīdbudhāttasyāṃ purūravāḥ /
purūravasamucpādya selā sudyumnatāṅgatā //
:n
1 atra chāyetipāṭho yuktaḥ
:p 8
272.d:
कन्येला च मनोरासीद्बुधात्तस्यां पुरूरवाः /
पुरूरवसमुच्पाद्य सेला सुद्युम्नताङ्गता //
:न्
1 अत्र छायेतिपाठो युक्तः
:प् 8
272.m:
And Manu had a daughter, Ilā; from Budha, Purūravas was born of her. / Having produced Purūravas, that Ilā became Sudyumna.
[Note]
1 Here the reading 'Chāyā' is appropriate. / [Page 8]

272.s:
sudyumnādutkalagayau vinatāśvastrayo nṛpāḥ /
utkalasyotkalaṃ rāṣṭraṃ vinatāśvasya paścimā //
272.d:
सुद्युम्नादुत्कलगयौ विनताश्वस्त्रयो नृपाः /
उत्कलस्योत्कलं राष्ट्रं विनताश्वस्य पश्चिमा //
272.m: From Sudyumna came the three kings Utkala, Gaya, and Vinatāśva. / Utkala's kingdom was Utkala; the western region belonged to Vinatāśva,

272.s:
dik sarvā rājavaryasya gayasya tu gayāpurī /
vaśiṣṭhavākyāt sudyumnaḥ pratiṣṭhānamavāpa ha //
272.d:
दिक् सर्वा राजवर्यस्य गयस्य तु गयापुरी /
वशिष्ठवाक्यात् सुद्युम्नः प्रतिष्ठानमवाप ह //
272.m: the entire [direction] to that best of kings, and Gaya's was Gayāpurī. / By the word of Vasiṣṭha, Sudyumna obtained Pratiṣṭhāna.

272.s:
tat purūravase prādātsudyumno rājyamāpya tu /
nariṣyataḥ śakāḥ putrā nābhāgasya ca vaiṣṇavaḥ //
272.d:
तत् पुरूरवसे प्रादात्सुद्युम्नो राज्यमाप्य तु /
नरिष्यतः शकाः पुत्रा नाभागस्य च वैष्णवः //
272.m: Having obtained that kingdom, Sudyumna gave it to Purūravas. / The Śakas were the sons of Nariṣyanta; and of Nābhāga, the Vaiṣṇava

272.s:
ambarīṣaḥ prajāpālo dhārṣṭakaṃ dhṛṣṭataḥ kulam /
sukalpānartau śaryārtervairohyānartato nṛpaḥ //
272.d:
अम्बरीषः प्रजापालो धार्ष्टकं धृष्टतः कुलम् /
सुकल्पानर्तौ शर्यार्तेर्वैरोह्यानर्ततो नृपः //
272.m: Ambarīṣa, the protector of subjects; the Dhārṣṭaka family descended from Dhṛṣṭa. / Sukalpa and Ānarta were [the sons] of Śaryāti; from Vairohya-Ānarta, the king,

272.s:
ānartaviṣayaścāsīt purī cāsīt kuśasthalī /
revasya raivataḥ putraḥ kakudmī nāma dhārmikaḥ //
272.d:
आनर्तविषयश्चासीत् पुरी चासीत् कुशस्थली /
रेवस्य रैवतः पुत्रः ककुद्मी नाम धार्मिकः //
272.m: there was the region of Ānarta, and the city was Kuśasthalī. / The righteous son of Reva was Raivata, named Kakudmin.

272.s:
jyeṣṭhaḥ putraśatasyāsīdrājyaṃ prāpya kuśasthalīm /
sa kanyāsahitaḥ śrutvā gāndharvaṃ brahmaṇo 'ntike //
272.d:
ज्येष्ठः पुत्रशतस्यासीद्राज्यं प्राप्य कुशस्थलीम् /
स कन्यासहितः श्रुत्वा गान्धर्वं ब्रह्मणो ऽन्तिके //
272.m: He was the eldest of a hundred sons, having obtained the kingdom Kuśasthalī. / Having listened, together with his daughter, to celestial music in the presence of Brahmā,

272.s:
muhūrtabhūtaṃ devasya martye bahuyugaṃ gatam /
ājagāma javenātha svāṃ purīṃ yādavair vṛtām //
272.d:
मुहूर्तभूतं देवस्य मर्त्ये बहुयुगं गतम् /
आजगाम जवेनाथ स्वां पुरीं यादवैर् वृताम् //
272.m: for what seemed a moment of the god, many ages passed in the mortal realm. / Then he quickly came to his city, which was surrounded by the Yādavas,

272.s:
kṛtāṃ dvāravatīṃ nāma bahudvārāṃ manoramām /
bhojavṛṣṇyandhakair guptāṃ(?) vāsudevapurogamaiḥ //
272.d:
कृतां द्वारवतीं नाम बहुद्वारां मनोरमाम् /
भोजवृष्ण्यन्धकैर् गुप्तां(?) वासुदेवपुरोगमैः //
272.m: made charming with many gates and named Dvāravatī, / protected by the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas, led by Vāsudeva.

272.s:
revatīṃ baladevāya dadau jñātvā hy aninditām /
tapaḥ sumeruśikhare taptvā viṣṇvālayaṃ gataḥ //
272.d:
रेवतीं बलदेवाय ददौ ज्ञात्वा ह्य् अनिन्दिताम् /
तपः सुमेरुशिखरे तप्त्वा विष्ण्वालयं गतः //
272.m: Knowing [this], he gave the faultless Revatī to Baladeva. / Having performed ascetic austerity on the summit of Mount Sumeru, he went to the abode of Viṣṇu.

272.s:
nābhāgasya ca putrau dvau vaiśyau brāhmaṇatāṃ gatau /
karūṣasya tu kārūṣāḥ kṣatriyā yuddhadurmadāḥ //
272.d:
नाभागस्य च पुत्रौ द्वौ वैश्यौ ब्राह्मणतां गतौ /
करूषस्य तु कारूषाः क्षत्रिया युद्धदुर्मदाः //
272.m: And the two sons of Nābhāga, [though born] Vaiśyas, attained the status of Brahmins. / But the descendants of Karūṣa were the Kārūṣas, Kṣatriyas intoxicatingly fierce in battle.

272.s:
śūdratvañca pṛṣadhro 'gāddhiṃsayitvā guroś ca gām /
manuputrādathekṣākorvikukṣirdevarāḍabhūt //
272.d:
शूद्रत्वञ्च पृषध्रो ऽगाद्धिंसयित्वा गुरोश् च गाम् /
मनुपुत्रादथेक्षाकोर्विकुक्षिर्देवराडभूत् //
272.m: Pṛṣadhra fell to the status of a Śūdra by slaying his guru's cow. / Then from Manu's son Ikṣvāku was born Vikukṣi, king among men.

272.s:
vikukṣestu kakutstho 'bhūttasya putraḥ suyodhanaḥ /
:p 9
tasya putraḥ pṛthur nāma viśvagaśvaḥ pṛthoḥ sutaḥ //
272.d:
विकुक्षेस्तु ककुत्स्थो ऽभूत्तस्य पुत्रः सुयोधनः /
:प् 9
तस्य पुत्रः पृथुर् नाम विश्वगश्वः पृथोः सुतः //
272.m:
From Vikukṣi was Kakutstha; his son was Suyodhana.
[Page 9]
His son was named Pṛthu; Viśvagaśva was the son of Pṛthu.

272.s:
āyustasya ca putro 'bhūdyuvanāśvas tathā sutaḥ /
yuvanāśvācca śrāvantaḥ pūrve śrāvantikā purī //
272.d:
आयुस्तस्य च पुत्रो ऽभूद्युवनाश्वस् तथा सुतः /
युवनाश्वाच्च श्रावन्तः पूर्वे श्रावन्तिका पुरी //
272.m: His son was Āyus, and Yuvanāśva was his son; / and from Yuvanāśva came Śrāvanta; formerly, [his city] was the city Śrāvantikā.

272.s:
śrāvantād vṛhadaśvo 'bhūt kubalāśvastato nṛpaḥ /
dhundhumāratvamagamaddhundhor nāmnā ca vai purā //
272.d:
श्रावन्ताद् वृहदश्वो ऽभूत् कुबलाश्वस्ततो नृपः /
धुन्धुमारत्वमगमद्धुन्धोर् नाम्ना च वै पुरा //
272.m: From Śrāvanta was Bṛhadaśva; from him the king was Kuvalāśva. / He attained the title 'Dhundhumāra' ('slayer of Dhundhu') of old on account of Dhundhu.

272.s:
dhundhumārāstrayo bhūpā dṛḍhāśvo daṇḍa eva ca /
kapilo 'tha dṛḍhāśvāttu haryaśvaś ca pramodakaḥ //
272.d:
धुन्धुमारास्त्रयो भूपा दृढाश्वो दण्ड एव च /
कपिलो ऽथ दृढाश्वात्तु हर्यश्वश् च प्रमोदकः //
272.m: The three kings [descended] from Dhundhumāra were Dṛḍhāśva, Daṇḍa, / and Kapila; from Dṛḍhāśva came Haryaśva and Pramodaka.

272.s:
haryaśvācca nikumbho 'bhūt saṃhatāśvo nikumbhataḥ /
akṛśāśvo raṇāśvaś ca saṃhatāśvasutāvubhau //
272.d:
हर्यश्वाच्च निकुम्भो ऽभूत् संहताश्वो निकुम्भतः /
अकृशाश्वो रणाश्वश् च संहताश्वसुतावुभौ //
272.m: From Haryaśva came Nikumbha; from Nikumbha, Saṃhatāśva. / Akṛśāśva and Raṇāśva were both sons of Saṃhatāśva.

272.s:
yuvanāśvo raṇāśvasya māndhātā yuvanāśvataḥ /
māndhātuḥ purukutso 'bhūnmucukundo dvitīyakaḥ //
272.d:
युवनाश्वो रणाश्वस्य मान्धाता युवनाश्वतः /
मान्धातुः पुरुकुत्सो ऽभून्मुचुकुन्दो द्वितीयकः //
