272.m: Yuvanāśva was [the son] of Raṇāśva; from Yuvanāśva came Māndhātṛ. / From Māndhātṛ came Purukutsa, and Mucukunda was the second.

272.s:
purukutsādasasyuś ca sambhūto narmadābhavaḥ /
sambhūtasya sudhanvābhūttridhanvātha sudhanvanaḥ //
272.d:
पुरुकुत्सादसस्युश् च सम्भूतो नर्मदाभवः /
सम्भूतस्य सुधन्वाभूत्त्रिधन्वाथ सुधन्वनः //
272.m: From Purukutsa, Asasyu was born of Narmadā; / of Sambhūta was Sudhanvan; then Tridhanvan was from Sudhanvan.

272.s:
tridhanvanastu taruṇastasya satyavrataḥ sutaḥ /
satyavratātsatyaratho hariś candraś ca tatsutaḥ //
272.d:
त्रिधन्वनस्तु तरुणस्तस्य सत्यव्रतः सुतः /
सत्यव्रतात्सत्यरथो हरिश् चन्द्रश् च तत्सुतः //
272.m: From Tridhanvan was Taruṇa; his son was Satyavrata. / From Satyavrata was Satyaratha, and Hariścandra was his son.

272.s:
hariś candrādrohitāśvo rohitāśvādvṛko 'bhavat /
vṛkādvāhuś ca vāhoś ca sagarastasya ca priyā //
272.d:
हरिश् चन्द्राद्रोहिताश्वो रोहिताश्वाद्वृको ऽभवत् /
वृकाद्वाहुश् च वाहोश् च सगरस्तस्य च प्रिया //
272.m: From Hariścandra came Rohitāśva; from Rohitāśva was Vṛka. / From Vṛka came Bāhu; and from Bāhu, Sagara. And his beloved wife,

272.s:
prabhā ṣaṣṭisahasrāṇāṃ sutānāṃ jananī hy abhūt /
tuṣṭādaurvānnṛpādekaṃ bhānumatyasamañjasam //
272.d:
प्रभा षष्टिसहस्राणां सुतानां जननी ह्य् अभूत् /
तुष्टादौर्वान्नृपादेकं भानुमत्यसमञ्जसम् //
272.m: Prabhā, was the mother of sixty thousand sons. / Through the grace of Aurva, Bhānumatī bore to the king one [son], Asamañjas.

272.s:
khanantaḥ pṛthivīṃ dagdhā viṣṇunā(1) bahusāgarāḥ /
asamañjaso 'ṃśrumāṃś ca dilīpo 'ṃśumato 'bhavat //
272.d:
खनन्तः पृथिवीं दग्धा विष्णुना(1) बहुसागराः /
असमञ्जसो ऽंश्रुमांश् च दिलीपो ऽंशुमतो ऽभवत् //
272.m: Digging the earth, the many sons of Sagara were burned by Viṣṇu. / Asamañjas's [son] was Aṃśumat, and Dilīpa was born from Aṃśumat.

272.s:
bhagīratho dilīpāttu yena gaṅgāvatāritā /
:n
1 munineti ja..
:p 10
bhagīrathāttu nābhāgo nābhāgādambarīṣakaḥ //
272.d:
भगीरथो दिलीपात्तु येन गङ्गावतारिता /
:न्
1 मुनिनेति ज..
:प् 10
भगीरथात्तु नाभागो नाभागादम्बरीषकः //
272.m:
From Dilīpa was Bhagīratha, by whom the Gaṅgā was brought down.
[Note]
1 Ja reads 'muninā' ('by the sage'). / [Page 10]
From Bhagīratha came Nābhāga; from Nābhāga, Ambarīṣa.

272.s:
sindhudvīpo 'mbarīṣāttu śrutāyustatsutaḥ smṛtaḥ /
śrutāyorṛtaparṇo 'bhūttasya kalmāṣapādakaḥ //
272.d:
सिन्धुद्वीपो ऽम्बरीषात्तु श्रुतायुस्तत्सुतः स्मृतः /
श्रुतायोरृतपर्णो ऽभूत्तस्य कल्माषपादकः //
272.m: From Ambarīṣa came Sindhudvīpa; Śrutāyus is remembered as his son. / From Śrutāyus came Ṛtuparṇa; his [son] was Kalmāṣapāda.

272.s:
kalmāṣāṅghreḥ sarvakarmā(1) hy anaraṇyastato 'bhavat /
anaraṇyāttu nighno 'tha anamitrastato raghuḥ //
272.d:
कल्माषाङ्घ्रेः सर्वकर्मा(1) ह्य् अनरण्यस्ततो ऽभवत् /
अनरण्यात्तु निघ्नो ऽथ अनमित्रस्ततो रघुः //
272.m: From Kalmāṣāṅghri came Sarvakarman, and from him was Anaraṇya. / From Anaraṇya came Nighna, then Anamitra, and from him Raghu.

272.s:
raghorabhuddilīpastu dilīpāccāpyajo nṛpaḥ /
dīrghavāhurajāt kālastvajāpālastato 'bhavat //
272.d:
रघोरभुद्दिलीपस्तु दिलीपाच्चाप्यजो नृपः /
दीर्घवाहुरजात् कालस्त्वजापालस्ततो ऽभवत् //
272.m: From Raghu was Dilīpa; and from Dilīpa was King Aja. / From Aja came Dīrghabāhu, and from Ajapāla came Kāla.

272.s:
tatha daśaratho jātastasya putracatuṣṭayam /
nārāyaṇātmakāḥ sarve rāmastasyāgrajo 'bhavat //
272.d:
तथ दशरथो जातस्तस्य पुत्रचतुष्टयम् /
नारायणात्मकाः सर्वे रामस्तस्याग्रजो ऽभवत् //
272.m: Then Daśaratha was born; his sons were four, / all having the nature of Nārāyaṇa; Rāma was his eldest son,

272.s:
rāvaṇāntakaro rājā hy ayodhyāyāṃ raghūttamaḥ /
vālmīkiryasya caritaṃ cakre tannāradaśravāt //
272.d:
रावणान्तकरो राजा ह्य् अयोध्यायां रघूत्तमः /
वाल्मीकिर्यस्य चरितं चक्रे तन्नारदश्रवात् //
272.m: the king who destroyed Rāvaṇa, the best of the Raghus in Ayodhyā, / whose deeds Vālmīki composed upon hearing [them] from Nārada.

272.s:
rāmaputrau kuśalavau sītāyāṃ kulavardhanau /
atithiś ca kuśājjajñe niṣadhastasya cātmajaḥ //
272.d:
रामपुत्रौ कुशलवौ सीतायां कुलवर्धनौ /
अतिथिश् च कुशाज्जज्ञे निषधस्तस्य चात्मजः //
272.m: Rāma's sons on Sītā were Kuśa and Lava, who made their lineage prosper. / Atithi was born from Kuśa, and Niṣadha was his son.

272.s:
niṣadhāttu nalo jajñe nabho 'jāyata vai nalāt /
nabhasaḥ puṇḍarīko 'bhūt sudhanvā ca tato 'bhavat //
272.d:
निषधात्तु नलो जज्ञे नभो ऽजायत वै नलात् /
नभसः पुण्डरीको ऽभूत् सुधन्वा च ततो ऽभवत् //
272.m: From Niṣadha was born Nala; Nabhas was indeed born from Nala. / From Nabhas came Puṇḍarīka, and from him was Sudhanvan.

272.s:
sudhanvano devānīko hy ahīnāśvaś ca tatsutaḥ /
ahīnāśvāt sahasrāśvaś candrālokastato 'bhavat //
272.d:
सुधन्वनो देवानीको ह्य् अहीनाश्वश् च तत्सुतः /
अहीनाश्वात् सहस्राश्वश् चन्द्रालोकस्ततो ऽभवत् //
272.m: From Sudhanvan came Devānīka, and Ahīnāśva was his son. / From Ahīnāśva came Sahasrharśva, and Candrāvaloka was from him.

272.s:
candrāvalokatastārāpīḍo 'smāccandraparvataḥ /
candragirerbhānurathaḥ śrutāyustasya cātmajaḥ /
ikṣvākuvaṃśaprabhavāḥ sūryavaṃśadharāḥ smṛtāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe suryavaṃśakīrtanaṃ nāma
dvisaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 sakarmābhūditi kha.. , cha.. , ca
:p 11
:ś atha trisaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
somavaṃśavarṇanaṃ
272.d:
चन्द्रावलोकतस्तारापीडो ऽस्माच्चन्द्रपर्वतः /
चन्द्रगिरेर्भानुरथः श्रुतायुस्तस्य चात्मजः /
इक्ष्वाकुवंशप्रभवाः सूर्यवंशधराः स्मृताः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सुर्यवंशकीर्तनं नाम
द्विसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 सकर्माभूदिति ख.. , छ.. , च
:प् 11
:श् अथ त्रिसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सोमवंशवर्णनं
272.m:
From Candrāvaloka came Tārāpīḍa; from him Candraparvata; / from Candragiri was Bhānuratha, and Śrutāyus was his son. / Those born in the lineage of Ikṣvāku are remembered as upholder of the Solar Dynasty.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-second chapter in the Agnipurāṇa, entitled 'The Glorification of the Solar Dynasty'.
:n
1. 'sakarmābhūt' according to kha.., cha.., ca
:p 11
Now begins the two hundred and seventy-third chapter.
Description of the Lunar Dynasty

273.s:
agnir uvāca
somavaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi paṭhitaṃ pāpanāśanam /
viṣṇunābhyabjajo brahmā brahmaputro 'triratritaḥ //
273.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
सोमवंशं प्रवक्ष्यामि पठितं पापनाशनम् /
विष्णुनाभ्यब्जजो ब्रह्मा ब्रह्मपुत्रो ऽत्रिरत्रितः //
273.m:
Agni said:
I shall proclaim the Lunar Dynasty, which destroys sins when recited: / Brahmā was born from Viṣṇu's navel-lotus; Brahmā's son was Atri; from Atri [arose] Soma.

273.s:
somaś cakre rājasūyaṃ trailokyaṃ dakṣiṇāndadau /
samāpte 'vabhṛthe somaṃ tadrūpālokanecchavaḥ //
273.d:
सोमश् चक्रे राजसूयं त्रैलोक्यं दक्षिणान्ददौ /
समाप्ते ऽवभृथे सोमं तद्रूपालोकनेच्छवः //
273.m: Soma performed the rājasūya sacrifice and gave the three worlds as the sacrificial fee. / When the concluding ablution was completed, desirous of beholding his form,

273.s:
kāmavāṇābhitaptāṅgyo naradevyaḥ siṣevire /
lakṣmīr narāyaṇaṃ tyaktvā sinīvālī ca kardamama //
273.d:
कामवाणाभितप्ताङ्ग्यो नरदेव्यः सिषेविरे /
लक्ष्मीर् नरायणं त्यक्त्वा सिनीवाली च कर्दमम //
273.m: Their limbs tormented by the arrows of love, divine wives attended upon Soma: / Lakṣmī abandoning Nārāyaṇa, and Sinīvālī [abandoning] Kardama,

273.s:
dyutiṃ vibhāvasuntyaktvā puṣṭirdhātāramavyayam /
prabhā prabhākarantyaktvā haviṣmantaṃ kuhūḥ svayam //
273.d:
द्युतिं विभावसुन्त्यक्त्वा पुष्टिर्धातारमव्ययम् /
प्रभा प्रभाकरन्त्यक्त्वा हविष्मन्तं कुहूः स्वयम् //
273.m: Dyuti abandoning Vibhāvasu, Puṣṭi [abandoning] the imperishable Dhātṛ, / Prabhā abandoning Prabhākara, Kuhū herself [abandoning] Haviṣmat,

273.s:
kīrtirjayantambhartāraṃ vasurmārīcakaśyayam /
dhṛtistyaktvā patiṃ nandīṃ somamevābhajattadā //
273.d:
कीर्तिर्जयन्तम्भर्तारं वसुर्मारीचकश्ययम् /
धृतिस्त्यक्त्वा पतिं नन्दीं सोममेवाभजत्तदा //
273.m: Kīrti [abandoning] her husband Jayanta, Vasu [abandoning] Kaśyapa son of Marīci, / Dhṛti abandoning her husband Nandī—they all resorted to Soma at that time.

273.s:
svakīyā iva somo 'pi kāmayāmāsa tāstadā /
evaṃ kṛtāpacārasya tāsāṃ bhartṛgaṇastadā //
273.d:
स्वकीया इव सोमो ऽपि कामयामास तास्तदा /
एवं कृतापचारस्य तासां भर्तृगणस्तदा //
273.m: Soma too desired them then, as though they were his own wives. / Though he had thus committed transgression, the assembly of their husbands then

273.s:
na śaśākāpacārāya(1) śāpaiḥ śastrādibhiḥ punaḥ /
saptalokaikanāthatvamavāptastapasā hy uta //
273.d:
न शशाकापचाराय(1) शापैः शस्त्रादिभिः पुनः /
सप्तलोकैकनाथत्वमवाप्तस्तपसा ह्य् उत //
273.m: Were unable to harm him by curses, weapons, or other means, / for he had attained singular lordship over the seven worlds by his ascetic austerity.

273.s:
vivabhrāma matistasya vinayādanayā hatā /
vṛhaspateḥ sa vai bhāryāṃ tārāṃ nāma yaśasvinīm //
273.d:
विवभ्राम मतिस्तस्य विनयादनया हता /
वृहस्पतेः स वै भार्यां तारां नाम यशस्विनीम् //
273.m: His intellect wandered astray, ruined by misconduct away from propriety. / The illustrious wife of Bṛhaspati, named Tārā,

273.s:
jahāra tarasā somo hy avamanyāṅgiraḥsutam /
tatastadyuddhamabhavat prakhyātaṃ tārakāmayam //
:n
1 na śaśākāpakārāyeti ña..
:p 12
273.d:
जहार तरसा सोमो ह्य् अवमन्याङ्गिरःसुतम् /
ततस्तद्युद्धमभवत् प्रख्यातं तारकामयम् //
:न्
1 न शशाकापकारायेति ञ..
:प् 12
273.m:
Soma forcibly abducted, slighting the son of Aṅgiras. / Then there arose that great war, renowned as Tārakāmaya,
:n
1. 'na śaśākāpakārāya' according to manuscript ña..
:p 12

273.s:
devānāṃ dānavānāñca lokakṣayakaraṃ mahat /
brahmā nivāryośanasantārāmaṅgirase dadau //
273.d:
देवानां दानवानाञ्च लोकक्षयकरं महत् /
ब्रह्मा निवार्योशनसन्तारामङ्गिरसे ददौ //
273.m: Between the gods and demons, causing the great destruction of worlds. / Brahmā, having restrained Uśanas, gave Tārā back to the son of Aṅgiras.

273.s:
tāmantaḥprasavāṃ dṛṣṭvā garbhaṃ tyajābravīdguruḥ /
garbhastyaktaḥ pradīpto 'tha prāhāhaṃ somasanbhavaḥ //
273.d:
तामन्तःप्रसवां दृष्ट्वा गर्भं त्यजाब्रवीद्गुरुः /
गर्भस्त्यक्तः प्रदीप्तो ऽथ प्राहाहं सोमसन्भवः //
273.m: Seeing her pregnant, Guru said: 'Cast out the child!' / Cast out, the radiant fetus then said: 'I am Soma's son.'

273.s:
evaṃ somādbudhaḥ puttraḥ puttrastasya purūravāḥ /
svargantyaktvorvaśī sā taṃ varayāmāsa cāpsarāḥ //
273.d:
एवं सोमाद्बुधः पुत्त्रः पुत्त्रस्तस्य पुरूरवाः /
स्वर्गन्त्यक्त्वोर्वशी सा तं वरयामास चाप्सराः //
273.m: Thus Budha was born as a son to Soma; his son was Purūravas. / Abandoning heaven, that apsaras Urvaśī chose him [as husband].

273.s:
tayā sahācaradrājā daśavarṣāṇi pañca ca /
pañca ṣaṭ sapta cāṣṭau ca daśa cāṣṭau mahāmune //
273.d:
तया सहाचरद्राजा दशवर्षाणि पञ्च च /
पञ्च षट् सप्त चाष्टौ च दश चाष्टौ महामुने //
273.m: With her the king lived for ten years and five, / and five, six, seven, and eight, and ten and eight, O great sage.

273.s:
eko 'gnirabhavat pūrvaṃ tena tretā pravartitā /
purūravā yogaśīlo gāndharvalokamīyivān //
273.d:
एको ऽग्निरभवत् पूर्वं तेन त्रेता प्रवर्तिता /
पुरूरवा योगशीलो गान्धर्वलोकमीयिवान् //
273.m: Formerly there was one fire; by him the threefold sacrificial fire was instituted. / Devoted to yoga, Purūravas went to the world of the Gandharvas.

273.s:
āyurdṛ.ḍhāyuraśvāyurdhanāyurdhṛtimān vasuḥ /
divijātaḥ śatāyuś ca suṣuve corvaśī nṛpān //
273.d:
आयुर्दृ.ढायुरश्वायुर्धनायुर्धृतिमान् वसुः /
दिविजातः शतायुश् च सुषुवे चोर्वशी नृपान् //
273.m: Āyus, Dṛḍhāyus, Aśvāyus, Dhanāyus, Dhṛtimat, Vasu, / Divijāta, and Śatāyus—Urvaśī gave birth to these kings.

273.s:
āyuṣo nahuṣaḥ putro vṛddhaśarmā rajis tathā /
darbho vipāpmā pañcāgnyaṃ(1) rajeḥ putraśataṃ hy abhūt //
273.d:
आयुषो नहुषः पुत्रो वृद्धशर्मा रजिस् तथा /
दर्भो विपाप्मा पञ्चाग्न्यं(1) रजेः पुत्रशतं ह्य् अभूत् //
273.m: The sons of Āyus were Nahuṣa, Vṛddhaśarman, as well as Raji, / Darbha, and Vipāpman—five like the sacred fires. Raji indeed had a hundred sons,

273.s:
rājeyā iti vikhyātā viṣṇudattavaro rajiḥ /
devāsure raṇe daityānabadhītsurayācitaḥ //
273.d:
राजेया इति विख्याता विष्णुदत्तवरो रजिः /
देवासुरे रणे दैत्यानबधीत्सुरयाचितः //
273.m: Known as the Rājeyas. Raji received a boon from Viṣṇu; / solicited by the gods, he slew the Daityas in the war between gods and demons.

273.s:
gatāyendrāya putratvaṃ datvā rājyaṃ divaṅgataḥ /
rajeḥ putrair hṛtaṃ rājyaṃ śakrasyātha sudurmanāḥ //
273.d:
गतायेन्द्राय पुत्रत्वं दत्वा राज्यं दिवङ्गतः /
रजेः पुत्रैर् हृतं राज्यं शक्रस्याथ सुदुर्मनाः //
273.m: Having granted sonship to Indra when his life was spent, he went to heaven. / Then Indra's kingdom was seized by the sons of Raji, and Śakra was deeply dejected.

273.s:
grahaśāntyādividhinā gururindrāya taddadau /
mohayitvā rajisutānāsaṃste nijadharmagāḥ //
273.d:
ग्रहशान्त्यादिविधिना गुरुरिन्द्राय तद्ददौ /
मोहयित्वा रजिसुतानासंस्ते निजधर्मगाः //
273.m: Guru restored it to Indra through rites such as the pacification of planets; / having deluded the sons of Raji, they fell away from their own proper duty.

273.s:
nahuṣasya sutāḥ sapta yatiryayātiruttamaḥ /
udbhavaḥ pañcakaś caiva śaryātimeghapālakau //
:n
1 pañcāgnyā iti ja.. / pañcāgnyamiti ña..
:p 13
273.d:
नहुषस्य सुताः सप्त यतिर्ययातिरुत्तमः /
उद्भवः पञ्चकश् चैव शर्यातिमेघपालकौ //
:न्
1 पञ्चाग्न्या इति ज.. / पञ्चाग्न्यमिति ञ..
:प् 13
273.m:
Nahuṣa had seven sons: Yati, the excellent Yayāti, / Udbhava, Pañcaka, and Śaryāti and Meghapālaka.
[Footnote]
1 'pañcāgnyaḥ' in ja.. / 'pañcāgnyam' in ña..
[Page 13]

273.s:
yatiḥ kumārabhāve 'pi viṣṇuṃ dhyātvā hariṃ gataḥ /
devayānī śakrakanyā yayāteḥ patny abhūt tadā //
273.d:
यतिः कुमारभावे ऽपि विष्णुं ध्यात्वा हरिं गतः /
देवयानी शक्रकन्या ययातेः पत्न्य् अभूत् तदा //
273.m: Yati, even in boyhood, meditating on Viṣṇu, attained Hari. / Devayānī, daughter of Śakra, then became the wife of Yayāti.

273.s:
vṛṣaparvajā śarmiṣṭhā yayāteḥ pañca tatsutāḥ /
yaduñca turvasuñcaiva devayānī vyajāyata //
273.d:
वृषपर्वजा शर्मिष्ठा ययातेः पञ्च तत्सुताः /
यदुञ्च तुर्वसुञ्चैव देवयानी व्यजायत //
273.m: Śarmiṣṭhā was the daughter of Vṛṣaparvan. Yayāti had five sons from them: / Devayānī gave birth to Yadu and Turvasu,

273.s:
druhyañcānūñca pūruñca śarmiṣṭhā vārṣaparvaṇī /
yaduḥ pūruścābhavatānteṣāṃ vaṃśavivardhanau //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe somavaṃśavarṇanaṃ nama
trisaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
atha catuḥsaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
yaduvaṃśavarṇanaṃ
273.d:
द्रुह्यञ्चानूञ्च पूरुञ्च शर्मिष्ठा वार्षपर्वणी /
यदुः पूरुश्चाभवतान्तेषां वंशविवर्धनौ //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सोमवंशवर्णनं नम
त्रिसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
अथ चतुःसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
यदुवंशवर्णनं
273.m:
And Śarmiṣṭhā, daughter of Vṛṣaparvan, [gave birth to] Druhyu, Anu, and Pūru. / Yadu and Pūru became the increasers of their lineages.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-third chapter, entitled 'Description of the Lunar Dynasty', in the great Agni Purāṇa.
Now begins the two hundred and seventy-fourth chapter:
Description of the Yadu Dynasty

274.s:
agnir uvāca
yadorāsanpañca putrā jyeṣṭhasteṣu sahasrajit /
nīlāñjako radhuḥ kroṣṭuḥ śatajicca sahasrajit //
274.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
यदोरासन्पञ्च पुत्रा ज्येष्ठस्तेषु सहस्रजित् /
नीलाञ्जको रधुः क्रोष्टुः शतजिच्च सहस्रजित् //
274.m: Agni said: / Yadu had five sons, the eldest among them was Sahasrajit: / Nīlāñjaka, Raghu, Kroṣṭu, Śatajit, and Sahasrajit.

274.s:
śatajiddhaihayo reṇuhayo haya iti trayaḥ /
dharmanetro haihayasya dharmanetrasya saṃhanaḥ //
274.d:
शतजिद्धैहयो रेणुहयो हय इति त्रयः /
धर्मनेत्रो हैहयस्य धर्मनेत्रस्य संहनः //
274.m: [From] Śatajit [were born] three: Haihaya, Reṇuhaya, and Haya. / Haihaya's [son was] Dharmanetra; Dharmanetra's [son was] Saṃhana.

274.s:
mahimā saṃhanasyāsīnmahimnao bhadrasenakaḥ /
bhadrasenād durgamo 'bhūddurgamātkanako 'bhavat //
274.d:
महिमा संहनस्यासीन्महिम्नओ भद्रसेनकः /
भद्रसेनाद् दुर्गमो ऽभूद्दुर्गमात्कनको ऽभवत् //
274.m: Mahiman was [the son] of Saṃhana; from Mahiman came Bhadrasenaka; / from Bhadrasena came Durgama; from Durgama was Kanaka.

274.s:
kanakāt kṛtavīryastu kṛtāgniḥ karavīrakaḥ /
kṛtaujāś ca caturtho 'bhūt kṛtavīryāttu so 'rjunaḥ //
274.d:
कनकात् कृतवीर्यस्तु कृताग्निः करवीरकः /
कृतौजाश् च चतुर्थो ऽभूत् कृतवीर्यात्तु सो ऽर्जुनः //
274.m: From Kanaka came Kṛtavīrya, Kṛtāgni, Karavīraka, / and Kṛtaujas was the fourth; and from Kṛtavīrya came that Arjuna.

274.s:
datto 'rjunāya tapate saptadvīpamahīśatām /
dadau bāhusahasrañca ajeyatvaṃ raṇe 'riṇā //
:p 14
274.d:
दत्तो ऽर्जुनाय तपते सप्तद्वीपमहीशताम् /
ददौ बाहुसहस्रञ्च अजेयत्वं रणे ऽरिणा //
:प् 14
274.m:
Datta gave to Arjuna, as he practiced ascetic austerity, lordship over the earth of seven continents, / and gave him a thousand arms and unconquerability in battle by foes,
[Page 14]

274.s:
adharme vartamānasya viṣṇuhastānmṛtirdhruvā /
daśa yajñasahasrāṇi so 'rjunaḥ kṛtavānnṛpāḥ //
274.d:
अधर्मे वर्तमानस्य विष्णुहस्तान्मृतिर्ध्रुवा /
दश यज्ञसहस्राणि सो ऽर्जुनः कृतवान्नृपाः //
274.m: And certain death from the hand of Viṣṇu should he turn to unrighteousness. / That Arjuna performed ten thousand sacrifices, O kings.

274.s:
anaṣṭadravyatā rāṣṭre tasya saṃsmaraṇādabhūt /
na nūnaṃ kārttavīryasya gatiṃ yāsyanti vai nṛpaḥ //
274.d:
अनष्टद्रव्यता राष्ट्रे तस्य संस्मरणादभूत् /
न नूनं कार्त्तवीर्यस्य गतिं यास्यन्ति वै नृपः //
274.m: By mere remembrance of him, no property was lost in his realm. / Truly, no kings will attain the rank of Kārttavīrya,

274.s:
yajñair dānaistapobhiś ca vikrameṇa śrutena ca /
kartavīryasya ca śataṃ putrāṇāṃ pañca vai parāḥ //
274.d:
यज्ञैर् दानैस्तपोभिश् च विक्रमेण श्रुतेन च /
कर्तवीर्यस्य च शतं पुत्राणां पञ्च वै पराः //
274.m: In sacrifices, gifts, ascetic austerities, valor, and sacred learning. / Kārtavīrya had a hundred sons, among whom five were pre-eminent:

274.s:
sūrasenaś ca sūraś ca dhṛṣṭoktaḥ kṛṣṇa eva ca /
jayadhvajaś ca nāmāsīdāvantyo nṛpatirmahān //
274.d:
सूरसेनश् च सूरश् च धृष्टोक्तः कृष्ण एव च /
जयध्वजश् च नामासीदावन्त्यो नृपतिर्महान् //
274.m: Śūrasena, Śūra, the one called Dhṛṣṭa, and Kṛṣṇa, / and Jayadhvaja by name, who was the great king of Avanti.

274.s:
jayadhvajāttālajaṅghastālajaṅghāttataḥ sutāḥ /
haihayānāṃ kulāḥ pañca bhojāścāvantayas tathā //
274.d:
जयध्वजात्तालजङ्घस्तालजङ्घात्ततः सुताः /
हैहयानां कुलाः पञ्च भोजाश्चावन्तयस् तथा //
274.m: From Jayadhvaja came Tālajaṅgha; from Tālajaṅgha were born sons: / the five clans of the Haihayas, the Bhojas, and likewise the Āvantyas,

274.s:
vītihotrāḥ svayaṃ jātāḥ śauṇḍikeyāstathaiva ca /
vītihotrādananto 'bhudanantāddurjayo nṛpaḥ //
274.d:
वीतिहोत्राः स्वयं जाताः शौण्डिकेयास्तथैव च /
वीतिहोत्रादनन्तो ऽभुदनन्ताद्दुर्जयो नृपः //
274.m: The Vītihotras born of himself, and likewise the Śauṇḍikeyas. / From Vītihotra came Ananta; from Ananta came King Durjaya.

274.s:
kroṣṭorvaṃśaṃ pravakṣyāmi yatra jāto hariḥ svayam /
kroṣṭostu vṛjinīvāṃś ca svāhābhūdvṛjinīvataḥ //
274.d:
क्रोष्टोर्वंशं प्रवक्ष्यामि यत्र जातो हरिः स्वयम् /
क्रोष्टोस्तु वृजिनीवांश् च स्वाहाभूद्वृजिनीवतः //
274.m: I shall declare the lineage of Kroṣṭu, in which Hari himself was born: / From Kroṣṭu came Vṛjinīvat; Svāhā was born from Vṛjinīvat.

274.s:
svāhāputrao ruṣadguś ca(1) tasya citrarathaḥ sutaḥ /
śaśavinduścitrarathāccakravartī harau rataḥ //
274.d:
स्वाहापुत्रओ रुषद्गुश् च(1) तस्य चित्ररथः सुतः /
शशविन्दुश्चित्ररथाच्चक्रवर्ती हरौ रतः //
274.m: Svāhā's son was Ruṣadgu; his son was Citraratha. / From Citraratha came Śaśabindu, a universal emperor devoted to Hari.

274.s:
śaśavindoś ca puttrāṇāṃ śatānāmabhavacchatam /
dhīmatāṃ cārurūpāṇāṃ bhūridraviṇatejasām //
274.d:
शशविन्दोश् च पुत्त्राणां शतानामभवच्छतम् /
धीमतां चारुरूपाणां भूरिद्रविणतेजसाम् //
274.m: Śaśabindu had a hundred hundred sons, / wise, of handsome form, possessing abundant wealth and splendor.

274.s:
pṛthuśravāḥ pradhāno 'bhūttasya putraḥ suyajñakaḥ /
suyajñasyośanāḥ putrastitikṣuruśanaḥsutaḥ //
274.d:
पृथुश्रवाः प्रधानो ऽभूत्तस्य पुत्रः सुयज्ञकः /
सुयज्ञस्योशनाः पुत्रस्तितिक्षुरुशनःसुतः //
274.m: Pṛthuśravas was foremost among them; his son was Suyajñaka. / Suyajña's son was Uśanas; Titikṣu was the son of Uśanas.

274.s:
titikṣostu marutto 'bhūttasmātkambalavarhiṣaḥ /
pañcāśadrukmakavacādrukmeṣuḥ pṛthurukmakaḥ //
:n
1 viṣāṃśuśceti ja..
:p 15
274.d:
तितिक्षोस्तु मरुत्तो ऽभूत्तस्मात्कम्बलवर्हिषः /
पञ्चाशद्रुक्मकवचाद्रुक्मेषुः पृथुरुक्मकः //
:न्
1 विषांशुश्चेति ज..
:प् 15
274.m:
From Titikṣu came Marutta; from him Kambalabarhis. / From Rukmakavaca came fifty [sons, including] Rukmeṣu and Pṛthurukmaka,
[Footnote]
1 'viṣāṃśuś ca' in ja..
[Page 15]

274.s:
havirjyāmaghaḥ pāpaghno jyāmaghaḥ strījito 'bhavat /
sevyāyāṃ jyāmaghādāsīdvidarbhastasya kauśikaḥ //
274.d:
हविर्ज्यामघः पापघ्नो ज्यामघः स्त्रीजितो ऽभवत् /
सेव्यायां ज्यामघादासीद्विदर्भस्तस्य कौशिकः //
274.m: Havis, and the destroyer of sins Jyāmagha; Jyāmagha was subjugated by his wife. / From Jyāmagha on Sevyā was Vidarbha; his [son was] Kauśika.

274.s:
lomapādaḥ krathaḥ śreṣṭhāt kṛtiḥ(1) syāllomapadataḥ /
kauśikasya cidiḥ putrastasmāccaidyā nṛpāḥ smṛtāḥ //
274.d:
लोमपादः क्रथः श्रेष्ठात् कृतिः(1) स्याल्लोमपदतः /
कौशिकस्य चिदिः पुत्रस्तस्माच्चैद्या नृपाः स्मृताः //
274.m: From the best Lomapāda came Kratha; Kṛti came from Lomapāda. / Kauśika's son was Cidi; from him the Caidya kings are remembered.

274.s:
krathādvidarbhaputrāś ca kuntiḥ kuntestu dhṛṣṭakaḥ /
dhṛṣṭasya nidhṛtistasya udarkākhyo vidūrathaḥ //
274.d:
क्रथाद्विदर्भपुत्राश् च कुन्तिः कुन्तेस्तु धृष्टकः /
धृष्टस्य निधृतिस्तस्य उदर्काख्यो विदूरथः //
274.m: From Kratha, son of Vidarbha, came sons: Kunti; from Kunti came Dhṛṣṭaka; / from Dhṛṣṭa came Nidhṛti; his son was Vidūratha, known as Udarka.

274.s:
daśārhaputro vyomastu vyomājjīmūta ucyate /
jīmūtaputro vikalastasya bhīmarathaḥ sutaḥ //
274.d:
दशार्हपुत्रो व्योमस्तु व्योमाज्जीमूत उच्यते /
जीमूतपुत्रो विकलस्तस्य भीमरथः सुतः //
274.m: The son of Daśārha was Vyoman; from Vyoman, Jīmūta is spoken of. / Jīmūta's son was Vikala; his son was Bhīmaratha.

274.s:
bhīmarathānnavarathastato dṛḍharatho 'bhavat /
śakuntiś ca dṛḍharathāt śakunteś ca karambhakaḥ //
274.d:
भीमरथान्नवरथस्ततो दृढरथो ऽभवत् /
शकुन्तिश् च दृढरथात् शकुन्तेश् च करम्भकः //
274.m: From Bhīmaratha came Navaratha; from him came Dṛḍharatha. / Śakunti was from Dṛḍharatha, and Karambhaka was from Śakunti.

274.s:
karambhāddevalāto 'bhūt(2) devakṣetraś ca tatsutaḥ /
devakṣetrānmadhurnāma madhordravaraso 'bhavat //
274.d:
करम्भाद्देवलातो ऽभूत्(2) देवक्षेत्रश् च तत्सुतः /
देवक्षेत्रान्मधुर्नाम मधोर्द्रवरसो ऽभवत् //
274.m: From Karambha came Devalāta, and Devakṣetra was his son. / From Devakṣetra came one named Madhu; from Madhu came Dravarasa.

274.s:
dravarasāt puruhūto 'bhūjjanturāsīttu tatsutaḥ /
guṇī tu yādavo rājā jantuputrastu sāttvataḥ //
274.d:
द्रवरसात् पुरुहूतो ऽभूज्जन्तुरासीत्तु तत्सुतः /
गुणी तु यादवो राजा जन्तुपुत्रस्तु सात्त्वतः //
274.m: From Dravarasa came Puruhūta; his son was Jantu. / The virtuous Yādava king, the son of Jantu, was Sāttvata.

274.s:
sāttvatādbhajamānastu vṛṣṇirandhaka eva ca /
devāvṛdhaś ca catvārasteṣāṃ vaṃśāstu viśrutāḥ(3) //
274.d:
सात्त्वताद्भजमानस्तु वृष्णिरन्धक एव च /
देवावृधश् च चत्वारस्तेषां वंशास्तु विश्रुताः(3) //
274.m: From Sāttvata came Bhajamāna, Vṛṣṇi, Andhaka, / and Devāvṛdha—four whose lineages are renowned.

274.s:
bhajamānasya vāhyo 'bhūdvṛṣṭiḥ kṛmirnimis tathā /
devāvṛdhādvabhrurāsīttasya śloko 'tra gīyate //
274.d:
भजमानस्य वाह्यो ऽभूद्वृष्टिः कृमिर्निमिस् तथा /
देवावृधाद्वभ्रुरासीत्तस्य श्लोको ऽत्र गीयते //
274.m: Of Bhajamāna were Bāhya, Vṛṣṭi, Kṛmi, and Nimi. / From Devāvṛdha came Babhru; about him this verse is sung:

274.s:
yathaiva śṛṇumo dūrāt guṇāṃstadvatsamantikāt /
vabhruḥ śreṣṭho manuṣyāṇāṃ devair devāvṛdhaḥsamaḥ //
274.d:
यथैव शृणुमो दूरात् गुणांस्तद्वत्समन्तिकात् /
वभ्रुः श्रेष्ठो मनुष्याणां देवैर् देवावृधःसमः //
274.m: 'Just as we hear of his virtues from afar, so are they found close at hand: / Babhru is foremost among men; Devāvṛdha is equal to the gods.'

274.s:
catvāraś ca sutā vabhrorvāsudevaparā nṛpāḥ /
:n
1 dhṛtiriti ña..
2 devarāto 'bhuditi kha.. , ga.. , gha.. , ja.. , ña.. , ṭa.. , ca
3 vistṛtā iti ka.. , cha.. , ca
:p 16
kuhuro bhajamānastu(1) śiniḥ kambalavarhiṣaḥ //
274.d:
चत्वारश् च सुता वभ्रोर्वासुदेवपरा नृपाः /
:न्
1 धृतिरिति ञ..
2 देवरातो ऽभुदिति ख.. , ग.. , घ.. , ज.. , ञ.. , ट.. , च
3 विस्तृता इति क.. , छ.. , च
:प् 16
कुहुरो भजमानस्तु(1) शिनिः कम्बलवर्हिषः //
274.m:
And the four sons of Babhru were kings devoted to Vāsudeva.
[Footnote]
1 'dhṛtiḥ' in ña..
2 'devarāto 'bhūt' in kha.., ga.., gha.., ja.., ña.., ṭa.., and
3 'vistṛtāḥ' in ka.., cha.., and
[Page 16]
Kuhura, Bhajamāna, Śini, and Kambalabarhis.

274.s:
kuhurasya(2) suto dhṛṣṇudhṛṣṇostu tanayo dhṛtiḥ /
dhṛteḥ kapotaromābhūttasya putrastu tittiriḥ //
274.d:
कुहुरस्य(2) सुतो धृष्णुधृष्णोस्तु तनयो धृतिः /
धृतेः कपोतरोमाभूत्तस्य पुत्रस्तु तित्तिरिः //
274.m: The son of Kuhura was Dhṛṣṇu; Dhṛṣṇu's son was Dhṛti. / From Dhṛti came Kapotaroman; his son was Tittiri.

274.s:
tittirestu naraḥ putrastasya candanadundubhiḥ /
punarvasustasya putra āhukaścāhukīsutaḥ //
274.d:
तित्तिरेस्तु नरः पुत्रस्तस्य चन्दनदुन्दुभिः /
पुनर्वसुस्तस्य पुत्र आहुकश्चाहुकीसुतः //
274.m: The son of Tittiri was Nara; his [son was] Candanadundubhi. / His son was Punarvasu; Āhuka and the daughter Āhukī [were his children].

274.s:
āhukāddevako jajñe ugrasenastato 'bhavat /
devavānupadevaś ca devakasya sutāḥ smṛtāḥ //
274.d:
आहुकाद्देवको जज्ञे उग्रसेनस्ततो ऽभवत् /
देववानुपदेवश् च देवकस्य सुताः स्मृताः //
274.m: From Āhuka was born Devaka; then Ugrasena came into being. / Devavat and Upadeva are known as the sons of Devaka.

274.s:
teṣāṃ svasāraḥ saptāsan vasudevāya tā dadau /
devakī śrutadevī ca mitradevī yathodharā //
274.d:
तेषां स्वसारः सप्तासन् वसुदेवाय ता ददौ /
देवकी श्रुतदेवी च मित्रदेवी यथोधरा //
274.m: They had seven sisters; he gave them to Vasudeva: / Devakī, Śrutadevī, Mitradevī, Yathodharā,

274.s:
śrīdevī satyadevī ca surāpī ceti saptamī /
navograsenasya sutāḥ kaṃsasteṣāñca pūrvajaḥ //
274.d:
श्रीदेवी सत्यदेवी च सुरापी चेति सप्तमी /
नवोग्रसेनस्य सुताः कंसस्तेषाञ्च पूर्वजः //
274.m: Śrīdevī, Satyadevī, and Surāpī as the seventh. / Ugrasena had nine sons, Kaṃsa being the eldest among them,

274.s:
nyagrodhaś ca sunāmā ca kaṅkaḥ śaṅkuś ca bhūmipaḥ /
sutanūrāṣṭrapālaś ca yuddhamuṣṭiḥ sumuṣṭikaḥ //
274.d:
न्यग्रोधश् च सुनामा च कङ्कः शङ्कुश् च भूमिपः /
सुतनूराष्ट्रपालश् च युद्धमुष्टिः सुमुष्टिकः //
274.m: As well as Nyagrodha, Sunāman, Kaṅka, and King Śaṅku, / Sutanu, Rāṣṭrapāla, Yuddhamuṣṭi, and Sumuṣṭika.

274.s:
bhajamānasya putro 'tha rathamukhyo vidūrathaḥ /
rājādhidevaḥ śūraś ca vidūrathasuto 'bhavat //
274.d:
भजमानस्य पुत्रो ऽथ रथमुख्यो विदूरथः /
राजाधिदेवः शूरश् च विदूरथसुतो ऽभवत् //
274.m: Then the son of Bhajamāna was Vidūratha, foremost of charioteers. / Rājādhideva and Śūra were the sons of Vidūratha.

274.s:
rājādhidevaputrau dvau śoṇāś caḥ śvetavāhanaḥ /
śoṇāśvasya sutāḥ pañca śamī śatrujidādayaḥ(3) //
274.d:
राजाधिदेवपुत्रौ द्वौ शोणाश् चः श्वेतवाहनः /
शोणाश्वस्य सुताः पञ्च शमी शत्रुजिदादयः(3) //
274.m: The two sons of Rājādhideva were Śoṇāśva and Śvetavāhana. / Śoṇāśva had five sons: Śamī, Śatrujit, and the rest.

274.s:
śamīputraḥ pratikṣetraḥ pratikṣetrasya bhojakaḥ /
bhojasya hṛdikaḥ putro hy adikasya daśātmajāḥ //
274.d:
शमीपुत्रः प्रतिक्षेत्रः प्रतिक्षेत्रस्य भोजकः /
भोजस्य हृदिकः पुत्रो ह्य् अदिकस्य दशात्मजाः //
274.m: Śamī's son was Pratikṣetra; of Pratikṣetra, Bhojaka. / The son of Bhoja was Hṛdika; and Hṛdika had ten sons:

274.s:
kṛtavarmā śatadhanvā devārho bhīṣaṇādayaḥ /
:n
1 kukuro bhajamānastviti ka.. / sundaro bhajamānastviti ja..
2 kukurasyeti ka..
3 śakrajidādaya iti kha..
:p 17
devārhāt kambalavarhirasamaujāstato 'bhavat //
274.d:
कृतवर्मा शतधन्वा देवार्हो भीषणादयः /
:न्
1 कुकुरो भजमानस्त्विति क.. / सुन्दरो भजमानस्त्विति ज..
2 कुकुरस्येति क..
3 शक्रजिदादय इति ख..
:प् 17
देवार्हात् कम्बलवर्हिरसमौजास्ततो ऽभवत् //
274.m:
Kṛtavarman, Śatadhanvan, Devārha, Bhīṣaṇa, and the rest.
[Footnote]
1 'kukuro bhajamānastu' in ka.. / 'sundaro bhajamānastu' in ja..
2 'kukurasya' in ka..
3 'Śakrajit and others' in manuscript kha.
From Devārha came Kambalabarhis; from him was Asamaujas.

274.s:
sudaṃṣṭraś ca suvāsaś ca dhṛṣṭo 'bhūdasamaujasaḥ /
gāndhārī caiva mādrī ca dhṛṣṭabhārye babhūvatuḥ //
274.d:
सुदंष्ट्रश् च सुवासश् च धृष्टो ऽभूदसमौजसः /
गान्धारी चैव माद्री च धृष्टभार्ये बभूवतुः //
274.m: Sudaṃṣṭra, Suvāsa, and Dhṛṣṭa were sons of Asamaujas. / Gāndhārī and Mādrī became the two wives of Dhṛṣṭa.

274.s:
sumitro 'bhūcca gāndhāryāṃ mādrī jajñe yudhājitam(1) /
anamitraḥ śinirdhṛṣṭāttato vai devamīḍhuṣaḥ //
274.d:
सुमित्रो ऽभूच्च गान्धार्यां माद्री जज्ञे युधाजितम्(1) /
अनमित्रः शिनिर्धृष्टात्ततो वै देवमीढुषः //
274.m: Sumitra was born of Gāndhārī, and Mādrī gave birth to Yudhājit. / Anamitra and Śini were born from Dhṛṣṭa, and from him indeed came Devamīḍhuṣa.

274.s:
anamitrasuto nighno nighnasyāpi prasenakaḥ /
satrājitaḥ praseno 'tha maṇiṃ sūryātsyamantakam //
274.d:
अनमित्रसुतो निघ्नो निघ्नस्यापि प्रसेनकः /
सत्राजितः प्रसेनो ऽथ मणिं सूर्यात्स्यमन्तकम् //
274.m: Anamitra's son was Nighna, and Nighna's son was Prasena. / Prasena and Satrājit [were his sons]. Then, [having obtained] the Syamantaka jewel from Sūrya,

274.s:
prāpyāraṇye carantantu siṃho hatvāgrahīnmaṇiṃ /
hato jāmbavatā siṃho jāmbavān hariṇā jitaḥ //
274.d:
प्राप्यारण्ये चरन्तन्तु सिंहो हत्वाग्रहीन्मणिं /
हतो जाम्बवता सिंहो जाम्बवान् हरिणा जितः //
274.m: a lion killed [Prasena] wandering in the forest and took the jewel. / The lion was slain by Jāmbavat, and Jāmbavat was conquered by Hari.

274.s:
tasmānmaṇiṃ jāmbavatīṃ prāpyāgāddārakāṃ purīm /
satrājitāya pradadau śatadhanvā jaghāna tam //
274.d:
तस्मान्मणिं जाम्बवतीं प्राप्यागाद्दारकां पुरीम् /
सत्राजिताय प्रददौ शतधन्वा जघान तम् //
274.m: Having obtained the jewel and Jāmbavatī from him, [Hari] went to the city of Dvārakā. / He gave it to Satrājit; [then] Śatadhanvan killed him.

274.s:
hatvā śatadhanuṃ kṛṣṇo maṇimādāya kīrtibhāk /
balayādavamukhyāgre akrūrānmaṇimarpayet //
274.d:
हत्वा शतधनुं कृष्णो मणिमादाय कीर्तिभाक् /
बलयादवमुख्याग्रे अक्रूरान्मणिमर्पयेत् //
274.m: Having slain Śatadhanu and taken the jewel, renowned Kṛṣṇa / presented the jewel, [recovered] from Akrūra, before Bala and the foremost Yādavas.

274.s:
mithyābhiśastiṃ kṛṣṇasya tyaktvā svargī ca sampaṭhan /
satrājito bhaṅgakāraḥ satyabhāmā hareḥ priyā //
274.d:
मिथ्याभिशस्तिं कृष्णस्य त्यक्त्वा स्वर्गी च सम्पठन् /
सत्राजितो भङ्गकारः सत्यभामा हरेः प्रिया //
274.m: Having recited [this], one is freed from false accusations concerning Kṛṣṇa and attains heaven. / Satrājit was the causer of discord; Satyabhāmā was the beloved of Hari.

274.s:
anamitrācchinirjajñe satyakastu śineḥ sutaḥ /
satyakātsātyakirjajñe yuyudhānāddhunirhyabhūt //
274.d:
अनमित्राच्छिनिर्जज्ञे सत्यकस्तु शिनेः सुतः /
सत्यकात्सात्यकिर्जज्ञे युयुधानाद्धुनिर्ह्यभूत् //
274.m: From Anamitra was born Śini, and Satyaka was the son of Śini. / From Satyaka, Sātyaki was born; from Yuyudhāna came Dhuni.

274.s:
dhuneryugandharaḥ putraḥ svāhyo 'bhut(2) sa yudhājitaḥ /
ṛṣabhakṣetrakau tasya hy ṛṣabhācca svaphalkakaḥ //
274.d:
धुनेर्युगन्धरः पुत्रः स्वाह्यो ऽभुत्(2) स युधाजितः /
ऋषभक्षेत्रकौ तस्य ह्य् ऋषभाच्च स्वफल्ककः //
274.m: Dhuni's son was Yugandhara; Svāhya was born from Yudhājit. / Ṛṣabha and Kṣetraka were his sons; and from Ṛṣabha came Svaphalka.

274.s:
svaphalkaputro hy akrūro akūrācca sudhanvakaḥ /
śūrāttu vasudevādyāḥ pṛthā pāṇḍoḥ priyābhavat //
:n
1 sudhājitamiti kha.. , cha.. ca
2 svāndhobhūditi kha.. , cha.. ca / sākṣo 'bhūditi ja..
:p 18
274.d:
स्वफल्कपुत्रो ह्य् अक्रूरो अकूराच्च सुधन्वकः /
शूरात्तु वसुदेवाद्याः पृथा पाण्डोः प्रियाभवत् //
:न्
1 सुधाजितमिति ख.. , छ.. च
2 स्वान्धोभूदिति ख.. , छ.. च / साक्षो ऽभूदिति ज..
:प् 18
274.m:
Svaphalka's son was Akrūra, and from Akrūra came Sudhanvan. / From Śūra came Vasudeva and the others; Pṛthā became the beloved [wife] of Pāṇḍu.
[Footnote]
1 'Sudhājitam' in manuscripts kha and cha.
2 'Svāndho 'bhūt' in manuscripts kha and cha; 'sākṣo 'bhūt' in manuscript ja.

274.s:
dharmādyudhiṣṭhiraḥ pāṇḍorvāyoḥ kuntyāṃ vṛkodaraḥ /
indrāddhanañjayo mādryāṃ nakulaḥ sahadevakaḥ //
274.d:
धर्माद्युधिष्ठिरः पाण्डोर्वायोः कुन्त्यां वृकोदरः /
इन्द्राद्धनञ्जयो माद्र्यां नकुलः सहदेवकः //
274.m: From Dharma [was born] Yudhiṣṭhira to Pāṇḍu; from Vāyu, Vṛkodara in Kuntī; / from Indra, Dhanañjaya; [and] in Mādrī, Nakula and Sahadeva.

274.s:
vasudevācca rohiṇyāṃ rāmaḥ sāraṇadurgamau /
vasudevācca devakyāmādau jātaḥ susenakaḥ //
274.d:
वसुदेवाच्च रोहिण्यां रामः सारणदुर्गमौ /
वसुदेवाच्च देवक्यामादौ जातः सुसेनकः //
274.m: From Vasudeva in Rohiṇī were born Rāma, Sāraṇa, and Durgama. / And from Vasudeva in Devakī was first born Susena,

274.s:
kīrtimān bhadrasenaś ca jārukhyo viṣṇudāsakaḥ /
bhadradehaḥ kaṃśa etān ṣaḍgarbhānnijaghāna ha //
274.d:
कीर्तिमान् भद्रसेनश् च जारुख्यो विष्णुदासकः /
भद्रदेहः कंश एतान् षड्गर्भान्निजघान ह //
274.m: Kīrtimat, Bhadrasena, the one named Jāru, Viṣṇudāsa, / [and] Bhadradeha. Kaṃsa indeed killed these six embryos.

274.s:
tato balastataḥ kṛṣṇaḥ subhadrā bhadrabhāṣiṇī /
cārudeṣṇaś ca śāmbādyāḥ kṛṣṇājjāmbavatīsutāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe yaduvaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāma
catuḥsaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha pañcasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
dvādaśasaṅgrāmāḥ
274.d:
ततो बलस्ततः कृष्णः सुभद्रा भद्रभाषिणी /
चारुदेष्णश् च शाम्बाद्याः कृष्णाज्जाम्बवतीसुताः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे यदुवंशवर्णनं नाम
चतुःसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ पञ्चसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
द्वादशसङ्ग्रामाः
274.m:
Then [was born] Bala; then Kṛṣṇa; [and] Subhadrā of auspicious speech. / Cārudeṣṇa, Śāmba, and others were the sons of Kṛṣṇa from Jāmbavatī.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-fourth chapter, entitled 'The Description of the Lineage of Yadu', in the Mahāpurāṇa called Āgneya.
Now, the two hundred and seventy-fifth chapter.
The Twelve Battles

275.s:
agnir uvāca
kaśyapo vasudevo 'bhūddevakī cāditirvarā /
devakyāṃ vasudevāttu kṛṣṇo 'bhūttapasānvitaḥ //
275.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
कश्यपो वसुदेवो ऽभूद्देवकी चादितिर्वरा /
देवक्यां वसुदेवात्तु कृष्णो ऽभूत्तपसान्वितः //
275.m: Agni said: / Kaśyapa became Vasudeva, and Devakī was the excellent Aditi. / From Vasudeva in Devakī was born Kṛṣṇa, endowed with ascetic austerity,

275.s:
dharmasaṃrakṣaṇārthāya hy adharmaharaṇāya ca /
surādeḥ pālanārthañca daityādermathanāya ca //
275.d:
धर्मसंरक्षणार्थाय ह्य् अधर्महरणाय च /
सुरादेः पालनार्थञ्च दैत्यादेर्मथनाय च //
275.m: for the protection of righteousness and the removal of unrighteousness, / for the guarding of the gods and others, and for the destruction of the Daityas and others.

275.s:
rukmaṇī satyabhāmā ca satyā nagnajitī priyā /
satyabhāmā hareḥ sevyā gāndhārī lakṣmaṇā tathā //
275.d:
रुक्मणी सत्यभामा च सत्या नग्नजिती प्रिया /
सत्यभामा हरेः सेव्या गान्धारी लक्ष्मणा तथा //
275.m: Rukmiṇī, Satyabhāmā, Satyā the daughter of Nagnajit, his beloved, / Satyabhāmā who was worthy of Hari's service, Gāndhārī, and Lakṣmaṇā,

275.s:
mitravindā(1) ca kālindī devī jāmbavatī tathā /
suśīlā ca tathā mādrī kauśalyā vijayā jayā //
:n
1 citravindeti kha.. , cha.. ca
:p 19
275.d:
मित्रविन्दा(1) च कालिन्दी देवी जाम्बवती तथा /
सुशीला च तथा माद्री कौशल्या विजया जया //
:न्
1 चित्रविन्देति ख.. , छ.. च
:प् 19
275.m:
Mitravindā, Kālindī, Queen Jāmbavatī, / Suśīlā, Mādrī, Kauśalyā, Vijayā, and Jayā—
[Footnote]
1 'Citravindā' in manuscripts kha and cha.

275.s:
evamādīni devīnāṃ sahasrāṇi tu ṣoḍaśa /
pradyumnādyāś ca rukmiṇyāṃ bhīmādyāḥ satyabhāmayā //
275.d:
एवमादीनि देवीनां सहस्राणि तु षोडश /
प्रद्युम्नाद्याश् च रुक्मिण्यां भीमाद्याः सत्यभामया //
275.m: these and others were the sixteen thousand queens. / Pradyumna and others were born of Rukmiṇī; Bhīma and others of Satyabhāmā;

275.s:
jāmbavatyāñca śāmbādyāḥ kṛṣṇasyāsaṃs tathāpare /
śataṃ śatasahasrāṇāṃ putrāṇāṃ tasya dhīmataḥ //
275.d:
जाम्बवत्याञ्च शाम्बाद्याः कृष्णस्यासंस् तथापरे /
शतं शतसहस्राणां पुत्राणां तस्य धीमतः //
275.m: and Śāmba and others of Jāmbavatī. Such were the sons of Kṛṣṇa and others. / One hundred times one hundred thousand were the sons of that wise one,

275.s:
aśītiś ca sahasrāṇi yādavāḥ kṛṣṇarakṣitāḥ /
pradyumnasya tu vaidarbhyāmaniruddho raṇapriyaḥ //
275.d:
अशीतिश् च सहस्राणि यादवाः कृष्णरक्षिताः /
प्रद्युम्नस्य तु वैदर्भ्यामनिरुद्धो रणप्रियः //
275.m: and eighty thousand Yādavas were protected by Kṛṣṇa. / To Pradyumna from the Vaidarbha princess was born Aniruddha, who loved battle.

275.s:
aniruddhasya vajrādyā yādavāḥ sumahābalāḥ /
tisraḥ koṭyo yādavānāṃ ṣaṣṭirlakṣāṇi dānavāḥ //
275.d:
अनिरुद्धस्य वज्राद्या यादवाः सुमहाबलाः /
तिस्रः कोट्यो यादवानां षष्टिर्लक्षाणि दानवाः //
275.m: Of Aniruddha were born Vajra and other exceedingly mighty Yādavas. / Thirty million were the Yādavas, and sixty hundred thousand were the Dānavas.

275.s:
manuṣye bādhakā ye tu tannāśāya babhūva saḥ /
kartuṃ karmavyavasthānaṃ manuṣyo jāyate hariḥ //
275.d:
मनुष्ये बाधका ये तु तन्नाशाय बभूव सः /
कर्तुं कर्मव्यवस्थानं मनुष्यो जायते हरिः //
275.m: For the destruction of those who caused harm to mankind, he came to be. / In order to establish the order of karma, Hari is born as a man.

275.s:
devāsurāṇāṃ saṅgrāmā dāyārthaṃ dvādaśābhavan /
prathamo nārasiṃhastu dvitīyo vāmano raṇaḥ //
275.d:
देवासुराणां सङ्ग्रामा दायार्थं द्वादशाभवन् /
प्रथमो नारसिंहस्तु द्वितीयो वामनो रणः //
275.m: Twelve were the battles between the gods and asuras over their heritage: / the first was the Nārasiṃha [battle], and the second was the Vāmana conflict;

275.s:
saṅgrāmastvatha vārāhaś caturtho 'mṛtamanthanaḥ /
tārakāmayasaṅgrāmaḥ ṣaṣṭho hy ājīvako raṇaḥ //
275.d:
सङ्ग्रामस्त्वथ वाराहश् चतुर्थो ऽमृतमन्थनः /
तारकामयसङ्ग्रामः षष्ठो ह्य् आजीवको रणः //
275.m: the [third] battle was the Vārāha, the fourth was the Churning for Nectar, / the [fifth] was the Tārakāmaya battle, and the sixth was the conflict named Ājīvaka;

275.s:
traipuraścāndhakabadho navamo vṛtraghātakaḥ /
jito hālāhalaścātha ghoraḥ kolāhalo raṇaḥ //
275.d:
त्रैपुरश्चान्धकबधो नवमो वृत्रघातकः /
जितो हालाहलश्चाथ घोरः कोलाहलो रणः //
275.m: the Traipura, the Slaying of Andhaka, the ninth was the Slaying of Vṛtra, / then Hālāhala was conquered, and the dreadful battle called Kolāhala.

275.s:
hiraṇyakaśipoścoro vidārya ca nakhaiḥ purā /
nārasiṃho devapālaḥ prahnādaṃ kṛtavān nṛpam //
275.d:
हिरण्यकशिपोश्चोरो विदार्य च नखैः पुरा /
नारसिंहो देवपालः प्रह्नादं कृतवान् नृपम् //
275.m: Formerly, having torn open the chest of Hiraṇyakaśipu with his claws, / Nārasiṃha, the protector of the gods, made Prahlāda king.

275.s:
devāsure vāmanaś ca chalitvā balimūrjitam /
mahendrāya dadau rājyaṃ kāśyapo 'ditisambhavaḥ //
275.d:
देवासुरे वामनश् च छलित्वा बलिमूर्जितम् /
महेन्द्राय ददौ राज्यं काश्यपो ऽदितिसम्भवः //
275.m: In the battle of the gods and asuras, Vāmana, having deceived the mighty Bali, / gave sovereignty to Mahendra, being Kaśyapa's son born of Aditi.

275.s:
varāhastu hiraṇyākṣaṃ hatvā devānapālayat /
ujjahāra bhuvaṃ devadevair abhiṣṭutaḥ //
275.d:
वराहस्तु हिरण्याक्षं हत्वा देवानपालयत् /
उज्जहार भुवं देवदेवैर् अभिष्टुतः //
275.m: Varāha, having slain Hiraṇyākṣa, protected the gods; / praised by the foremost of the gods, he lifted up the earth.

275.s:
manthānaṃ mandaraṃ kṛtvā netraṃ kṛtvā tu vāsukim /
:p 20
surāsuraiś ca mathitaṃ(1) devebhyaścāmṛtaṃ dadau //
275.d:
मन्थानं मन्दरं कृत्वा नेत्रं कृत्वा तु वासुकिम् /
:प् 20
सुरासुरैश् च मथितं(1) देवेभ्यश्चामृतं ददौ //
275.m:
Having made Mandara the churning rod and Vāsuki the churning rope,
[Page 20]
it was churned by the gods and asuras, and he gave the nectar to the gods.

275.s:
tārakāmayasaṅgrāme tadā devāś ca pālitāḥ /
nivāryendraṃ gurūn devān dānavānsomavaṃśakṛtam //
275.d:
तारकामयसङ्ग्रामे तदा देवाश् च पालिताः /
निवार्येन्द्रं गुरून् देवान् दानवान्सोमवंशकृतम् //
275.m: In the Tārakāmaya battle, the gods were then protected; / having held back Indra, the preceptors, the gods, and the Dānavas, [he established] the progenitor of the Lunar Dynasty.

275.s:
viśvāmitravaśiṣṭhātrikavayaś ca raṇe surān /
apālayante nirvārya rāgadveṣādidānavān //
275.d:
विश्वामित्रवशिष्ठात्रिकवयश् च रणे सुरान् /
अपालयन्ते निर्वार्य रागद्वेषादिदानवान् //
275.m: Viśvāmitra, Vasiṣṭha, Atri, and Kavya in battle / protected the gods, warding off the Dānavas such as passion and hatred.

275.s:
pṛthvīrathe brahmayanturīśasya śaraṇo hariḥ /
dadāha tripuraṃ devapālako daityamardanaḥ //
275.d:
पृथ्वीरथे ब्रह्मयन्तुरीशस्य शरणो हरिः /
ददाह त्रिपुरं देवपालको दैत्यमर्दनः //
275.m: With the earth as the chariot and Brahmā as the charioteer, Hari became the arrow of the Lord / and burned Tripura, [as] the protector of the gods and crusher of the Daityas.

275.s:
gaurīṃ jihīrṣuṇā rudramandhakenārditaṃ hariḥ /
anuraktaś ca revatyāṃ cakrecāndhāsurārdanam //
275.d:
गौरीं जिहीर्षुणा रुद्रमन्धकेनार्दितं हरिः /
अनुरक्तश् च रेवत्यां चक्रेचान्धासुरार्दनम् //
275.m: When Rudra was troubled by Andhaka who sought to abduct Gaurī, Hari, / attached to Revatī, brought about the destruction of the asura Andhaka.

275.s:
apāṃ phenamayo bhūtvā devāsuraraṇe haran(2) /
vṛtraṃ devaharaṃ viṣṇurdevadharmānapālayat //
275.d:
अपां फेनमयो भूत्वा देवासुररणे हरन्(2) /
वृत्रं देवहरं विष्णुर्देवधर्मानपालयत् //
275.m: Becoming the foam of the waters in the battle between the gods and asuras, / destroying Vṛtra, the destroyer of the gods, Viṣṇu preserved the religious duties of the gods.

275.s:
śālvādīn dānavān jitvā hariḥ paraśurāmakaḥ /
apālayat surādīṃś ca duṣṭakṣatraṃ nihatya ca //
275.d:
शाल्वादीन् दानवान् जित्वा हरिः परशुरामकः /
अपालयत् सुरादींश् च दुष्टक्षत्रं निहत्य च //
275.m: Having conquered Śālva and other Dānavas, Hari as Paraśurāma / protected the gods and others, having slain the wicked Kṣatriyas.

275.s:
hālāhalaṃ viṣaṃ daityaṃ nirākṛtya maheśvarāt /
bhayaṃ nirṇāśayāmāsa devānāṃ madhusūdanaḥ //
275.d:
हालाहलं विषं दैत्यं निराकृत्य महेश्वरात् /
भयं निर्णाशयामास देवानां मधुसूदनः //
275.m: Having dispelled the Daitya Hālāhala, the poison, Madhusūdana / destroyed the fear of the gods from the great lord [Śiva].

275.s:
devāsure raṇe yaś ca daityaḥ kolāhalo jitaḥ /
pālitāś ca surāḥ sarve viṣṇunā dharmapālanāt //
275.d:
देवासुरे रणे यश् च दैत्यः कोलाहलो जितः /
पालिताश् च सुराः सर्वे विष्णुना धर्मपालनात् //
275.m: And in the battle of the gods and asuras, the Daitya Kolāhala was conquered; / and all the gods were protected by Viṣṇu through the preservation of righteousness.

275.s:
rājāno rājaputrāś ca munayo devatā hariḥ /
yaduktaṃ yacca naivoktamavatārā harerime //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe dvādaśasaṅgrāmā nāma
pañcasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 surāsurair amanthābdhimiti ka.. , cha.. ca..
2 devāsuraharo 'bhavaditi ka.. , gha.. , ña.. , ṭa.. ca..
:p 21
:ś atha ṣaṭsaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
rājavaṃśavarṇanaṃ
275.d:
राजानो राजपुत्राश् च मुनयो देवता हरिः /
यदुक्तं यच्च नैवोक्तमवतारा हरेरिमे //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे द्वादशसङ्ग्रामा नाम
पञ्चसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 सुरासुरैर् अमन्थाब्धिमिति क.. , छ.. च..
2 देवासुरहरो ऽभवदिति क.. , घ.. , ञ.. , ट.. च..
:प् 21
:श् अथ षट्सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
राजवंशवर्णनं
275.m:
Kings, princes, sages, and deities are Hari; / whatever has been spoken of and whatever has not been spoken of—these are the incarnations of Hari.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-fifth chapter, entitled 'The Twelve Battles', in the Mahāpurāṇa called Āgneya.
[Footnote]
1 'Surāsurair amanthābdhim' in manuscripts ka and cha.
2 'Devāsuraharo 'bhavat' in manuscripts ka, gha, ña, and ṭa.
Now, the two hundred and seventy-sixth chapter.
The Description of the Royal Dynasties

276.s:
agnir uvāca
turvasoś ca suto vargo gobhānustasya cātmajaḥ(1) /
gobhānorāsīt(2) traiśānistraiśānestu karandhamaḥ //
276.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
तुर्वसोश् च सुतो वर्गो गोभानुस्तस्य चात्मजः(1) /
गोभानोरासीत्(2) त्रैशानिस्त्रैशानेस्तु करन्धमः //
276.m: Agni said: / Turvasu's son was Varga, and Gobhānu was his son. / From Gobhānu came Traiśāni, and from Traiśāni came Karandhama.

276.s:
karandhamānmaruttobhūd duṣmantastasya cātmajaḥ /
duṣmantasya varūtho 'bhūdgāṇḍīrastu varūthataḥ //
276.d:
करन्धमान्मरुत्तोभूद् दुष्मन्तस्तस्य चात्मजः /
दुष्मन्तस्य वरूथो ऽभूद्गाण्डीरस्तु वरूथतः //
276.m: From Karandhama arose Marutta, and Duṣmanta was his son. / From Duṣmanta arose Varūtha, and Gāṇḍīra from Varūtha.

276.s:
gāṇḍīrāccaiva gāndhāraḥ pañca jānapadāstataḥ /
gāndhārāḥ keralāścolāḥ pāṇḍyāḥ kolā(3) mahābalāḥ //
276.d:
गाण्डीराच्चैव गान्धारः पञ्च जानपदास्ततः /
गान्धाराः केरलाश्चोलाः पाण्ड्याः कोला(3) महाबलाः //
276.m: And from Gāṇḍīra came Gāndhāra; from him arose five peoples: / the Gāndhāras, Keralas, Colas, Pāṇḍyas, and the mighty Kolas.

276.s:
druhyastu vabhrusetuś ca babhrusetoḥ purovasuḥ /
tato gāndhārā gāndhārair dharmo dharmād ghṛto 'bhavat //
276.d:
द्रुह्यस्तु वभ्रुसेतुश् च बभ्रुसेतोः पुरोवसुः /
ततो गान्धारा गान्धारैर् धर्मो धर्माद् घृतो ऽभवत् //
276.m: Druhyu's [son] was Babhrusetu, and from Babhrusetu came Purovasu; / from him came the Gāndhāras. From Gāndhāra came Dharma, and from Dharma, Ghṛta.

276.s:
ghṛtāttu viduṣastasmāt pracetāstasya vai śatam /
ānadraś ca sabhānaraścākṣuṣaḥ parameṣukaḥ //
276.d:
घृतात्तु विदुषस्तस्मात् प्रचेतास्तस्य वै शतम् /
आनद्रश् च सभानरश्चाक्षुषः परमेषुकः //
276.m: From Ghṛta came Viduṣ; from him Pracetas, who indeed had a hundred [sons]: / Ānadrā, Sabhānara, Cākṣuṣa, and Parameṣuka.

276.s:
sabhānarāt kālānalaḥ kālānalajasrṛñjayaḥ /
purañjayaḥ sṛñjayasya tatputro janamejayaḥ //
276.d:
सभानरात् कालानलः कालानलजस्रृञ्जयः /
पुरञ्जयः सृञ्जयस्य तत्पुत्रो जनमेजयः //
276.m: From Sabhānara came Kālānala; Sṛñjaya was born of Kālānala. / Purañjaya was the son of Sṛñjaya, and his son was Janamejaya.

276.d:
तत्पुत्रस्तु महाशालस्तत्पुत्रो ऽभुन्महामनाः /
तस्मादुशीनरो ब्रह्मन्नृगायान्तु नृगस्ततः //
276.m: His son was Mahāśāla; his son was Mahāmanas. / From him came Uśīnara, O Brahmin; and then Nṛga upon Nṛgā.

276.s:
narāyāntu naraścāsīt kṛmistu kṛmitaḥ sutaḥ /
:n
1 śobhānustasya cātmaja iti kha ..
2 śobhānorāsīditi kha ..
3 karṇā iti ja.. , ṭa.. ca ..
:p 22
daśāyāṃ subrato jajñe dṛśadvatyāṃ śivis tathā //
276.d:
नरायान्तु नरश्चासीत् कृमिस्तु कृमितः सुतः /
:न्
1 शोभानुस्तस्य चात्मज इति ख ..
2 शोभानोरासीदिति ख ..
3 कर्णा इति ज.. , ट.. च ..
:प् 22
दशायां सुब्रतो जज्ञे दृशद्वत्यां शिविस् तथा //
276.m:
Upon Narā was Nara, and Kṛmi was the son born of Kṛmī.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "Śobhānu was his son" in manuscript kha.
[Variant reading:] "From Śobhānu arose" in manuscript kha.
[Variant reading:] "Karṇas" in manuscripts ja and ṭa.
Subrata was born upon Daśā, and likewise Śivi upon Dṛṣadvatī.

276.s:
śive putrāstu catvāraḥ pṛthudarbhaś ca vīrakaḥ /
kaikeyo bhadrakasteṣāṃ nāmrā janapadāḥ śubhāḥ //
276.d:
शिवे पुत्रास्तु चत्वारः पृथुदर्भश् च वीरकः /
कैकेयो भद्रकस्तेषां नाम्रा जनपदाः शुभाः //
276.m: Śivi had four sons: Pṛthudarbha, Vīraka, / Kaikeya, and Bhadraka; auspicious realms bear their names.

276.s:
titikṣuruśīnarajastitikṣoś ca ruṣadrathaḥ /
ruṣadrathādabhūtpailaḥ pailācca sutapāḥ sutaḥ //
276.d:
तितिक्षुरुशीनरजस्तितिक्षोश् च रुषद्रथः /
रुषद्रथादभूत्पैलः पैलाच्च सुतपाः सुतः //
276.m: Titikṣu was born of Uśīnara, and from Titikṣu came Ruṣadratha. / From Ruṣadratha arose Paila, and from Paila his son Sutapas.

276.s:
mahāyogi balistasmādaṅgo vaṅgaś ca mukhyakaḥ /
puṇḍraḥ kaliṅgo bāleyo baliryogī balānvitaḥ //
276.d:
महायोगि बलिस्तस्मादङ्गो वङ्गश् च मुख्यकः /
पुण्ड्रः कलिङ्गो बालेयो बलिर्योगी बलान्वितः //
276.m: From him came the great yogi Bali. The chief [sons] were Aṅga and Vaṅga, / Puṇḍra, Kaliṅga, and Bāleya; Bali was a yogi endowed with might.

276.s:
aṅgāddadhivāhano 'bhūt(1) tasmāddiviratho nṛpaḥ /
divirathāddharmarathastasya citrarathaḥ sutaḥ //
276.d:
अङ्गाद्दधिवाहनो ऽभूत्(1) तस्माद्दिविरथो नृपः /
दिविरथाद्धर्मरथस्तस्य चित्ररथः सुतः //
276.m: From Aṅga arose Dadhivāhana; from him King Diviratha. / From Diviratha came Dharmaratha; his son was Citraratha.

276.s:
citrarathātsatyaratho lomapadaś ca tatsutaḥ /
lomapādāccaturaṅgaḥ pṛthulākṣaś ca tatsutaḥ //
276.d:
चित्ररथात्सत्यरथो लोमपदश् च तत्सुतः /
लोमपादाच्चतुरङ्गः पृथुलाक्षश् च तत्सुतः //
276.m: From Citraratha came Satyaratha, and Lomapāda was his son. / From Lomapāda came Caturaṅga, and Pṛthulākṣa was his son.

276.s:
pṛthulākṣācca campo 'bhūccampāddharyaṅgako 'bhavat /
haryaṅgācca bhadraratho bṛhatkarmā ca tatsutaḥ //
276.d:
पृथुलाक्षाच्च चम्पो ऽभूच्चम्पाद्धर्यङ्गको ऽभवत् /
हर्यङ्गाच्च भद्ररथो बृहत्कर्मा च तत्सुतः //
276.m: From Pṛthulākṣa arose Campa; from Campa arose Haryaṅgaka. / From Haryaṅga came Bhadraratha, and his son was Bṛhatkarman.
From him arose Bṛhadbhānu; from Bṛhadbhānu, Bṛhātmavat. / From him indeed was Jayadratha; from Jayadratha, Bṛhadratha.

276.s:
vṛhadrathādviśvajicca karṇo viśvajito 'bhavat /
karṇasya vṛṣasenastu pṛthusenastadātmajaḥ /
eto 'ṅgavaṃśajā bhūpāḥ pūrorvaṃśaṃ vibodha me //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe rājavaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāma
ṣaṭsaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
1 dadhivāmanobhūditi kha.. , cha.. , ña.. , ca..
:p 23
:ś atha saptasapratyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
puruvaṃśavarṇanaṃ
276.d:
वृहद्रथाद्विश्वजिच्च कर्णो विश्वजितो ऽभवत् /
कर्णस्य वृषसेनस्तु पृथुसेनस्तदात्मजः /
एतो ऽङ्गवंशजा भूपाः पूरोर्वंशं विबोध मे //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे राजवंशवर्णनं नाम
षट्सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
1 दधिवामनोभूदिति ख.. , छ.. , ञ.. , च..
:प् 23
:श् अथ सप्तसप्रत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
पुरुवंशवर्णनं
276.m:
From Bṛhadratha came Viśvajit, and Karṇa was born of Viśvajit. / Karṇa's [son] was Vṛṣasena, and Pṛthusena was his son. / These kings were born in the lineage of Aṅga; learn now from me the lineage of Pūru.
Thus ends the two hundred seventy-sixth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, entitled 'Description of the Royal Dynasties.'
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "Dadhivāmana arose" in manuscripts kha, cha, ña, and ca.
Now, the two hundred seventy-seventh chapter.
Description of the Lineage of Pūru

277.s:
agnir uvāca
purorjanamejayo 'bhūtprācīnnantastu tatsutaḥ /
prācīnnantānmanastyustu tasmādvītamayo nṛpaḥ //
277.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
पुरोर्जनमेजयो ऽभूत्प्राचीन्नन्तस्तु तत्सुतः /
प्राचीन्नन्तान्मनस्त्युस्तु तस्माद्वीतमयो नृपः //
277.m: Agni said: / From Pūru arose Janamejaya, and Prācīnvat was his son. / From Prācīnvat came Manasyu; from him King Vītamaya.

277.s:
śundhurvītamayāccābhūcchundhorbahuvidhaḥ(1) sutaḥ /
bahuvidhācca saṃyātirahovādī ca tatsutaḥ //
277.d:
शुन्धुर्वीतमयाच्चाभूच्छुन्धोर्बहुविधः(1) सुतः /
बहुविधाच्च संयातिरहोवादी च तत्सुतः //
277.m: Śundhu arose from Vītamaya; Bahuvidha was the son of Śundhu. / From Bahuvidha came Saṃyāti, and Rahovādin was his son.

277.s:
tasya putro 'tha bhadrāśoa bhadrāśvasya daśātmajāḥ /
ṛceyuś ca kṛṣeyuś ca sannateyus tathātmajaḥ //
277.d:
तस्य पुत्रो ऽथ भद्राशोअ भद्राश्वस्य दशात्मजाः /
ऋचेयुश् च कृषेयुश् च सन्नतेयुस् तथात्मजः //
277.m: His son then was Bhadrāśva; Bhadrāśva had ten sons: / Ṛceyu, Kṛṣeyu, and likewise his son Sannateyu,

277.s:
ghṛteyuś ca citeyuś ca sthaṇḍileyuś ca sattamaḥ /
dharmeyuḥ sannateyuś ca kṛceyurmatinārakaḥ //
277.d:
घृतेयुश् च चितेयुश् च स्थण्डिलेयुश् च सत्तमः /
धर्मेयुः सन्नतेयुश् च कृचेयुर्मतिनारकः //
277.m: Ghṛteyu, Citeyu, and Sthaṇḍileyu the most excellent, / Dharmeyu, Sannateyu, Kṛceyu, and Matināra.

277.s:
taṃsuroghaḥ pratirathaḥ purasto matinārajāḥ /
āsītpatirathātkaṇvaḥ kaṇvānmedhātithistvabhūt //
277.d:
तंसुरोघः प्रतिरथः पुरस्तो मतिनारजाः /
आसीत्पतिरथात्कण्वः कण्वान्मेधातिथिस्त्वभूत् //
277.m: Taṃsurogha, Pratiratha, and Purasta were born of Matināra. / From Pratiratha was Kaṇva, and from Kaṇva arose Medhātithi.

277.s:
taṃsuroghācca catvāro duṣmanto 'tha pravīrakaḥ /
sumantaścānayo vīro duṣmantādbharato 'bhavat //
277.d:
तंसुरोघाच्च चत्वारो दुष्मन्तो ऽथ प्रवीरकः /
सुमन्तश्चानयो वीरो दुष्मन्ताद्भरतो ऽभवत् //
277.m: From Taṃsurogha came four: Duṣmanta, then Pravīraka, / Sumanta, and Anaya the hero. From Duṣmanta arose Bharata

277.s:
śakuntalāyāntu balī yasya nāmnā tu bhāratāḥ /
suteṣu mātṛkopena naṣṭeṣu bharatasya ca //
277.d:
शकुन्तलायान्तु बली यस्य नाम्ना तु भारताः /
सुतेषु मातृकोपेन नष्टेषु भरतस्य च //
277.m: upon Śakuntalā, mighty, after whose name the Bhāratas are called. / And when the sons of Bharata were lost through their mother's wrath,

277.s:
tato marudbhirānīya putraḥ sa tu vṛhaspateḥ /
saṃkrāmito bharadvājaḥ kratubhirvitatho 'bhavat //
277.d:
ततो मरुद्भिरानीय पुत्रः स तु वृहस्पतेः /
संक्रामितो भरद्वाजः क्रतुभिर्वितथो ऽभवत् //
277.m: then that son of Bṛhaspati, Bharadvāja, having been brought by the Maruts / and transferred [to him], became Vitatha through sacrifices.

277.s:
sa cāpi vitathaḥ putrān janayāmāsa pañca vai /
:n
1 śagbhurvītamayāścābhūcchambhorbahuvidha iti kha.. , ja.. , ca..
:p 24
suhotrañca suhotāraṅgayaṅgarbhantathaiva ca //
277.d:
स चापि वितथः पुत्रान् जनयामास पञ्च वै /
:न्
1 शग्भुर्वीतमयाश्चाभूच्छम्भोर्बहुविध इति ख.. , ज.. , च..
:प् 24
सुहोत्रञ्च सुहोतारङ्गयङ्गर्भन्तथैव च //
277.m:
And he, Vitatha, fathered five sons indeed:
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "Śaṅbhu arose from Vītamaya; Bahuvidha was Śambhu's [son]" in manuscripts kha, ja, and ca.
Suhotra, Suhotṛ, Gaya, and likewise Garbha,

277.s:
kapilaś ca mahātmānaṃ suketuñca sutadvayam /
kauśikañca gṛtsapatiṃ tathā gṛtsapateḥ sutāḥ //
277.d:
कपिलश् च महात्मानं सुकेतुञ्च सुतद्वयम् /
कौशिकञ्च गृत्सपतिं तथा गृत्सपतेः सुताः //
277.m: Kapila, and the two sons the noble [one] and Suketu, / and Kauśika, and Gṛtsapati; and the sons of Gṛtsapati

277.s:
brahmāṇāḥ kṣatriyā vaiśyāḥ kāśe dīrghatamāḥ(1)sutāḥ /
tato dhanvantariścāsīttatsuto 'bhūcca ketumān //
277.d:
ब्रह्माणाः क्षत्रिया वैश्याः काशे दीर्घतमाः(1)सुताः /
ततो धन्वन्तरिश्चासीत्तत्सुतो ऽभूच्च केतुमान् //
277.m: were Brahmins, Kṣatriyas, and Vaiśyas. In Kāśi were the sons of Dīrghatamas; / then arose Dhanvantari, and Ketumat was his son.

277.s:
ketumato hemaratho divodāsa itiśrutaḥ /
pratardano divodāsādbhargavatsau pratardanāt //
277.d:
केतुमतो हेमरथो दिवोदास इतिश्रुतः /
प्रतर्दनो दिवोदासाद्भर्गवत्सौ प्रतर्दनात् //
277.m: Hemaratha was the son of Ketumat; he is famed as Divodāsa. / From Divodāsa came Pratardana; Bharga and Vatsa were from Pratardana.

277.s:
vatsādanarka āsīcca anarkāt kṣemako 'bhavat /
kṣemakadvarṣaketuś ca varṣaketorvibhuḥ smṛtaḥ(2) //
277.d:
वत्सादनर्क आसीच्च अनर्कात् क्षेमको ऽभवत् /
क्षेमकद्वर्षकेतुश् च वर्षकेतोर्विभुः स्मृतः(2) //
277.m: From Vatsa was Anarka, and from Anarka arose Kṣemaka. / From Kṣemaka came Varṣaketu, and from Varṣaketu, Vibhu is remembered.

277.s:
vibhorānartaḥ putro 'bhūdvibhoś ca sukumārakaḥ /
sukumārātsatyaketurvatsabhūmistu vatsakāt //
277.d:
विभोरानर्तः पुत्रो ऽभूद्विभोश् च सुकुमारकः /
सुकुमारात्सत्यकेतुर्वत्सभूमिस्तु वत्सकात् //
277.m: Anarta was the son of Vibhu, and also Sukumāraka from Vibhu. / From Sukumāra came Satyaketu, and Vatsabhūmi from Vatsaka.

277.s:
suhotrasya vṛhatputro vṛhatastanayāstrayaḥ /
ajamīḍho dvimīḍhaś ca purumīḍhaś ca vīryavān //
277.d:
सुहोत्रस्य वृहत्पुत्रो वृहतस्तनयास्त्रयः /
अजमीढो द्विमीढश् च पुरुमीढश् च वीर्यवान् //
277.m: Suhotra's son was Bṛhat; Bṛhat had three sons: / Ajamīḍha, Dvimīḍha, and Purumīḍha endowed with valor.

277.s:
ajamīḍhasya keśinyāṃ jajñe jahnuḥ pratāpavān(3) /
jahnorabhūdajakāśvo balākāśvastadātmajaḥ //
277.d:
अजमीढस्य केशिन्यां जज्ञे जह्नुः प्रतापवान्(3) /
जह्नोरभूदजकाश्वो बलाकाश्वस्तदात्मजः //
277.m: To Ajamīḍha upon Keśinī was born the radiant Jahnu. / From Jahnu arose Ajakāśva; Balākāśva was his son.

277.s:
valākāśvasya kuśikaḥ kuśikāt gādhirindrakaḥ /
gādheḥ satyavatī kanyā viśvāmitraḥ sūtottamaḥ //
277.d:
वलाकाश्वस्य कुशिकः कुशिकात् गाधिरिन्द्रकः /
गाधेः सत्यवती कन्या विश्वामित्रः सूतोत्तमः //
277.m: Kuśika was the son of Valākāśva; from Kuśika came Gādhi, an Indra [among men]. / Gādhi's daughter was Satyavatī, and Viśvāmitra was his excellent son.

277.s:
devarātaḥ katimukhā viśvāmitrasya te sutāḥ /
śunaḥśepho 'ṣṭakaścānyo hy ajamīḍhāt suto 'bhavat //
277.d:
देवरातः कतिमुखा विश्वामित्रस्य ते सुताः /
शुनःशेफो ऽष्टकश्चान्यो ह्य् अजमीढात् सुतो ऽभवत् //
277.m: Devarāta, those headed by Kati, Śunaḥśepha, / and another, Aṣṭaka, were the sons of Viśvāmitra. From Ajamīḍha another son arose

277.s:
nīlinyāṃ śāntiraparaḥ purujātiḥ suśāntitaḥ /
:n
1 kāśadīrghatamā iti ja..
2 suta iti kha.. , cha.. , ja.. , ca
3 prabhāvavāniti kha..
:p 25
purujātestu vāhyāśvo vāhyāścvāt pañca pārthivāḥ //
277.d:
नीलिन्यां शान्तिरपरः पुरुजातिः सुशान्तितः /
:न्
1 काशदीर्घतमा इति ज..
2 सुत इति ख.. , छ.. , ज.. , च
3 प्रभाववानिति ख..
:प् 25
पुरुजातेस्तु वाह्याश्वो वाह्याश्च्वात् पञ्च पार्थिवाः //
277.m:
upon Nīlinī, Śānti; Purujāti came from Suśānti.
[Footnote]
[Variant reading:] "kāśadīrghatamāḥ" in manuscript ja.
[Variant reading:] "son" in manuscripts kha, cha, ja, and ca.
[Variant reading:] "endowed with power" in manuscript kha.
From Purujāti came Vāhyāśva; from Vāhyāśva came five rulers:

277.s:
mukulaḥ sṛñjayaś caiva rājā vṛhadiṣus tathā /
yavīnaraś ca(1) kṛmilaḥ pāñcālā iti viśrutāḥ //
277.d:
मुकुलः सृञ्जयश् चैव राजा वृहदिषुस् तथा /
यवीनरश् च(1) कृमिलः पाञ्चाला इति विश्रुताः //
277.m: Mukula, Sṛñjaya, King Bṛhadiṣu, / Yavīnara, and Kṛmila; they are renowned as the Pāñcālas.

277.s:
mukulasya tu maukulyāḥ kṣetropetā dvijātayaḥ /
cañcāśvo mukulājjajñe cañcāśvānmithunaṃ hy abhut //
277.d:
मुकुलस्य तु मौकुल्याः क्षेत्रोपेता द्विजातयः /
चञ्चाश्वो मुकुलाज्जज्ञे चञ्चाश्वान्मिथुनं ह्य् अभुत् //
277.m: The descendants of Mukula were the Maukulyas, twice-born endowed with fields. / Cañcāśva was born of Mukula; from Cañcāśva a twin pair arose:

277.s:
divodāso hy ahalyā ca ahalyāyāṃ śaradvatāt /
śatānandaḥ śatānandāt satyadhṛnmithunantataḥ //
277.d:
दिवोदासो ह्य् अहल्या च अहल्यायां शरद्वतात् /
शतानन्दः शतानन्दात् सत्यधृन्मिथुनन्ततः //
277.m: Divodāsa and Ahalyā. Upon Ahalyā from Śaradvat / was born Śatānanda; from Śatānanda, Satyadhṛti; then a twin pair:

277.s:
kṛpaḥ kṛpī kivodāsānmaitreyaḥ somapastataḥ /
sṛñjayāt pañcadhanuṣaḥ somadattaś ca tatsutaḥ //
277.d:
कृपः कृपी किवोदासान्मैत्रेयः सोमपस्ततः /
सृञ्जयात् पञ्चधनुषः सोमदत्तश् च तत्सुतः //
277.m: Kṛpa and Kṛpī. From Divodāsa came Maitreya; then Somapa. / From Sṛñjaya came Pañcadhanuṣ, and Somadatta was his son.

277.s:
sahadevaḥ somadattāt sahadevāttu somakaḥ /
āsīcca somakājjanturjantoś ca pṛṣataḥ sutaḥ //
277.d:
सहदेवः सोमदत्तात् सहदेवात्तु सोमकः /
आसीच्च सोमकाज्जन्तुर्जन्तोश् च पृषतः सुतः //
277.m: Sahadeva came from Somadatta; from Sahadeva came Somaka. / From Somaka was Jantu, and Pṛṣata was Jantu's son.

277.s:
pṛṣatāddrupadastasmāddhṛṣṭadyumno 'tha tatsutaḥ /
dhṛṣṭhaketuś ca dhūminyāmṛkṣo 'bhūdajamīḍhataḥ //
277.d:
पृषताद्द्रुपदस्तस्माद्धृष्टद्युम्नो ऽथ तत्सुतः /
धृष्ठकेतुश् च धूमिन्यामृक्षो ऽभूदजमीढतः //
277.m: From Pṛṣata came Drupada; from him Dhṛṣṭadyumna, and then his son / Dhṛṣṭaketu. Upon Dhūminī arose Ṛkṣa from Ajamīḍha.

277.s:
ṛkṣātsamvaraṇo jajñe kuruḥ samvaraṇāttataḥ /
yaḥ prayāgādapākramya kurukṣetrañcakāra ha //
277.d:
ऋक्षात्सम्वरणो जज्ञे कुरुः सम्वरणात्ततः /
यः प्रयागादपाक्रम्य कुरुक्षेत्रञ्चकार ह //
277.m: From Ṛkṣa was born Saṃvaraṇa, and Kuru then from Saṃvaraṇa, / who, setting out from Prayāga, established Kurukṣetra.

277.s:
kuroḥ sudhanvā sudhanuḥ parikṣiccārimejayaḥ /
sudhanvanaḥ suhotro 'bhūt suhotrāccyavano hy abhūt //
277.d:
कुरोः सुधन्वा सुधनुः परिक्षिच्चारिमेजयः /
सुधन्वनः सुहोत्रो ऽभूत् सुहोत्राच्च्यवनो ह्य् अभूत् //
277.m:
From Kuru sprang Sudhanvan, Sudhanus, Parikṣit, and Arimejaya.
From Sudhanvan was Suhotra, and from Suhotra sprang Cyavana.

277.s:
vaśiṣṭhaparicārābhyāṃ saptāsan girikāsutāḥ /
vṛhadrathaḥ kuśo vīro yaduḥ pratyagraho balaḥ //
277.d:
वशिष्ठपरिचाराभ्यां सप्तासन् गिरिकासुताः /
वृहद्रथः कुशो वीरो यदुः प्रत्यग्रहो बलः //
277.m:
By Vaśiṣṭha and Paricāra, Girikā had seven sons:
Bṛhadratha, Kuśa, the hero Yadu, Pratyagraha, and Bala,

277.s:
matsyakālī kuśāgro 'to hy āsīdrājño vṛhadrathāt /
kuśāgrādvṛṣabho jajñe tasya satyahitaḥ sutaḥ //
277.d:
मत्स्यकाली कुशाग्रो ऽतो ह्य् आसीद्राज्ञो वृहद्रथात् /
कुशाग्राद्वृषभो जज्ञे तस्य सत्यहितः सुतः //
277.m:
Matsyakālī, and Kuśāgra; these came from King Bṛhadratha.
From Kuśāgra was born Vṛṣabha; his son was Satyahita.

277.s:
sudhanvā tatsutaścorja ūrjādāsīcca sambhavaḥ /
:n
1 yavīnacaśceti kha.., cha.. , ña.. , ca
:p 26
sambhavācca jarāsandhaḥ sahadevaś ca tatsutaḥ //
277.d:
सुधन्वा तत्सुतश्चोर्ज ऊर्जादासीच्च सम्भवः /
:न्
1 यवीनचश्चेति ख.., छ.. , ञ.. , च
:प् 26
सम्भवाच्च जरासन्धः सहदेवश् च तत्सुतः //
277.m:
His son was Sudhanvan; then Ūrja; and from Ūrja came Sambhava.
[Note]
1. 'yavīnacaś ca' in manuscripts kha, cha, ña, and ca. / [Page 26]
And from Sambhava came Jarāsandha, and his son was Sahadeva.

277.s:
sahadevādudāpiś ca udāpeḥ śrutakarmakaḥ /
parikṣitasya dāyādo dhārmiko janamejayaḥ //
277.d:
सहदेवादुदापिश् च उदापेः श्रुतकर्मकः /
परिक्षितस्य दायादो धार्मिको जनमेजयः //
277.m:
From Sahadeva was Udāpi, and from Udāpi was Śrutakarmaka.
The righteous Janamejaya was the heir of Parikṣit.

277.s:
janamejayāttrasadasyurjahnostu surathaḥ sutaḥ /
śrutasenograsenau ca bhīmasenaś ca nāmataḥ //
277.d:
जनमेजयात्त्रसदस्युर्जह्नोस्तु सुरथः सुतः /
श्रुतसेनोग्रसेनौ च भीमसेनश् च नामतः //
277.m:
From Janamejaya came Trasadasyu; but of Jahnu, the son was Suratha;
and by name Śrutasena, Ugrasena, and Bhīmasena.

277.s:
janamejayasya putrau tu suratho mahimāṃs tathā /
surathādvidūratho 'bhūdṛkṣa āsīdvidūrathāt //
277.d:
जनमेजयस्य पुत्रौ तु सुरथो महिमांस् तथा /
सुरथाद्विदूरथो ऽभूदृक्ष आसीद्विदूरथात् //
277.m:
The sons of Janamejaya were Suratha and Mahīmant.
From Suratha came Vidūratha; from Vidūratha came Ṛkṣa.

277.s:
ṛkṣasya tu dvitīyasya bhīmaseno 'bhavatsutaḥ /
pratīpo bhīmasenāttu pratīpasya tu śāntanuḥ //
277.d:
ऋक्षस्य तु द्वितीयस्य भीमसेनो ऽभवत्सुतः /
प्रतीपो भीमसेनात्तु प्रतीपस्य तु शान्तनुः //
277.m:
The son of the second Ṛkṣa was Bhīmasena.
From Bhīmasena came Pratīpa; and of Pratīpa was Śāntanu.

277.s:
devāpirvāhlikaś caiva somadattastu śāntanoḥ /
vāhlikātsomadatto 'bhudbhūrirbhūrisravāḥ śalaḥ //
277.d:
देवापिर्वाह्लिकश् चैव सोमदत्तस्तु शान्तनोः /
वाह्लिकात्सोमदत्तो ऽभुद्भूरिर्भूरिस्रवाः शलः //
277.m:
Śāntanu's [brothers] were Devāpi and Bāhlika, and Somadatta [was Bāhlika's son].
From Bāhlika was Somadatta, and [from him] Bhūri, Bhūriśravas, and Śala.

277.s:
gaṅgāyāṃ śāntanorbhīṣmaḥ kālyāyāṃ vicitravīryakaḥ /
kṛṣṇadvaipāyanaś caiva kṣetre vaicitravīryake //
277.d:
गङ्गायां शान्तनोर्भीष्मः काल्यायां विचित्रवीर्यकः /
कृष्णद्वैपायनश् चैव क्षेत्रे वैचित्रवीर्यके //
277.m:
From Śāntanu by Gaṅgā was Bhīṣma; by Kālī was Vicitravīrya;
and Kṛṣṇadvaipāyana, in the wife of Vicitravīrya,

277.s:
dhṛtaraṣṭrañca pāṇḍuñca vidurañcāpyajījanat /
pāṇḍoryudhiṣṭhiraḥ kuntyāṃ bhīmaś caivārjunastrayaḥ //
277.d:
धृतरष्ट्रञ्च पाण्डुञ्च विदुरञ्चाप्यजीजनत् /
पाण्डोर्युधिष्ठिरः कुन्त्यां भीमश् चैवार्जुनस्त्रयः //
277.m:
begot Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Pāṇḍu, and also Vidura.
To Pāṇḍu by Kuntī were three: Yudhiṣṭhira, Bhīma, and Arjuna.

277.s:
nakulaḥ sahadevaś ca pāṇḍormādyrāñca daivataḥ /
arjunasya ca saubhadraḥ parikṣidabhimanyutaḥ //
277.d:
नकुलः सहदेवश् च पाण्डोर्माद्य्राञ्च दैवतः /
अर्जुनस्य च सौभद्रः परिक्षिदभिमन्युतः //
277.m:
Nakula and Sahadeva were Pāṇḍu's by Mādrī through the deities.
Arjuna's son was the son of Subhadrā [Abhimanyu], and Parikṣit was from Abhimanyu.

277.s:
draupadī pāṇḍavānāñca priyā tasyāṃ yudhiṣṭhirāt /
prativindhyo bhīmasenācchrutakīrtirdhanañjayāt(1) //
277.d:
द्रौपदी पाण्डवानाञ्च प्रिया तस्यां युधिष्ठिरात् /
प्रतिविन्ध्यो भीमसेनाच्छ्रुतकीर्तिर्धनञ्जयात्(1) //
277.m:
And Draupadī was the beloved of the Pāṇḍavas; on her, from Yudhiṣṭhira,
was Prativindhya; from Bhīmasena [was Sutasoma]; from Dhanañjaya was Śrutakīrti;

277.s:
sahadevācchrutakarmā śatānīkastu nākuliḥ /
bhīmasenāddhiḍimbāyāmanya āsīd ghaṭītkacaḥ //
277.d:
सहदेवाच्छ्रुतकर्मा शतानीकस्तु नाकुलिः /
भीमसेनाद्धिडिम्बायामन्य आसीद् घटीत्कचः //
277.m:
from Sahadeva was Śrutakarman; and Śatānīka was the son of Nakula.
From Bhīmasena by Hiḍimbā another son was Ghaṭotkaca.

277.s:
ete bhūtā bhaviṣyāś ca nṛpāḥ saṃkhyā na vidyate /
:n
1 atra pāṭhaḥ patitaḥ dhanañjayāt ka utpanna iti
viśeṣāprāpteḥ
:p 27
gatāḥ kālena kālo hi haristaṃ pūjayeddvija //
homamagnausamuddiśya kuru sarvapradaṃ yataḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe puruvaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāma
saptasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athāṣṭasaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
siddhauṣadhāni
277.d:
एते भूता भविष्याश् च नृपाः संख्या न विद्यते /
:न्
1 अत्र पाठः पतितः धनञ्जयात् क उत्पन्न इति
विशेषाप्राप्तेः
:प् 27
गताः कालेन कालो हि हरिस्तं पूजयेद्द्विज //
होममग्नौसमुद्दिश्य कुरु सर्वप्रदं यतः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे पुरुवंशवर्णनं नाम
सप्तसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथाष्टसप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सिद्धौषधानि
277.m:
These kings, past and future, are beyond reckoning.
[Note]
1. Here the text is deficient, as it does not clearly specify who was born from Dhanañjaya. / [Page 27]
They have passed away in time; for Time is Hari. A twice-born should worship him.
Perform a fire oblation aimed into the fire, since it bestows all things.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-seventh chapter, entitled 'Description of the Puru Lineage', in the great Purāṇa of Agni.
Now begins the two hundred and seventy-eighth chapter:
Proven Remedies.

278.s:
agnir uvāca
āyurvedaṃ pravakṣyāmi suśrutāya yamabravīt /
devo dhanvantariḥ sāraṃ mṛtasañjīvanīkaraṃ //
278.d:
अग्निर् उवाच
आयुर्वेदं प्रवक्ष्यामि सुश्रुताय यमब्रवीत् /
देवो धन्वन्तरिः सारं मृतसञ्जीवनीकरं //
278.m:
Agni said:
I shall proclaim the Āyurveda which the divine Dhanvantari
spoke to Suśruta—the essence that revives the dead.

278.s:
suśruta uvāca
āyurvedaṃ mama brūhi narāśvebharugardanam /
siddhayogānsiddhamantrānmṛtasañjīvanīkarān //
278.d:
सुश्रुत उवाच
आयुर्वेदं मम ब्रूहि नराश्वेभरुगर्दनम् /
सिद्धयोगान्सिद्धमन्त्रान्मृतसञ्जीवनीकरान् //
278.m:
Suśruta said:
Tell me the Āyurveda that removes the diseases of men, horses, and elephants,
proven formulations, proven mantras that revive the dead.

278.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
rakṣan balaṃ hi jvaritaṃ laṅghitaṃ bhojayedbhiṣak /
saviśvaṃ lājamaṇḍantu tṛḍjvarāntaṃ śṛtaṃ jalam //
278.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
रक्षन् बलं हि ज्वरितं लङ्घितं भोजयेद्भिषक् /
सविश्वं लाजमण्डन्तु तृड्ज्वरान्तं शृतं जलम् //
278.m:
Dhanvantari said:
Preserving strength, the physician should feed one who has fasted in fever
scum of parched paddy with ginger, and boiled water that ends thirst and fever.

278.s:
mustaparpaṭakośīracandanodīcyanāgaraiḥ /
ṣaḍahe ca vyatikrānte tittakaṃ pāyayeddhruvaṃ //
278.d:
मुस्तपर्पटकोशीरचन्दनोदीच्यनागरैः /
षडहे च व्यतिक्रान्ते तित्तकं पाययेद्ध्रुवं //
278.m:
With nut-grass, parpaṭaka, vetiver, sandalwood, bālā, and dry ginger;
and when six days have passed, he should unfailingly make him drink a bitter [decoction].

278.s:
snehayettaktadoṣantu(1) tatastañca virecayet /
jīrṇāḥ ṣaṣṭikanīvāraraktaśālipramodakāḥ //
278.d:
स्नेहयेत्तक्तदोषन्तु(1) ततस्तञ्च विरेचयेत् /
जीर्णाः षष्टिकनीवाररक्तशालिप्रमोदकाः //
278.m:
He should lubricate one whose humours are mature, and then purge him.
Old ṣaṣṭika, wild rice, red rice, pramodaka,

278.s:
tadvidhāste jvareṣviṣṭā yavānāṃ vikṛtis tathā /
mudgā masūrāś ca ṇakāḥ kulatthāś ca sakuṣṭhakāḥ //
:n
1 pakvadoṣantviti ña..
:p 28
278.d:
तद्विधास्ते ज्वरेष्विष्टा यवानां विकृतिस् तथा /
मुद्गा मसूराश् च णकाः कुलत्थाश् च सकुष्ठकाः //
:न्
1 पक्वदोषन्त्विति ञ..
:प् 28
278.m:
and similar grains are recommended in fevers, as well as barley preparations,
mudga, lentils, chickpeas, and horse gram along with kuṣṭha,
[Note]
1. 'pakvadoṣantv' in manuscript ña. / [Page 28]

278.s:
āṭakyo nārakādyāś ca karkoṭakakatolvakam /
paṭolaṃ saphalaṃ nimbaṃ parpaṭaṃ dāḍimaṃ jvare //
278.d:
आटक्यो नारकाद्याश् च कर्कोटककतोल्वकम् /
पटोलं सफलं निम्बं पर्पटं दाडिमं ज्वरे //
278.m:
pigeon peas, oranges and the like, spine gourd, katphala,
pointed gourd with fruit, neem, parpaṭa, and pomegranate in fever.

278.s:
adhoge vamanaṃ śastamūrdhvage ca virecanam /
raktapitte tathā pānaṃ ṣaḍaṅgaṃ śuṇṭhivarjitam //
278.d:
अधोगे वमनं शस्तमूर्ध्वगे च विरेचनम् /
रक्तपित्ते तथा पानं षडङ्गं शुण्ठिवर्जितम् //
278.m:
In downward hemorrhage, emesis is commended; in upward, purgation;
in internal hemorrhage, the six-fold drink without dry ginger [is commended].

278.s:
śaktugodhūmalājāś ca yavaśālimasūrakāḥ /
sakuṣṭhacaṇakā mudgā bhakṣyā godhūmakā hitāḥ //
278.d:
शक्तुगोधूमलाजाश् च यवशालिमसूरकाः /
सकुष्ठचणका मुद्गा भक्ष्या गोधूमका हिताः //
278.m:
Barley meal, wheat, parched grain, barley, rice, and lentils,
chickpeas with kuṣṭha, mudga, and cooked wheat preparations are wholesome.

278.s:
sādhitā ghṛtadugdhābhyāṃ kṣaudraṃ vṛṣaraso madhu /
atīsāre purāṇānāṃ śālīnāṃ bhakṣaṇaṃ hitaṃ //
278.d:
साधिता घृतदुग्धाभ्यां क्षौद्रं वृषरसो मधु /
अतीसारे पुराणानां शालीनां भक्षणं हितं //
278.m:
Prepared with ghee and milk, small honey, juice of vāsā, and honey.
In diarrhea, the eating of aged rice is wholesome,

278.s:
anabhiṣyandi yaccānnaṃ lodhravalkalasaṃyutam /
mārutaṃ varjayed yatnaḥ kāryo gulmeṣu sarvathā //
278.d:
अनभिष्यन्दि यच्चान्नं लोध्रवल्कलसंयुतम् /
मारुतं वर्जयेद् यत्नः कार्यो गुल्मेषु सर्वथा //
278.m:
and food that does not cause obstruction of channels, combined with lodhra bark.
In phantom tumours, one must avoid wind-generating foods; every effort should be made [to that end].

278.s:
vāṭyaṃ kṣīreṇa cāśnīyādvāstūkaṃ ghṛtasādhitaṃ /
godhūmaśālayastiktā hitā jaṭhariṇāmatha //
278.d:
वाट्यं क्षीरेण चाश्नीयाद्वास्तूकं घृतसाधितं /
गोधूमशालयस्तिक्ता हिता जठरिणामथ //
278.m:
One should eat barley gruel with milk, and goosefoot cooked with ghee.
Wheat and rice dishes, and bitters, are beneficial for patients with abdominal disease.

278.s:
godhūmaśālayo mudgā brahmarkṣakhadiro 'bhayā /
pañcakolañjāṅgalāś ca nimbadhātryaḥ paṭolakāḥ //
278.d:
गोधूमशालयो मुद्गा ब्रह्मर्क्षखदिरो ऽभया /
पञ्चकोलञ्जाङ्गलाश् च निम्बधात्र्यः पटोलकाः //
278.m:
Wheat, rice, mudga, brahmadāru, khadira, chebulic myrobalan,
the five spices, dry-land game meat, neem, āmalakī, pointed gourd,

278.s:
mātulaṅgarasājātiśuṣkamūlakasaindhavāḥ /
kuṣṭhināñca tathā śastaṃ pānārthe khadirodakaṃ //
278.d:
मातुलङ्गरसाजातिशुष्कमूलकसैन्धवाः /
कुष्ठिनाञ्च तथा शस्तं पानार्थे खदिरोदकं //
278.m:
citron juice, jasmine, dried radish, and rock salt;
and for leprosy patients, khadira-infused water is commended for drinking.

278.s:
masūrasudgau peyārthe bhojyā jirṇāś ca śālayaḥ /
nimbaparpaṭakaiḥ śākair jāṅgalānāṃ tathā rasaḥ //
278.d:
मसूरसुद्गौ पेयार्थे भोज्या जिर्णाश् च शालयः /
निम्बपर्पटकैः शाकैर् जाङ्गलानां तथा रसः //
278.m:
Lentils and mudga are for drinks, and aged rice for meals,
with neem and parpaṭaka greens, and meat broth of dry-land animals.

278.s:
viḍaṅgaṃ maricaṃ mustaṃ kuṣṭhaṃ lodhraṃ suvarcikā /
manaḥśilā ca vāleyaḥ kuṣṭhahā mūtrapeṣitaḥ //
278.d:
विडङ्गं मरिचं मुस्तं कुष्ठं लोध्रं सुवर्चिका /
मनःशिला च वालेयः कुष्ठहा मूत्रपेषितः //
278.m:
Viḍaṅga, black pepper, nut-grass, kuṣṭha, lodhra, natron,
realgar, and [donkey] dung, ground with [cow] urine, destroy leprosy.

278.s:
apūpakuṣṭhakulmāṣayavādyā mehināṃ hitāḥ /
yavānnavikṛtirmudgā kulatthā jīrṇaśālayaḥ //
278.d:
अपूपकुष्ठकुल्माषयवाद्या मेहिनां हिताः /
यवान्नविकृतिर्मुद्गा कुलत्था जीर्णशालयः //
278.m:
Cakes, kuṣṭha, steamed barley grains, and the like are beneficial for patients with urinary disorders;
preparations of barley food, mudga, horse gram, and aged rice;

278.s:
tiktarukṣāṇi śākāni tiktāni haritāni ca /
:p 29
tailāni tilaśigrukavibhītakeṅgudāni ca //
278.d:
तिक्तरुक्षाणि शाकानि तिक्तानि हरितानि च /
:प् 29
तैलानि तिलशिग्रुकविभीतकेङ्गुदानि च //

278.s:
mudgāḥ sayavagodhūmā dhānyaṃ varṣasthatañca yat /
jāṅgalasya rasaḥ śasto bhojane rājayakṣmiṇāṃ //
278.d:
मुद्गाः सयवगोधूमा धान्यं वर्षस्थतञ्च यत् /
जाङ्गलस्य रसः शस्तो भोजने राजयक्ष्मिणां //
278.m:
Mudga with barley and wheat, grain that has aged for a year,
and broth of dry-land animals is commended as food for those suffering from consumption.

278.s:
kaulatthamaudgako rāsnāśuṣkamūlakajāṅgalaiḥ /
pūpair vā viskaraiḥ siddhair dadhidāḍimasādhitaiḥ //
278.d:
कौलत्थमौद्गको रास्नाशुष्कमूलकजाङ्गलैः /
पूपैर् वा विस्करैः सिद्धैर् दधिदाडिमसाधितैः //
278.m:
With horse-gram, mudga, rāsnā, dried radish, and dry-land game,
or cakes, or birds that scatter food, prepared with curd and pomegranate,

278.s:
mātulaṅgarasakṣaudradrākṣāvyoṣādisaṃskṛtaiḥ /
yavagodhūmaśālyannair bhojayecchvāsakāsinaṃ //
278.d:
मातुलङ्गरसक्षौद्रद्राक्षाव्योषादिसंस्कृतैः /
यवगोधूमशाल्यन्नैर् भोजयेच्छ्वासकासिनं //
278.m:
seasoned with citron juice, small honey, grapes, the three pungents, and so on,
with food of barley, wheat, and rice, one should feed one who suffers from asthma and cough.

278.s:
daṣamūlavalārāsnākulatthair upasādhitāḥ /
peyāḥ pūparasāḥ kvāthāḥ śvāsahikkānivāraṇāḥ //
278.d:
दषमूलवलारास्नाकुलत्थैर् उपसाधिताः /
पेयाः पूपरसाः क्वाथाः श्वासहिक्कानिवारणाः //
278.m:
Prepared with the ten roots, balā, rāsnā, and horse gram,
drinks, pastry soups, and decoctions dispel asthma and hiccups.

278.s:
śuṣkamūlakakaulatthamūlajāṅgalajairasaiḥ(?) /
yavagodhūmaśālyannaṃ jīrṇam sośīramācaret //
278.d:
शुष्कमूलककौलत्थमूलजाङ्गलजैरसैः(?) /
यवगोधूमशाल्यन्नं जीर्णम् सोशीरमाचरेत् //
278.m:
With broths made from dried radish, horse gram, roots, and dry-land game,
one should consume aged barley, wheat, and rice food, along with vetiver.

278.s:
sothavān saguḍāṃ pathyāṃ khādedvā guḍanāgaram /
takrañca citrakañcobhau grahaṇīroganāśanau //
278.d:
सोथवान् सगुडां पथ्यां खादेद्वा गुडनागरम् /
तक्रञ्च चित्रकञ्चोभौ ग्रहणीरोगनाशनौ //
278.m:
One with edema should eat chebulic myrobalan with molasses, or molasses with dry ginger.
Both buttermilk and plumbago destroy diseases of the duodenum.

278.s:
purāṇayavagodhūmaśālayo jaṅgalo rasaḥ /
mudgāmalakakharjūramṛdvīkāvadarāṇi ca //
278.d:
पुराणयवगोधूमशालयो जङ्गलो रसः /
मुद्गामलकखर्जूरमृद्वीकावदराणि च //
278.m:
Aged barley, wheat, and rice; meat broth of dry-land animals;
mudga, āmalakī, dates, grapes, and jujube fruits;

278.s:
madhu sarpiḥ payaḥ śakraṃ nimbaparpaṭakau vṛṣam /
takrāriṣṭāś ca(1) śasyante satataṃ vātarogiṇām //
278.d:
मधु सर्पिः पयः शक्रं निम्बपर्पटकौ वृषम् /
तक्रारिष्टाश् च(1) शस्यन्ते सततं वातरोगिणाम् //
278.m:
honey, ghee, milk, curd, neem, parpaṭaka, and vāsā,
and fermented buttermilk preparations are constantly commended for patients of wind disorders.

278.s:
hṛdrogiṇo virecyāstu pippalyo hikkināṃ hitāḥ /
takrāvalālasindhūni muktāni śiśirāmbhasā //
278.d:
हृद्रोगिणो विरेच्यास्तु पिप्पल्यो हिक्किनां हिताः /
तक्रावलालसिन्धूनि मुक्तानि शिशिराम्भसा //
278.m:
Those with heart disease must be purged; long pepper is beneficial for those with hiccups;
churned curd with black salt, mixed with cold water,

278.s:
muktāḥ sauvarcalājādi madyaṃ śastaṃ madātyaye(2) /
sakṣaudrapayasā lākṣāṃ pivecca kṣatavānnaraḥ //
:n
1 bhadrāviṣṭāśceti kha..
2 sadāmaye iti ña.. / damātyaye iti ṭa..
:p 30
278.d:
मुक्ताः सौवर्चलाजादि मद्यं शस्तं मदात्यये(2) /
सक्षौद्रपयसा लाक्षां पिवेच्च क्षतवान्नरः //
:न्
1 भद्राविष्टाश्चेति ख..
2 सदामये इति ञ.. / दमात्यये इति ट..
:प् 30
278.m:
pearls, black salt, and roasted grain; wine is commended in alcohol intoxication;
and an injured person should drink lac resin with milk and small honey.
[Note]
1. 'bhadrāviṣṭāś ca' in manuscript kha.
2. In manuscript ña, “sadāmaye”; in manuscript ṭa, “damātyaye”.
[Section] 30

278.s:
kṣayaṃ māṃsarasāhāro vahnisaṃrakṣaṇājjayet /
śālayo bhojane raktā nīvārakalamādayaḥ //
278.d:
क्षयं मांसरसाहारो वह्निसंरक्षणाज्जयेत् /
शालयो भोजने रक्ता नीवारकलमादयः //
278.m:
One should conquer consumption through a diet of meat broth by preserving the digestive fire.
Red rice, wild rice, kalamā rice, and the like are recommended for food;

278.s:
yavānnavikṛtirmāsaṃ śākaṃ sauvarcalaṃ śaṭī /
pathyā tathaivārśasāṃ yanmaṇḍaṃ takrañca vāriṇā(1) //
278.d:
यवान्नविकृतिर्मासं शाकं सौवर्चलं शटी /
पथ्या तथैवार्शसां यन्मण्डं तक्रञ्च वारिणा(1) //
278.m:
preparations of barley, meat, suvarcala greens, and śaṭī,
and likewise for piles, yellow myrobalan, rice scum, and buttermilk with water.

278.s:
mustābhyāsas tathā lepaścitrakeṇa haridrayā /
yavānnavikṛtiḥ śālirvāstūkaṃ sasuvarcalam //
278.d:
मुस्ताभ्यासस् तथा लेपश्चित्रकेण हरिद्रया /
यवान्नविकृतिः शालिर्वास्तूकं ससुवर्चलम् //
278.m:
Constant use of mustā, an ointment with leadwort and turmeric,
preparations of barley, winter rice, and goosefoot with suvarcala [are beneficial].

278.s:
trapuṣarvārugodhūmāḥ kṣīrekṣughṛtasaṃyutāḥ /
mūtrakṛcchre ca śastāḥ syuḥ pāne maṇḍasurādayaḥ //
278.d:
त्रपुषर्वारुगोधूमाः क्षीरेक्षुघृतसंयुताः /
मूत्रकृच्छ्रे च शस्ताः स्युः पाने मण्डसुरादयः //
278.m:
Cucumbers, snake melons, and wheat combined with milk, sugarcane juice, and ghee,
and for dysuria, rice scum, wine, and the like are recommended for drink.

278.s:
lājāḥ śaktus tathā kṣaudraṃ śūnyaṃ māṃsaṃ parūṣakam /
vārtākulāvaśikhinaśchardighnāḥ pānakāni ca //
278.d:
लाजाः शक्तुस् तथा क्षौद्रं शून्यं मांसं परूषकम् /
वार्ताकुलावशिखिनश्छर्दिघ्नाः पानकानि च //
278.m:
Parched grain, barley flour, honey, dried meat, parūṣaka fruit,
eggplants, kulmāṣa grains, quail, partridge, and syrups cure vomiting.

278.s:
śālyannantoyapayasī kevaloṣṇe śṛte 'pi vā /
tṛṣṇāghne mustaguḍayorguṭikā vā mukhe dhṛtā //
278.d:
शाल्यन्नन्तोयपयसी केवलोष्णे शृते ऽपि वा /
तृष्णाघ्ने मुस्तगुडयोर्गुटिका वा मुखे धृता //
278.m:
Boiled winter rice, water and milk drunk hot or boiled,
or a pill of mustā and jaggery held in the mouth, removes thirst.

278.s:
yavānnavikṛtiḥ pūpaṃ(2) śuṣkamūlakajantathā /
śākaṃ paṭolavetrāgramurustambhavināśanam //
278.d:
यवान्नविकृतिः पूपं(2) शुष्कमूलकजन्तथा /
शाकं पटोलवेत्राग्रमुरुस्तम्भविनाशनम् //
278.m:
A preparation of barley, cake, and dried radishes,
and greens of trichosanthes and cane-tips destroy stiffness of the thighs.

278.s:
mudgāḍhakamasūrāṇāṃ satilair jāṅgalairasaiḥ(?) /
sasaindhavaghṛtadrākṣāśuṇṭhyāmalakakolajaiḥ //
278.d:
मुद्गाढकमसूराणां सतिलैर् जाङ्गलैरसैः(?) /
ससैन्धवघृतद्राक्षाशुण्ठ्यामलककोलजैः //
278.m:
With juices of mung bean, pigeon pea, and lentil, together with sesame and broth of wild animals,
prepared with rock salt, ghee, raisins, dried ginger, emblic myrobalan, and jujube,

278.s:
yūṣaiḥ purāṇagodhūmayavaśālyannamabhyaset /
visarpī sasitākṣaudramṛdvīkādāḍimodakam //
278.d:
यूषैः पुराणगोधूमयवशाल्यन्नमभ्यसेत् /
विसर्पी ससिताक्षौद्रमृद्वीकादाडिमोदकम् //
278.m:
with these soups one should eat old wheat, barley, and winter rice.
For erysipelas: sugar, honey, raisins, and pomegranate water;

278.s:
raktayaṣṭikagodhūmayavamudgādikaṃ laghu /
kākamārī ca vetrāgraṃ vāstukañca suvarcalā //
278.d:
रक्तयष्टिकगोधूमयवमुद्गादिकं लघु /
काकमारी च वेत्राग्रं वास्तुकञ्च सुवर्चला //
278.m:
red yaṣṭika rice, wheat, barley, mung beans, and the like, which are light,
black nightshade, cane-tips, goosefoot, and suvarcala greens;

278.s:
vātaśoṇitanāśāya toyaṃ śastaṃ sitaṃ madhu /
:n
1 pathyā tathaiva kāśasya maṇḍaṃ takrañca vāruṇamiti kha.. , ña.. ,
ca
2 yūṣamiti kha.. , ja.. ca
:p 31
nāśārogeśu ca hitaṃ ghṛtaṃ durvāprasādhitam //
278.d:
वातशोणितनाशाय तोयं शस्तं सितं मधु /
:न्
1 पथ्या तथैव काशस्य मण्डं तक्रञ्च वारुणमिति ख.. , ञ.. ,
च
2 यूषमिति ख.. , ज.. च
:प् 31
नाशारोगेशु च हितं घृतं दुर्वाप्रसाधितम् //
278.m:
for destroying gout, water, sugar, and honey are praised.
[Footnote]
1. In manuscripts kha, ña, and ca: “pathyā tathaiva kāśasya maṇḍaṃ takrañca vāruṇam”.
2. In manuscripts kha and ja: “yūṣam”.
[Section] 31
And in diseases of the nose, ghee prepared with dūrvā grass is beneficial.

278.s:
bhṛṅgarājarase siddhaṃ tailaṃ dhātrīrase 'pi vā /
naśyaṃ sarvāmayeṣviṣṭaṃ mūrdhajantūdbhaveṣu ca //
278.d:
भृङ्गराजरसे सिद्धं तैलं धात्रीरसे ऽपि वा /
नश्यं सर्वामयेष्विष्टं मूर्धजन्तूद्भवेषु च //
278.m:
Oil prepared in the juice of bhṛṅgarāja or in the juice of emblic myrobalan
is recommended as nasal drops in all diseases and when worms arise in the head.

278.s:
śītatoyānnapānañca tilānāṃ vipra bhakṣaṇam /
dvijadārḍhyakaraṃ proktaṃ tathā tuṣṭikaramparam //
278.d:
शीततोयान्नपानञ्च तिलानां विप्र भक्षणम् /
द्विजदार्ढ्यकरं प्रोक्तं तथा तुष्टिकरम्परम् //
278.m:
Food and drink with cold water, and eating sesame seeds, O brāhmaṇa,
is declared to produce firmness of the teeth and to give supreme satisfaction.

278.s:
gaṇḍūṣaṃ tilatailena dvijadārḍhyakaraṃ paraṃ /
viḍaṅgacūrṇaṃ gomūtraṃ sarvatra kṛmināśane //
278.d:
गण्डूषं तिलतैलेन द्विजदार्ढ्यकरं परं /
विडङ्गचूर्णं गोमूत्रं सर्वत्र कृमिनाशने //
278.m:
Gargling with sesame oil produces supreme firmness of the teeth.
Powder of viḍaṅga with cow's urine destroys worms in every circumstance.

278.s:
dhātrīphalānyathājyañca śirolepanamuttamam /
śirorogavināśāya snigdhamuṣṇañca bhojanam //
278.d:
धात्रीफलान्यथाज्यञ्च शिरोलेपनमुत्तमम् /
शिरोरोगविनाशाय स्निग्धमुष्णञ्च भोजनम् //
278.m:
Fruits of emblic myrobalan with ghee are an excellent plaster for the head.
For curing head diseases, warm and unctuous food [is prescribed].

278.s:
tailaṃ vā vastamūtrañca karṇapūraṇamuttamam /
karṇaśūlavināśāya sarvaśuktāni(1) vā dvija //
278.d:
तैलं वा वस्तमूत्रञ्च कर्णपूरणमुत्तमम् /
कर्णशूलविनाशाय सर्वशुक्तानि(1) वा द्विज //
278.m:
Oil or goat's urine is an excellent ear-drop;
or all vinegars, O twice-born, destroy earache.

278.s:
girimṛccandanaṃ lākṣā mālatī kalikā tathā /
saṃyojyā yā kṛtā vartiḥ kṣataśukraharī tu sā //
278.d:
गिरिमृच्चन्दनं लाक्षा मालती कलिका तथा /
संयोज्या या कृता वर्तिः क्षतशुक्रहरी तु सा //
