278.m:
Red chalk, sandalwood, lac, and jasmine bud
combined into a wick destroy corneal ulcer.

278.s:
vyoṣaṃ triphalayā yuktaṃ tucchakañca tathā jalam /
sarvākṣirogaśamanaṃ tathā caiva rasāñjanaṃ //
278.d:
व्योषं त्रिफलया युक्तं तुच्छकञ्च तथा जलम् /
सर्वाक्षिरोगशमनं तथा चैव रसाञ्जनं //
278.m:
The three pungents joined with the three fruits, and empty water,
and rasāñjana soothe all eye diseases.

278.s:
ājyabhṛṣṭaṃ śilāpiṣṭaṃ lodhrakāñjikasaindhavaiḥ /
āścyotanāvināśāya sarvanetrāmaye hitam //
278.d:
आज्यभृष्टं शिलापिष्टं लोध्रकाञ्जिकसैन्धवैः /
आश्च्योतनाविनाशाय सर्वनेत्रामये हितम् //
278.m:
Lodhra fried in ghee, ground on a stone with sour gruel and rock salt,
is beneficial in eye-drops for curing all afflictions of the eye.

278.s:
girimṛccandanair lepo vahirnetrasya śasyate /
netrāmayavighātārthaṃ triphalāṃ śīlayet sadā //
278.d:
गिरिमृच्चन्दनैर् लेपो वहिर्नेत्रस्य शस्यते /
नेत्रामयविघातार्थं त्रिफलां शीलयेत् सदा //
278.m:
A plaster of red chalk and sandalwood is recommended outside the eye.
To counteract eye diseases, one should continually use the three fruits.

278.s:
rātrau tu madhusarpirbhyāṃ dīrghamāyurjijīviṣuḥ /
śatāvarīrase siddhau vṛṣyau kṣīraghṛtau smṛtau //
278.d:
रात्रौ तु मधुसर्पिर्भ्यां दीर्घमायुर्जिजीविषुः /
शतावरीरसे सिद्धौ वृष्यौ क्षीरघृतौ स्मृतौ //
278.m:
At night, one desiring a long life [takes them] with honey and ghee.
Milk and ghee prepared in the juice of asparagus are regarded as aphrodisiacs.

278.s:
kalambikāni māṣāś ca vṛṣyau kṣīraghṛtau tathā /
:n
1 sarvaśuklānnīti kha..
:p 32
āyuṣyā triphalā jñeyā pūrvavanmadhukānvitā //
278.d:
कलम्बिकानि माषाश् च वृष्यौ क्षीरघृतौ तथा /
:न्
1 सर्वशुक्लान्नीति ख..
:प् 32
आयुष्या त्रिफला ज्ञेया पूर्ववन्मधुकान्विता //
278.m:
Kalambīka and black gram, as well as milk and ghee, are aphrodisiacs;
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript kha: “sarvaśuklānni”.
[Section] 32
the three fruits combined with licorice as before are to be known as promoting longevity.

278.s:
madhukādirasopetā balīpalitanāśinī /
vacāsiddhaghṛtaṃ vipra bhūtadoṣavināśanam //
278.d:
मधुकादिरसोपेता बलीपलितनाशिनी /
वचासिद्धघृतं विप्र भूतदोषविनाशनम् //
278.m:
Endowed with the juice of licorice and other [drugs], they destroy wrinkles and grey hair.
Ghee prepared with sweet flag, O brāhmaṇa, destroys spirit afflictions;

278.s:
kavyaṃ buddhipradañcaiva(1) tathā sarvārthasādhanam /
valākalkakaṣāyeṇa siddhamabhyañjane hitam //
278.d:
कव्यं बुद्धिप्रदञ्चैव(1) तथा सर्वार्थसाधनम् /
वलाकल्ककषायेण सिद्धमभ्यञ्जने हितम् //
278.m:
it confers poetic wisdom and accomplishes all aims.
[Ghee] prepared with the paste and decoction of balā is beneficial for massage,

278.s:
rāsnāsahacarair vāpi tailaṃ vātavikāriṇām /
anabhiṣyandi yaccānnaṃ tadbraṇeṣu praśasyate //
278.d:
रास्नासहचरैर् वापि तैलं वातविकारिणाम् /
अनभिष्यन्दि यच्चान्नं तद्ब्रणेषु प्रशस्यते //
278.m:
or oil [prepared] with rāsnā and sahacara for those suffering from wind disorders.
And whatever food is non-catarrhal is recommended for wounds.

278.s:
śaktupiṇḍī tathaivāmlā pācanāya praśasyate /
pakvasya ca tathā bhede nimbacūrṇañca ropaṇe //
278.d:
शक्तुपिण्डी तथैवाम्ला पाचनाय प्रशस्यते /
पक्वस्य च तथा भेदे निम्बचूर्णञ्च रोपणे //
278.m:
A sour ball of barley flour is recommended for suppurating;
and for the bursting of a ripe [abscess], nimba powder [is praised] for healing.

278.s:
tathā śūcyupacāraś ca(2) balikarma viśeṣataḥ /
sūtikā ca tathā rakṣā prāṇināntu sadā hitā //
278.d:
तथा शूच्युपचारश् च(2) बलिकर्म विशेषतः /
सूतिका च तथा रक्षा प्राणिनान्तु सदा हिता //
278.m:
So too, pure practice, and especially sacrificial offerings,
and protection in the lying-in room are always beneficial to living beings.

278.s:
bhakṣaṇaṃ nimbapatrāṇāṃ sarpadaṣṭasya bheṣajam /
tālanimbadalaṅkeśyaṃ jīrṇantailaṃ yavāghṛtam //
278.d:
भक्षणं निम्बपत्राणां सर्पदष्टस्य भेषजम् /
तालनिम्बदलङ्केश्यं जीर्णन्तैलं यवाघृतम् //
278.m:
Eating nimba leaves is a remedy for one bitten by a snake.
Palm-fruit and nimba leaves are good for hair; aged oil and barley ghee [are effective].

278.s:
dhūpo vṛścikadaṣṭasya śikhipatraghṛtena vā /
arkakṣīreṇa saṃpiṣṭaṃ lopā vījaṃ palāśajaṃ //
278.d:
धूपो वृश्चिकदष्टस्य शिखिपत्रघृतेन वा /
अर्कक्षीरेण संपिष्टं लोपा वीजं पलाशजं //
278.m:
Incense [is prescribed] for one bitten by a scorpion, or with peacock feathers and ghee;
or seeds of palāśa ground with the milk of calotropis [made into] a plaster.

278.s:
vṛścikārtasya kṛṣṇā vā śivā ca phalasaṃyutā(3) /
arkakṣīraṃ tilaṃ tailaṃ palalañca guḍaṃ samam //
278.d:
वृश्चिकार्तस्य कृष्णा वा शिवा च फलसंयुता(3) /
अर्कक्षीरं तिलं तैलं पललञ्च गुडं समम् //
278.m:
For one afflicted by a scorpion, black pepper or yellow myrobalan with fruits [may be used].
Calotropis milk, sesame, oil, meat, and jaggery in equal parts,

278.s:
pānājjayati durvāraṃ śvaviṣaṃ śīghrameva tu /
pītvā mūlaṃ trivṛttulyaṃ taṇḍulīyasya sarpiṣā //
278.d:
पानाज्जयति दुर्वारं श्वविषं शीघ्रमेव तु /
पीत्वा मूलं त्रिवृत्तुल्यं तण्डुलीयस्य सर्पिषा //
278.m:
by drinking, swiftly overcomes the irresistible poison of a dog.
Having drunk the root of taṇḍulīya equal to trivṛt along with ghee,

278.s:
sarpakīṭaviṣāṇyāśu jayatyatibalānyapi /
candanaṃ padmakaṅkuṣṭhaṃ latāmbūśīrapāṭalāḥ //
:n
1 kanṭhyaṃ vṛddhipradañcaiveti kha..
2 pratyupacāraiśceti kha..
3 kalasaṃyuteti ka..
:p 33
278.d:
सर्पकीटविषाण्याशु जयत्यतिबलान्यपि /
चन्दनं पद्मकङ्कुष्ठं लताम्बूशीरपाटलाः //
:न्
1 कन्ठ्यं वृद्धिप्रदञ्चैवेति ख..
2 प्रत्युपचारैश्चेति ख..
3 कलसंयुतेति क..
:प् 33
278.m:
one swiftly conquers the poison of snakes and insects, even when extremely strong.
Sandalwood, padmaka, costus, latā, vetiver, and pāṭalā,
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript kha: “kaṇṭhyaṃ vṛddhipradañcaiva”.
2. In manuscript kha: “pratyupacāraiśceti”.
3. In manuscript ka: “kalasaṃyuteti”.
[Section] 33

278.s:
nirguṇḍī śārivā selurlūtāviṣaharo gadaḥ /
śirovirecanaṃ śastaṃ guḍanāgarakaṃ dvija //
278.d:
निर्गुण्डी शारिवा सेलुर्लूताविषहरो गदः /
शिरोविरेचनं शस्तं गुडनागरकं द्विज //
278.m:
nirguṇḍī, Indian sarsaparilla, and selu form an ailment-curing remedy against spider poison.
For head evacuation, jaggery and ginger are commended, O twice-born.

278.s:
snehapāne tathā vastau tailaṃ dhṛtamanuttamam /
svedanīyaḥ paro vahniḥ śītāmbhaḥstambhanaṃ param //
278.d:
स्नेहपाने तथा वस्तौ तैलं धृतमनुत्तमम् /
स्वेदनीयः परो वह्निः शीताम्भःस्तम्भनं परम् //
278.m:
In the drinking of unctuous substances and in enemas, oil and ghee are unsurpassed.
Fire is the supreme sweating agent, and cold water is the supreme astringent.

278.s:
trivṛddhi recane śreṣṭhā vamane madanaṃ tathā /
vastirvireko vamanaṃ tailaṃ sarpis tathā madhu /
vātapittabalāśānāṃ krameṇa paramauṣadhaṃ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe siddhauṣadhāni
nāmāṣṭsaptatyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś athaikonāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
sarvarogaharāṇyauṣadhāni
278.d:
त्रिवृद्धि रेचने श्रेष्ठा वमने मदनं तथा /
वस्तिर्विरेको वमनं तैलं सर्पिस् तथा मधु /
वातपित्तबलाशानां क्रमेण परमौषधं //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सिद्धौषधानि
नामाष्ट्सप्तत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथैकोनाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
सर्वरोगहराण्यौषधानि
278.m:
Trivṛt is best for purging, and madana fruit for vomiting;
enema, purging, and vomiting, as well as oil, ghee, and honey,
are the supreme remedies respectively for wind, bile, and phlegm.
Thus ends the two hundred and seventy-eighth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named “Proven Remedies”.
Now the two hundred and seventy-ninth chapter:
Remedies Destroying All Diseases

279.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
śārīramānamāgantusahajā vyādhayo matāḥ /
śārīrā jvarakuṣṭhādyā krodhādyā mānasā matāḥ //
279.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
शारीरमानमागन्तुसहजा व्याधयो मताः /
शारीरा ज्वरकुष्ठाद्या क्रोधाद्या मानसा मताः //

279.s:
āgantavo vighātotthā sahajāḥ kṣujjarādayaḥ /
śārīrāgantunāśāya sūryavāre ghṛtaṃ guḍam //
279.d:
आगन्तवो विघातोत्था सहजाः क्षुज्जरादयः /
शारीरागन्तुनाशाय सूर्यवारे घृतं गुडम् //
279.m:
exogenous [diseases] arise from trauma; innate [diseases] are hunger, old age, and so on.
For the destruction of bodily and exogenous [diseases], on a Sunday one should offer

279.s:
lavaṇaṃ sahiraṇyañca viprāyāpūpamarpayet /
candre cābhyaṅgado vipre sarvarogaiḥ pramucyate //
279.d:
लवणं सहिरण्यञ्च विप्रायापूपमर्पयेत् /
चन्द्रे चाभ्यङ्गदो विप्रे सर्वरोगैः प्रमुच्यते //
279.m:
ghee, jaggery, salt, and sweet cakes along with gold to a brāhmaṇa;
and giving an unction on a Monday to a brāhmaṇa, one is freed from all diseases.

279.s:
tailaṃ śanaiś care dadyādāśvine gorasānnadaḥ /
ghṛtena payasā liṅgaṃ saṃsnāpya syādrugujjhitaḥ //
:p 34
279.d:
तैलं शनैश् चरे दद्यादाश्विने गोरसान्नदः /
घृतेन पयसा लिङ्गं संस्नाप्य स्याद्रुगुज्झितः //
:प् 34
279.m:
One should give oil on a Saturday; in the month of Āśvina, giving dairy products and food,
and bathing the liṅga with ghee and milk, one becomes free from disease.
[Section] 34

279.s:
gāyatryā hāvayedvahnau dūrvāntrimadhurāplutām /
yasmin bhe vyādhimāpnoti tasmin snānaṃ baliḥ śubhe //
279.d:
गायत्र्या हावयेद्वह्नौ दूर्वान्त्रिमधुराप्लुताम् /
यस्मिन् भे व्याधिमाप्नोति तस्मिन् स्नानं बलिः शुभे //
279.m:
One should sacrifice into the fire with the Gāyatrī dūrvā grass smeared with the three sweets.
Under whichever asterism one contracts a disease, under that auspicious one bath and offering [are prescribed].

279.s:
mānasānāṃ rujādīnāṃ viṣṇoḥ stotraṃ haraṃ bhavet /
vātapittakaphā doṣā dhātavaś ca tathā śṛṇu //
279.d:
मानसानां रुजादीनां विष्णोः स्तोत्रं हरं भवेत् /
वातपित्तकफा दोषा धातवश् च तथा शृणु //
279.m:
For mental afflictions and the like, a hymn of praise to Viṣṇu will be the remover.
Wind, bile, and phlegm are the humours, and also the bodily tissues; hear about them:

279.s:
bhuktaṃ pakvāśayādannaṃ dvidhā yāti ca suśruta /
aṃśenaikena kiṭṭadvaṃ rasatāñcāpareṇa ca //
279.d:
भुक्तं पक्वाशयादन्नं द्विधा याति च सुश्रुत /
अंशेनैकेन किट्टद्वं रसताञ्चापरेण च //
279.m:
O Suśruta, the food eaten from the digestive tract goes two ways:
by one portion into waste, and into the state of nutrient fluid by the other.

279.s:
kiṭṭabhāgo malastatra vinmūtrasvedadūṣikāḥ /
nāsāmalaṅkarṇamalaṃ tathā dehamalañca yat //
279.d:
किट्टभागो मलस्तत्र विन्मूत्रस्वेददूषिकाः /
नासामलङ्कर्णमलं तथा देहमलञ्च यत् //
279.m:
There the waste portion is excretion: feces, urine, sweat, rheum of the eyes,
nasal mucus, earwax, and whatever is bodily excrement.

279.s:
rasabhāgādrasastatra samācchoṇitatāṃ vrajet /
māṃsaṃ raktattito medo medaso 'sthnaś ca sambhavaḥ //
279.d:
रसभागाद्रसस्तत्र समाच्छोणिततां व्रजेत् /
मांसं रक्तत्तितो मेदो मेदसो ऽस्थ्नश् च सम्भवः //
279.m: From the nutrient part, the chyle there duly turns into blood; / from blood, flesh; from that, fat; and from fat occurs the production of bone.

279.s:
asthno majjā tataḥ śukraṃ śukādrāgastathaujasaḥ /
deśamārtiṃ balaṃ śaktiṃ kālaṃ prakṛtimeva ca //
279.d:
अस्थ्नो मज्जा ततः शुक्रं शुकाद्रागस्तथौजसः /
देशमार्तिं बलं शक्तिं कालं प्रकृतिमेव च //
279.m: From bone comes marrow; from that, semen; from semen comes lustrous vigor, and similarly vitality. / Having considered the place, the disease, the bodily strength, digestive power, season, and constitution,

279.s:
jñātvā cikitsataṃ kuryādbheṣajasya tathā balam /
tithiṃ riktāntyajed bhaumaṃ mandabhandāruṇograkam //
279.d:
ज्ञात्वा चिकित्सतं कुर्याद्भेषजस्य तथा बलम् /
तिथिं रिक्तान्त्यजेद् भौमं मन्दभन्दारुणोग्रकम् //
279.m: as well as the strength of the medicine, one should administer treatment. / One should avoid an empty lunar day, Tuesday, Saturday, and a fierce, unfavorable [day].

279.s:
harigodvijacandrārkasurādīn pratipūjya ca /
śṛṇu mantramimaṃ vidvan bheṣajārambhamācaret //
279.d:
हरिगोद्विजचन्द्रार्कसुरादीन् प्रतिपूज्य च /
शृणु मन्त्रमिमं विद्वन् भेषजारम्भमाचरेत् //
279.m: Having worshipped Hari, the cow, the twice-born, the moon, the sun, the gods, and others, / listen to this mantra, O wise one, and begin [administering] the medicine:

279.s:
brahmadakṣāśvirudrendrabhūcandrārkānilānalāḥ /
ṛṣayaś cauṣadhigrāmā bhūtasaṅghāś ca pāntu te //
279.d:
ब्रह्मदक्षाश्विरुद्रेन्द्रभूचन्द्रार्कानिलानलाः /
ऋषयश् चौषधिग्रामा भूतसङ्घाश् च पान्तु ते //
279.m: "May Brahmā, Dakṣa, the Aśvins, Rudra, Indra, Earth, the Moon, the Sun, Wind, and Fire, / the sages, the multitude of medicinal herbs, and the hosts of beings protect you!

279.s:
rasāyanamivarṣīṇāṃ devānāmamṛtaṃ yathā /
sudhevottamanāgānāṃ bhaiṣajyamidamastu te //
279.d:
रसायनमिवर्षीणां देवानाममृतं यथा /
सुधेवोत्तमनागानां भैषज्यमिदमस्तु ते //
279.m: Just as the elixir of life is to the sages, just as nectar is to the gods, / just as heavenly ambrosia is to the foremost serpents, so may this medicine be to you!"

279.s:
vātaśleṣmātako deśo bahuvṛkṣo bahūdakaḥ /
anūpaḍtibikhyāto jāṅgalastadvivarjitaḥ //
279.d:
वातश्लेष्मातको देशो बहुवृक्षो बहूदकः /
अनूपड्तिबिख्यातो जाङ्गलस्तद्विवर्जितः //
279.m: A region that aggravates wind and phlegm, having many trees and much water, / is known as marshy; the arid [region] is devoid of these.

279.s:
kiñcidvṛkṣodako deśas tathā sādhāraṇaḥ smṛtaḥ /
:p 35
jāṅgalaḥ pittabahulo madhyaḥ sādhāraṇaḥ smṛtaḥ //
279.d:
किञ्चिद्वृक्षोदको देशस् तथा साधारणः स्मृतः /
:प् 35
जाङ्गलः पित्तबहुलो मध्यः साधारणः स्मृतः //
279.m:
A region with some trees and water is regarded as moderate.
[Page 35]
The arid [region] has an excess of bile; the intermediate is regarded as moderate.

279.s:
rūkṣmaḥ śītaś calo vāyuḥ pittamuṣṇaṃ kaṭutrayam /
sthirāmlasnigdhamadhuraṃ balāśañca pracakṣate //
279.d:
रूक्ष्मः शीतश् चलो वायुः पित्तमुष्णं कटुत्रयम् /
स्थिराम्लस्निग्धमधुरं बलाशञ्च प्रचक्षते //
279.m: Wind is dry, cold, and mobile; bile is hot, pungent, and sharp; / phlegm is declared to be stable, sour, unctuous, and sweet.

279.s:
vṛddhiḥ samānair eteṣāṃ viparītair viparyayaḥ /
rasāḥ svādvamlalavaṇāḥ śleṣmalā vāyunāśanāḥ //
279.d:
वृद्धिः समानैर् एतेषां विपरीतैर् विपर्ययः /
रसाः स्वाद्वम्ललवणाः श्लेष्मला वायुनाशनाः //
279.m: Their increase is caused by similar [qualities], their decrease by opposite ones. / Tastes that are sweet, sour, and salty increase phlegm and destroy wind.

279.s:
kaṭutiktakaṣāyāś ca vātalāḥ śleṣmanāśanāḥ /
kaṭvamlalavaṇā jñeyās tathā pittavivardhanāḥ //
279.d:
कटुतिक्तकषायाश् च वातलाः श्लेष्मनाशनाः /
कट्वम्ललवणा ज्ञेयास् तथा पित्तविवर्धनाः //
279.m: Pungent, bitter, and astringent [tastes] increase wind and destroy phlegm. / Pungent, sour, and salty [tastes] are to be known as increasing bile.

279.s:
tiktasvādukaṣāyāś ca tathā pittavināśanāḥ /
rasasyaitadguṇaṃ nāsti vipākasyaitadiṣyate //
279.d:
तिक्तस्वादुकषायाश् च तथा पित्तविनाशनाः /
रसस्यैतद्गुणं नास्ति विपाकस्यैतदिष्यते //
279.m: Bitter, sweet, and astringent [tastes] destroy bile. / This is not a quality of the taste [alone]; it is held to belong to the post-digestive effect.

279.s:
vīryoṣṇāḥ kaphavātaghnāḥ śītāḥ pittavināśanāḥ /
prabhāvatas tathā karma te kurvanti ca suśruta //
279.d:
वीर्योष्णाः कफवातघ्नाः शीताः पित्तविनाशनाः /
प्रभावतस् तथा कर्म ते कुर्वन्ति च सुश्रुत //
279.m: Substances hot in potency destroy phlegm and wind; cold ones destroy bile; / and they also act by their specific potency, O Suśruta.

279.s:
śiśire ca vasante ca nidāghe ca tathā kramāt /
cayaprakopapraśamāḥ kaphasya tu prakīrtitāḥ //
279.d:
शिशिरे च वसन्ते च निदाघे च तथा क्रमात् /
चयप्रकोपप्रशमाः कफस्य तु प्रकीर्तिताः //
279.m: In the cold season, spring, and summer, respectively, / the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of phlegm are proclaimed.

279.s:
nidāghavarṣārātrau ca tathā śaradi suśruta /
cayaprakopapraśamāḥ pavanasya prakīrtitāḥ //
279.d:
निदाघवर्षारात्रौ च तथा शरदि सुश्रुत /
चयप्रकोपप्रशमाः पवनस्य प्रकीर्तिताः //
279.m: In summer, the rainy season, and autumn, O Suśruta, / the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of wind are proclaimed.

279.s:
meghakāle ca śaradi hemante ca yathākramāt /
cayaprakopapraśamās tathā pittasya kīrtitāḥ //
279.d:
मेघकाले च शरदि हेमन्ते च यथाक्रमात् /
चयप्रकोपप्रशमास् तथा पित्तस्य कीर्तिताः //
279.m: In the rainy season, autumn, and early winter, respectively, / the accumulation, aggravation, and pacification of bile are declared.

279.s:
varṣādyo visargastu hemantādyās tathā trayaḥ /
śiśirādyās tathādānaṃ grīṣmāntā ṛtavastrayaḥ //
279.d:
वर्षाद्यो विसर्गस्तु हेमन्ताद्यास् तथा त्रयः /
शिशिराद्यास् तथादानं ग्रीष्मान्ता ऋतवस्त्रयः //
279.m: The release [period] begins with the rainy season, consisting of the three starting with early winter; / the period of absorption begins with the cold season, consisting of the three seasons ending with summer.

279.s:
saumyo visargastvādānamāgneyaṃ parikīrtitam /
varṣādīṃstrīnṛtūn somaś caran paryāyaśo rasān //
279.d:
सौम्यो विसर्गस्त्वादानमाग्नेयं परिकीर्तितम् /
वर्षादींस्त्रीनृतून् सोमश् चरन् पर्यायशो रसान् //
279.m: The release [period] is lunar, while the period of absorption is proclaimed to be solar. / The moon, traversing the three seasons beginning with the rainy season, in turn,

279.s:
janayatyamlalavaṇamadhurāṃstrīn yathākramam /
śiśirādīnṛtūnarkaś caran paryayaśo rasān //
:p 36
279.d:
जनयत्यम्ललवणमधुरांस्त्रीन् यथाक्रमम् /
शिशिरादीनृतूनर्कश् चरन् पर्ययशो रसान् //
:प् 36
279.m:
produces the three tastes: sour, salty, and sweet, respectively. / The sun, traversing the seasons beginning with the cold season, in turn,
[Page 36]

279.s:
vivardhayettathā tiktakaṣāyakaṭukān kramāt /
yathā rajanyo vardhante valamekaṃ hi vardhate //
279.d:
विवर्धयेत्तथा तिक्तकषायकटुकान् क्रमात् /
यथा रजन्यो वर्धन्ते वलमेकं हि वर्धते //
279.m: increases bitter, astringent, and pungent [tastes] in succession. / As the nights lengthen, strength alone increases;

279.s:
kramaśo 'tha manuṣyāṇāṃ hīyamānāsu hīyate /
rātribhuktadinānāñca vayasaś ca tathaiva ca //
279.d:
क्रमशो ऽथ मनुष्याणां हीयमानासु हीयते /
रात्रिभुक्तदिनानाञ्च वयसश् च तथैव च //
279.m: and gradually, as they diminish, it diminishes in human beings. / In the beginning, middle, and end of the night, of digestion, of the day,

279.s:
ādimadhyāvasāneṣu kaphapittasamīraṇāḥ /
prakopaṃ yānti kopādau kāle teṣāñcayaḥ smṛtaḥ //
279.d:
आदिमध्यावसानेषु कफपित्तसमीरणाः /
प्रकोपं यान्ति कोपादौ काले तेषाञ्चयः स्मृतः //
279.m: and likewise of life, phlegm, bile, and wind / undergo aggravation. Their accumulation is remembered at the time prior to aggravation;

279.s:
prakopottarake kāle śamasteṣāṃ prakīrtitaḥ /
adibhojanato vipra tathā cābhojanena ca //
279.d:
प्रकोपोत्तरके काले शमस्तेषां प्रकीर्तितः /
अदिभोजनतो विप्र तथा चाभोजनेन च //
279.m: their pacification is proclaimed at the time following aggravation. / From overeating, O twice-born one, and likewise from fasting,

279.s:
rogā hi sarve jāyante vegodīraṇadhāraṇaiḥ /
annena kukṣerdvāvaṃśāvekaṃ pānena pūrayet //
279.d:
रोगा हि सर्वे जायन्ते वेगोदीरणधारणैः /
अन्नेन कुक्षेर्द्वावंशावेकं पानेन पूरयेत् //
279.m: indeed all diseases arise, [and also] by exciting or suppressing natural urges. / One should fill two parts of the stomach with food, and one with drink;

279.s:
āśrayaṃ pavanādīnāṃ tathaikamavaśeṣayet /
vyādher nidānasya tathā viparītamathauṣadham //
279.d:
आश्रयं पवनादीनां तथैकमवशेषयेत् /
व्याधेर् निदानस्य तथा विपरीतमथौषधम् //
279.m: and one should leave one part empty for the movement of wind and the others. / Medicine should be administered that is contrary to the disease and its cause;

279.s:
kartavyametadevātra mayā sāraṃ prakīrtitam /
nābherūrdhvamadhaś caiva gudaśroṇyostathaiva ca //
279.d:
कर्तव्यमेतदेवात्र मया सारं प्रकीर्तितम् /
नाभेरूर्ध्वमधश् चैव गुदश्रोण्योस्तथैव च //
279.m: this alone should be done; I have stated the essence here. / Above the navel, below it, and likewise in the anus and pelvis,

279.s:
balāśapittavātānāṃ dehe sthānaṃ prakīrtitaṃ /
tathāpi sarvagāś caite dehe vāyurviśeṣataḥ //
279.d:
बलाशपित्तवातानां देहे स्थानं प्रकीर्तितं /
तथापि सर्वगाश् चैते देहे वायुर्विशेषतः //
279.m: the locations of phlegm, bile, and wind in the body are declared; / nevertheless, these move throughout the whole body, especially wind.

279.s:
dehasya madhye hṛdayaṃ sthānaṃ tanmanasaḥ smṛtam /
kṛśo 'lpakeśaś capalo bahuvāgviṣamānalaḥ //
279.d:
देहस्य मध्ये हृदयं स्थानं तन्मनसः स्मृतम् /
कृशो ऽल्पकेशश् चपलो बहुवाग्विषमानलः //
279.m: The heart in the center of the body is remembered as the seat of the mind. / A person who is emaciated, has little hair, is fickle, talkative, has irregular digestive fire,

279.s:
vyomagaś ca tathā svapne vātaprakṛtirucyate /
akālapalitaḥ krodhī prasvedī madhurapriyaḥ //
279.d:
व्योमगश् च तथा स्वप्ने वातप्रकृतिरुच्यते /
अकालपलितः क्रोधी प्रस्वेदी मधुरप्रियः //
279.m: and moves through the sky in dreams, is said to have a wind constitution. / One whose hair greys prematurely, who is wrathful, sweats profusely, is fond of sweets,

279.s:
svapne ca dīptimatprekṣī pittaprakṛtirucyate /
dṛḍhāṅgaḥ sthiracittaś ca suprabhaḥ snigdhasūrdhajaḥ //
279.d:
स्वप्ने च दीप्तिमत्प्रेक्षी पित्तप्रकृतिरुच्यते /
दृढाङ्गः स्थिरचित्तश् च सुप्रभः स्निग्धसूर्धजः //
279.m: and sees bright lights in dreams, is said to have a bile constitution. / One whose limbs are firm, whose mind is steady, who has good luster, glossy hair,

279.s:
śuddhāmbudarśī svapne ca kaphaprakṛtiko naraḥ /
:p 37
tāmasā rājasāś caiva sātvikāś ca tathā smṛtāḥ //
279.d:
शुद्धाम्बुदर्शी स्वप्ने च कफप्रकृतिको नरः /
:प् 37
तामसा राजसाश् चैव सात्विकाश् च तथा स्मृताः //
279.m:
and sees clear water in dreams, is a person of phlegm constitution.
[Page 37]
They are also regarded as tamasic, rajasic, and sattvic, respectively,

279.s:
manuṣyā munirśādūla vātapittakaphātmakāḥ /
raktapittaṃ vyavāyācca gurukarmapravartanaiḥ //
279.d:
मनुष्या मुनिर्शादूल वातपित्तकफात्मकाः /
रक्तपित्तं व्यवायाच्च गुरुकर्मप्रवर्तनैः //
279.m: O tiger among sages—men characterized by wind, bile, and phlegm. / From sexual intercourse, undertaking heavy labor,

279.s:
kadannabhojanādvāyurdehe śokācca kupyati /
vidāhināṃ tatholkānāmuṣṇānnādhvanisevināṃ(1) //
279.d:
कदन्नभोजनाद्वायुर्देहे शोकाच्च कुप्यति /
विदाहिनां तथोल्कानामुष्णान्नाध्वनिसेविनां(1) //
279.m: eating bad food, and from grief, wind is aggravated in the body. / In those who consume burning substances, firebrands, hot food, and engage in travel,

279.s:
pittaṃ prakopamāyāti bhayena ca tathā dvija /
atyambupānagurvannabhojināṃ bhuktaśāyinām //
279.d:
पित्तं प्रकोपमायाति भयेन च तथा द्विज /
अत्यम्बुपानगुर्वन्नभोजिनां भुक्तशायिनाम् //
279.m: bile becomes aggravated, and likewise from fear, O twice-born one. / In those who drink too much water, eat heavy food, sleep after meals,

279.s:
ślekeṣmāprakopamāyāti tathā ye cālasā janāḥ /
vātādyutthāni rogāṇi jñātvā śāmyāni lakṣaṇaiḥ //
279.d:
श्लेकेष्माप्रकोपमायाति तथा ये चालसा जनाः /
वाताद्युत्थानि रोगाणि ज्ञात्वा शाम्यानि लक्षणैः //
279.m: and people who are indolent, phlegm becomes aggravated. / Having identified diseases arising from wind and the others, which are pacified through their symptoms:

279.s:
asthibhaṅgaḥ kaṣāyatvamāsye śuṣkāsyatā tathā /
jṛmbhaṇaṃ lomaharṣaś ca vātikavyādhilakṣaṇam //
279.d:
अस्थिभङ्गः कषायत्वमास्ये शुष्कास्यता तथा /
जृम्भणं लोमहर्षश् च वातिकव्याधिलक्षणम् //
279.m: bone fracture, astringency in the mouth, dryness of the mouth, / yawning, and horripilation are the signs of a wind-born disease.

279.s:
nakhanetraśirāṇāntu pītatvaṃ kaṭutā mukhe /
tṛṣṇā dāhoṣṇatā caiva pittavyādhinidarśanam //
279.d:
नखनेत्रशिराणान्तु पीतत्वं कटुता मुखे /
तृष्णा दाहोष्णता चैव पित्तव्याधिनिदर्शनम् //
279.m: Yellowness of the nails, eyes, and veins, bitterness in the mouth, / thirst, a burning sensation, and feverish heat are the indicators of a bile disease.

279.s:
ālasyañca prasekaś ca gurutā madhurāsyatā /
uṣṇābhilāṣitā ceti ślaiṣmikavyādhilakṣaṇam //
279.d:
आलस्यञ्च प्रसेकश् च गुरुता मधुरास्यता /
उष्णाभिलाषिता चेति श्लैष्मिकव्याधिलक्षणम् //
279.m: Lethargy, excessive salivation, heaviness, sweetness in the mouth, / and a craving for warmth are the signs of a phlegm disease.

279.s:
snigdhoṣṇamannamabhyaṅgastailapānādi vātanut /
ājyaṃ kṣīraṃ sitādyañca candraraśmyādi pittanut //
279.d:
स्निग्धोष्णमन्नमभ्यङ्गस्तैलपानादि वातनुत् /
आज्यं क्षीरं सिताद्यञ्च चन्द्ररश्म्यादि पित्तनुत् //
279.m: Unctuous, hot food, massage, drinking medicated oils, and the like dispel wind. / Ghee, milk, sugar, and moonbeams dispel bile.

279.s:
sakṣaudraṃ triphalātailaṃ vyāyāmādi kaphāpaham /
sarvarogapraśāntyai syadviṣṇordhyānañca pūjanam //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe sarvarogaharāṇyauṣadhāni
nāmonāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:n
tatholkānāmuṣmaṇāmadhvasevināmiti kha..
:p 38
:ś athāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
rasādilakṣaṇaṃ
279.d:
सक्षौद्रं त्रिफलातैलं व्यायामादि कफापहम् /
सर्वरोगप्रशान्त्यै स्यद्विष्णोर्ध्यानञ्च पूजनम् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे सर्वरोगहराण्यौषधानि
नामोनाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:न्
तथोल्कानामुष्मणामध्वसेविनामिति ख..
:प् 38
:श् अथाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
रसादिलक्षणं
279.m:
Triphalā oil with honey, exercise, and the like remove phlegm. / Meditation upon and worship of Viṣṇu will effect the pacification of all diseases.
Thus in the great Agni Purāṇa, the two hundred and seventy-ninth chapter, entitled "Medicines That Dispel All Diseases."
[Note]
"tatholkānāmuṣmaṇāmadhvasevinām" in manuscript Kha. / [Page 38]
Now, the two hundred and eightieth chapter.
Characteristics of Tastes and Other Properties.

280.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
rasādilakṣaṇaṃ vakṣye bheṣajānāṃ guṇaṃ śṛṇu /
rasavīryavipākajño nṛpādīnrakṣayennaraḥ //
280.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
रसादिलक्षणं वक्ष्ये भेषजानां गुणं शृणु /
रसवीर्यविपाकज्ञो नृपादीन्रक्षयेन्नरः //
280.m: Dhanvantari said: / I shall state the characteristics of tastes and so forth; listen to the qualities of medicines. / A person who understands taste, potency, and post-digestive effect can protect kings and others.

280.s:
rasāḥ svādvamlalavaṇāḥ somajāḥ parikīrtitāḥ /
kaṭutiktakaṣāyāni tathāgneyā mahābhuja //
280.d:
रसाः स्वाद्वम्ललवणाः सोमजाः परिकीर्तिताः /
कटुतिक्तकषायानि तथाग्नेया महाभुज //
280.m: Sweet, sour, and salty tastes are declared to be born of Soma; / pungent, bitter, and astringent tastes are fiery, O mighty-armed one.

280.s:
tridhā vipāko dravyasya kaṭvamlalavaṇātmakaḥ /
dvidhā vīyya samuddiṣṭamuṣṇaṃ śītaṃ tathaiva ca //
280.d:
त्रिधा विपाको द्रव्यस्य कट्वम्ललवणात्मकः /
द्विधा वीय्य समुद्दिष्टमुष्णं शीतं तथैव च //
280.m: The post-digestive effect of a substance is threefold, consisting of pungent, sour, and sweet. / Potency is declared to be twofold: hot and cold.

280.s:
anirdeśyaprabhāvaś ca oṣadhīnāṃ dvijottama /
madhuraś ca kaṣāyaś ca tiktaś caiva tathā rasaḥ //
280.d:
अनिर्देश्यप्रभावश् च ओषधीनां द्विजोत्तम /
मधुरश् च कषायश् च तिक्तश् चैव तथा रसः //
280.m: And the specific potency of medicinal plants is inexplicable, O best of the twice-born. / Sweet, astringent, and bitter tastes

280.s:
śītavīryāḥ samuddiṣṭāḥ śeṣāstūṣṇāḥprakīrtitāḥ /
guḍucī tatra tiktapi bhavatyuṣṇātivīryataḥ //
280.d:
शीतवीर्याः समुद्दिष्टाः शेषास्तूष्णाःप्रकीर्तिताः /
गुडुची तत्र तिक्तपि भवत्युष्णातिवीर्यतः //
280.m: are taught to be cold in potency, while the remaining ones are proclaimed to be hot. / Among them, guḍūcī, though bitter, is hot due to its superior potency.

280.s:
uṣṇā kaṣāyāpi tathā pathyā bhavati mānada /
madhuropi tathā māṃsa uṣṇa eva prakīrtitaḥ //
280.d:
उष्णा कषायापि तथा पथ्या भवति मानद /
मधुरोपि तथा मांस उष्ण एव प्रकीर्तितः //
280.m: Likewise pathyā, though astringent, is hot, O giver of honor; / meat also, though sweet, is declared to be hot.

280.s:
lavaṇo madhraś caiva vipākamadhurau smṛtau /
amloṣṇaś ca tathā proktaḥ śeṣāḥ kaṭuvipākinaḥ //
280.d:
लवणो मध्रश् चैव विपाकमधुरौ स्मृतौ /
अम्लोष्णश् च तथा प्रोक्तः शेषाः कटुविपाकिनः //
280.m: Salty and sweet tastes are taught to have sweet post-digestive effects; / sour is hot, and the rest have pungent post-digestive effects.

280.s:
vīryapāke viparyaste prabhāvāttatra niś cayaḥ /
madhuro 'pi kaṭuḥ pāke yacca kṣaudraṃ(1) prakīrtitaṃ //
280.d:
वीर्यपाके विपर्यस्ते प्रभावात्तत्र निश् चयः /
मधुरो ऽपि कटुः पाके यच्च क्षौद्रं(1) प्रकीर्तितं //
280.m: When potency and post-digestive transformation are inverted, the decision is based on specific action (prabhāva); / thus honey, though sweet, is taught to be pungent in post-digestive effect.

280.s:
kvāthayet ṣoḍaśaguṇaṃ viveddravyāccaturguṇam /
:n
1 yavakṣaudramiti kha..
:p 39
kalpanaiṣā kaṣāyasya yatra nokto vidhirbhavet //
280.d:
क्वाथयेत् षोडशगुणं विवेद्द्रव्याच्चतुर्गुणम् /
:न्
1 यवक्षौद्रमिति ख..
:प् 39
कल्पनैषा कषायस्य यत्र नोक्तो विधिर्भवेत् //
280.m:
One should boil sixteen times [as much water], and drink four times [as much as] the substance.
[Footnote]
1. 'Yavakṣaudram' in manuscript kha. / [page 39]
This is the formulation of a decoction where no specific rule has been declared.

280.s:
kaṣāyantu bhavettoyaṃ snehapāke caturguṇaṃ(1) /
dravyatulyaṃ samuddhṛtya dravyaṃ snehaṃ kṣipedbudhaḥ //
280.d:
कषायन्तु भवेत्तोयं स्नेहपाके चतुर्गुणं(1) /
द्रव्यतुल्यं समुद्धृत्य द्रव्यं स्नेहं क्षिपेद्बुधः //
280.m: The decoction water in cooking unctuous substance should be fourfold; / having taken equal substance to substance, the wise one should add the unctuous substance.

280.s:
tāvatpramāṇaṃ dravyasya snehapādaṃ tataḥ kṣipet /
toyavarjantu yaddravyaṃ snehadravyaṃ tathā bhavet //
280.d:
तावत्प्रमाणं द्रव्यस्य स्नेहपादं ततः क्षिपेत् /
तोयवर्जन्तु यद्द्रव्यं स्नेहद्रव्यं तथा भवेत् //
280.m: One should then add a fourth part of the unctuous substance of the substance's measure; / and that which is substance devoid of water becomes the unctuous substance.

280.s:
saṃvartitauṣadhaḥ pākaḥ snehānāṃ parikīrtitaḥ /
tattulyatā tu lehyasya tathā bhavati suśruta(2) //
280.d:
संवर्तितौषधः पाकः स्नेहानां परिकीर्तितः /
तत्तुल्यता तु लेह्यस्य तथा भवति सुश्रुत(2) //
280.m: The cooking of unctuous substances is declared to be [done] when the medicinal paste rolls together into a ball; / its equality, O Suśruta, becomes likewise for an electuary.

280.s:
svacchamalpauṣadhaṃ kvāthaṃ kaṣāyañcoktavadbhavet /
akṣaṃ cūrṇasya nirdiṣṭaṃ kaṣāyasya catuṣpalaṃ //
280.d:
स्वच्छमल्पौषधं क्वाथं कषायञ्चोक्तवद्भवेत् /
अक्षं चूर्णस्य निर्दिष्टं कषायस्य चतुष्पलं //
280.m: A clear decoction with little medicine and an astringent drink are as described; / an akṣa is declared for a powder, and four palas for a decoction.

280.s:
madhyamaiṣā smṛtā mātrā nāsti mātrāvikalpanā /
vayaḥ kālaṃ balaṃ vahniṃ deśaṃ dravyaṃ rujaṃ tathā //
280.d:
मध्यमैषा स्मृता मात्रा नास्ति मात्राविकल्पना /
वयः कालं बलं वह्निं देशं द्रव्यं रुजं तथा //
280.m: This is considered the middling dose; there is no fixed determination of dose; / observing age, season, strength, digestive fire, region, substance, and disease,

280.s:
samavekṣya mahābhāga mātrāyāḥ kalpanā bhavet /
saumyāstatra rasāḥ prāyo vijñeyā dhātuvardhanāḥ //
280.d:
समवेक्ष्य महाभाग मात्रायाः कल्पना भवेत् /
सौम्यास्तत्र रसाः प्रायो विज्ञेया धातुवर्धनाः //
280.m: the formulation of the dosage should be made, O fortunate one. / Gentle tastes there are generally to be known as increasing the bodily tissues.

280.s:
madhurāstu viśeṣeṇa vijñeyā dhātuvardhanāḥ /
doṣāṇāñcaiva dhātūnāṃ dravyaṃ samaguṇantu yat //
280.d:
मधुरास्तु विशेषेण विज्ञेया धातुवर्धनाः /
दोषाणाञ्चैव धातूनां द्रव्यं समगुणन्तु यत् //
280.m: Sweet tastes especially are to be known as increasing the bodily tissues. / A substance that possesses qualities equal to the humors and bodily tissues

280.s:
tadeva vṛddhaye jñeyaṃ viparītaṃ kṣamāvaham /
upastambhatrayaṃ proktaṃ dehe 'sminmanujottama //
280.d:
तदेव वृद्धये ज्ञेयं विपरीतं क्षमावहम् /
उपस्तम्भत्रयं प्रोक्तं देहे ऽस्मिन्मनुजोत्तम //
280.m: is to be known as producing their increase, while one of opposite qualities brings about their decrease. / Three supporting pillars are declared in this body, O best of men:

280.s:
āhāro maithunaṃ nidrā teṣu yatnaḥ sadā bhavet /
asevanāt sevanācca atyantaṃ nāśamāpnuyāt //
280.d:
आहारो मैथुनं निद्रा तेषु यत्नः सदा भवेत् /
असेवनात् सेवनाच्च अत्यन्तं नाशमाप्नुयात् //
280.m: food, sexual intercourse, and sleep; one must always take care in these; / through non-practice or excessive practice one would meet total ruin.

280.s:
kṣayasya bṛṃhaṇaṃ kāryaṃ sthuladehasya karṣaṇam /
rakṣaṇaṃ madhyakāyasya dehabhedāstrayo matāḥ //
:n
1 snehapāke ca tadguṇamiti kha..
2 tattulyatāpyasya tathā yathā bhavati suśruta iti kha..
:p 40
280.d:
क्षयस्य बृंहणं कार्यं स्थुलदेहस्य कर्षणम् /
रक्षणं मध्यकायस्य देहभेदास्त्रयो मताः //
:न्
1 स्नेहपाके च तद्गुणमिति ख..
2 तत्तुल्यताप्यस्य तथा यथा भवति सुश्रुत इति ख..
:प् 40
280.m:
Nourishment is to be given to the emaciated; reduction for the obese body; / preservation for the middling body—three divisions of bodies are recognized.
[Footnote]
1. 'And in the cooking of an unctuous substance, that quality' in manuscript kha.
2. 'Its equality also becomes as it is, O Suśruta' in manuscript kha. / [page 40]

280.s:
upakramadvayaṃ proktaṃ tarpaṇaṃ vāpyatarpaṇaṃ /
hitāśī ca mitāśī ca jīrṇāśī ca tathā bhavet //
280.d:
उपक्रमद्वयं प्रोक्तं तर्पणं वाप्यतर्पणं /
हिताशी च मिताशी च जीर्णाशी च तथा भवेत् //
280.m: Two treatments are declared: nourishing or depletive. / One should eat wholesome food, eat measured food, and eat when previous food is digested.

280.s:
oṣadhīnāṃ pañcavidhā tathā bhavati kalpanā /
rasaḥ kalkaḥ śṛtaḥ śītaḥ phāṇḍaś ca manujottama //
280.d:
ओषधीनां पञ्चविधा तथा भवति कल्पना /
रसः कल्कः शृतः शीतः फाण्डश् च मनुजोत्तम //
280.m: The preparation of herbs is fivefold, O best of men: / fresh juice, paste, decoction, cold infusion, and hot infusion.

280.s:
rasaś ca pīḍako jñeyaḥ kalka āloḍitād bhavet /
kvathitaś ca śṛto jñeyaḥ śītaḥ paryuṣito niśāṃ //
280.d:
रसश् च पीडको ज्ञेयः कल्क आलोडिताद् भवेत् /
क्वथितश् च शृतो ज्ञेयः शीतः पर्युषितो निशां //
280.m: Fresh juice should be known as obtained by pressing; paste comes from churning [or grinding]; / decoction is known as boiled; cold infusion is what has stood overnight;

280.s:
sadyobhiśṛtapūtaṃ yat tat phāṇṭamabhidhīyate /
karaṇānāṃ śatañcaiva ṣaṣṭiś caivādhikā smṛtā //
280.d:
सद्योभिशृतपूतं यत् तत् फाण्टमभिधीयते /
करणानां शतञ्चैव षष्टिश् चैवाधिका स्मृता //
280.m: that which is instantly boiled and filtered is called a hot infusion. / The operations are remembered to be one hundred and sixty in addition.

280.s:
yo vetti sa hy ajeyaḥ sthātsambandhe vāhuśauṇḍikaḥ /
āhāraśuddhiragnyarthamagnimūlaṃ balaṃ nṛṇāṃ //
280.d:
यो वेत्ति स ह्य् अजेयः स्थात्सम्बन्धे वाहुशौण्डिकः /
आहारशुद्धिरग्न्यर्थमग्निमूलं बलं नृणां //
280.m: He who knows this would indeed be unconquerable, skilled in bodily wrestling. / Purity of food is for the sake of the digestive fire; the digestive fire is the root of men's strength.

280.s:
sasindhutriphalāñcādyātsurājñi abhivarṇadāṃ /
jāṅgalañca rasaṃ sindhuyuktaṃ dadhi payaḥ kaṇāṃ //
280.d:
ससिन्धुत्रिफलाञ्चाद्यात्सुराज्ञि अभिवर्णदां /
जाङ्गलञ्च रसं सिन्धुयुक्तं दधि पयः कणां //
280.m: One should consume triphalā with rock salt, O good king, as it imparts complexion; / and wild meat broth with rock salt, curd, milk, and pippalī.

280.s:
rasādhikaṃ samaṃ kuryānnaro vātādhiko 'pi vā /
nidāghe mardanaṃ proktaṃ śiśire ca samaṃ bahu //
280.d:
रसाधिकं समं कुर्यान्नरो वाताधिको ऽपि वा /
निदाघे मर्दनं प्रोक्तं शिशिरे च समं बहु //
280.m: A man should make an excess of bodily fluid equal, or if he has an excess of vāta. / Massage is prescribed in the summer, and equally extensive in the dewy season;

280.s:
vasante madhyamaṃ jñeyannidāghe mardanolvaṇaṃ /
tvacantu prathamaṃ mardyamaṅgañca tadanantaraṃ //
280.d:
वसन्ते मध्यमं ज्ञेयन्निदाघे मर्दनोल्वणं /
त्वचन्तु प्रथमं मर्द्यमङ्गञ्च तदनन्तरं //
280.m: it should be known as moderate in spring, and intense massage in summer. / First the skin should be massaged, and immediately after, the limb.

280.s:
snāyurudhiradeheṣu asthi bhātīva māṃsalaṃ /
skandhau bāhū tathaiveha tathā jaṅghe sajānunī //
280.d:
स्नायुरुधिरदेहेषु अस्थि भातीव मांसलं /
स्कन्धौ बाहू तथैवेह तथा जङ्घे सजानुनी //
280.m: In bodies having tendons and blood, the bone appears as if fleshy; / the shoulders, the arms, and likewise here the shanks with the knees,

280.s:
arivanmardayet prajño jatru vakṣaś ca pūrvavat /
aṅgasandhiṣu sarveṣu niṣpīḍya bahulaṃ tathā //
280.d:
अरिवन्मर्दयेत् प्रज्ञो जत्रु वक्षश् च पूर्ववत् /
अङ्गसन्धिषु सर्वेषु निष्पीड्य बहुलं तथा //
280.m: the wise one should massage like an enemy, and the collarbones and chest as before; / and pressing firmly upon all the joints of the limbs,

280.s:
prasārayedaṅgasandhīnna ca kṣepeṇa cākramāt /
nījīrṇe tu śramaṃ kuryānna bhuktvā pītavānnaraḥ //
280.d:
प्रसारयेदङ्गसन्धीन्न च क्षेपेण चाक्रमात् /
नीजीर्णे तु श्रमं कुर्यान्न भुक्त्वा पीतवान्नरः //
280.m: he should extend the joints of the limbs, but not with sudden jerk or out of order. / A man should not exert himself when food is undigested, nor after eating or drinking.

280.s:
dinasya tu caturbhāga ūrdhvantu praharārdhake /
:p 41
vyāyāmaṃ naiva kartavyaṃ snāyācchītāmbunā sakṛt //
280.d:
दिनस्य तु चतुर्भाग ऊर्ध्वन्तु प्रहरार्धके /
:प् 41
व्यायामं नैव कर्तव्यं स्नायाच्छीताम्बुना सकृत् //
280.m:
At the fourth part of the day, but after half a prahara,
[page 41]
exercise should not be done; one should bathe once with cold water.

280.s:
vāryuṣṇañca śramaṃ jahyāddhṛdā śvāsanna dhārayet /
vyāyāmaś ca kaphaṃ hanyādvātaṃ hanyācca mardanaṃ //
280.d:
वार्युष्णञ्च श्रमं जह्याद्धृदा श्वासन्न धारयेत् /
व्यायामश् च कफं हन्याद्वातं हन्याच्च मर्दनं //
280.m: Warm water dispels exhaustion; one should not hold the breath with the chest. / Exercise destroys kapha, and massage destroys vāta;

280.s:
snānaṃ pittādhikaṃ hanyāttasyānte cātapāḥ priyāḥ /
ātapakleśakarmādau kṣemavyāyāmino narāḥ //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe rasādilakṣaṇaṃ
nāmāśītyadhikadvisatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:ś athaikāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
vṛkṣāyurvedaḥ
280.d:
स्नानं पित्ताधिकं हन्यात्तस्यान्ते चातपाः प्रियाः /
आतपक्लेशकर्मादौ क्षेमव्यायामिनो नराः //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे रसादिलक्षणं
नामाशीत्यधिकद्विसततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:श् अथैकाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
वृक्षायुर्वेदः
280.m:
bathing destroys excess pitta, and at the end of it sunshine is pleasant. / In heat, toil, exertion and the like, people are secure exercises.
Thus ends the two hundred and eightieth chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named 'Characteristics of Tastes and the Rest'.
Now begins the two hundred and eighty-first chapter.
Arbori-horticulture (Vṛkṣāyurveda).

281.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
vṛkṣāyurvedamākhyāsye plakṣaścottarataḥ śubhaḥ /
prāgvaṭo yāmyatastvāmra āpye 'śvatthaḥ karmeṇa tu //
281.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
वृक्षायुर्वेदमाख्यास्ये प्लक्षश्चोत्तरतः शुभः /
प्राग्वटो याम्यतस्त्वाम्र आप्ये ऽश्वत्थः कर्मेण तु //
281.m: Dhanvantari said: / I shall declare arbori-horticulture. The plakṣa is auspicious to the north; / the banyan to the east, the mango to the south, and the aśvattha in order to the west.

281.s:
dakṣiṇāṃ diśamutpannāḥ samīpe kaṇṭakadrumāḥ /
udyānaṃ gṛhavāse(1) syāt tilān vāpyatha puṣpitān //
281.d:
दक्षिणां दिशमुत्पन्नाः समीपे कण्टकद्रुमाः /
उद्यानं गृहवासे(1) स्यात् तिलान् वाप्यथ पुष्पितान् //
281.m: Thorny trees growing in the southern direction near [the dwelling] / should be in the garden of the dwelling, or [one should sow] flowering sesamum seeds.

281.s:
gṛhṇīyādropayedvṛkṣān dvijañcandraṃ prapūjya ca /
dhruvāṇi pañca vāyavyaṃ hastaṃ prājeśavaiṣṇavaṃ //
281.d:
गृह्णीयाद्रोपयेद्वृक्षान् द्विजञ्चन्द्रं प्रपूज्य च /
ध्रुवाणि पञ्च वायव्यं हस्तं प्राजेशवैष्णवं //
281.m: Having worshipped a brāhmaṇa and the moon, one should take and plant the trees / during the five fixed nakṣatras, the windy nakṣatra (Svāti), Hasta, Prajāpati's (Rohiṇī), and Viṣṇu's (Śravaṇa).

281.s:
nakṣatrāṇi tathā mūlaṃ śasyante drumaropaṇe /
praveśayennadīvāhān puṣkariṇyāntu(2) kārayet //
:n
1 gṛhavāme iti ña..
2 puṣkariṇyāntviti pāṭho na samyak pratibhāti
:p 42
281.d:
नक्षत्राणि तथा मूलं शस्यन्ते द्रुमरोपणे /
प्रवेशयेन्नदीवाहान् पुष्करिण्यान्तु(2) कारयेत् //
:न्
1 गृहवामे इति ञ..
2 पुष्करिण्यान्त्विति पाठो न सम्यक् प्रतिभाति
:प् 42
281.m:
These lunar asterisms and Mūla are praised for planting trees. / One should cause river currents to enter and make lotus ponds.
[Footnote]
1. 'To the left of the house' in manuscript ña.
2. 'In a lotus pond' does not seem a proper reading. / [page 42]

281.s:
hastā maghā tathā maitramādyaṃ puṣyaṃ savāsavaṃ /
jalāśayasamārambhe vāruṇañcottarātrayam //
281.d:
हस्ता मघा तथा मैत्रमाद्यं पुष्यं सवासवं /
जलाशयसमारम्भे वारुणञ्चोत्तरात्रयम् //
281.m: Hasta, Maghā, Maitra (Anurādhā), Ādya (Aśvinī), Puṣya, Vāsava (Dhaniṣṭhā), / Vāruṇa (Śatabhiṣaj), and the three Uttarās (Uttaraphālgunī, Uttarāṣāḍhā, Uttarabhādrapadā) [are auspicious] when undertaking a reservoir of water.

281.s:
saṃpūjya varuṇaṃ viṣṇuṃ parjanyaṃ tat samācaret /
ariṣṭāśokapunnāgaśirīṣāḥ sapriyaṅgavaḥ //
281.d:
संपूज्य वरुणं विष्णुं पर्जन्यं तत् समाचरेत् /
अरिष्टाशोकपुन्नागशिरीषाः सप्रियङ्गवः //
281.m: Having worshipped Varuṇa, Viṣṇu, and Parjanya, one should undertake it: / soapberry, aśoka, punnāga, śirīṣa, together with priyaṅgu,

281.s:
aśokaḥ kadalī jambus tathā vakuladāḍimāḥ /
sāyaṃ prātastu gharmartau śītakāle dināntare //
281.d:
अशोकः कदली जम्बुस् तथा वकुलदाडिमाः /
सायं प्रातस्तु घर्मर्तौ शीतकाले दिनान्तरे //
281.m: aśoka, plantain, rose apple, as well as bakula and pomegranate. / In the hot season, [they should be watered] evening and morning; in the cold season, every other day;

281.s:
varṣāratrau bhuvaḥ śoṣe sektavyā ropitā drumāḥ /
uttamaṃ viṃśatirhastā madhyamaṃ ṣoḍaśāntaram //
281.d:
वर्षारत्रौ भुवः शोषे सेक्तव्या रोपिता द्रुमाः /
उत्तमं विंशतिर्हस्ता मध्यमं षोडशान्तरम् //
281.m: in the rainy season, when the earth is dry, the planted trees must be watered. / An interval of twenty cubits is best, sixteen is middling,

281.s:
sthānāt sthānāntaraṃ kāryaṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ dvādaśāvaraṃ /
viphalāḥ syurghanā vṛkṣāḥ śastreṇādau hi śodhanam //
281.d:
स्थानात् स्थानान्तरं कार्यं वृक्षाणां द्वादशावरं /
विफलाः स्युर्घना वृक्षाः शस्त्रेणादौ हि शोधनम् //
281.m: and twelve from place to place is the least for trees. / Densely planted trees become fruitless; first, indeed, cleansing with a weapon [is done].

281.s:
viḍaṅgaghṛtapaṅkāktān secayecchītavāriṇā /
phalanāśe kulathaiś ca māsair mudgair yavaistilaiḥ //
281.d:
विडङ्गघृतपङ्काक्तान् सेचयेच्छीतवारिणा /
फलनाशे कुलथैश् च मासैर् मुद्गैर् यवैस्तिलैः //
281.m: One should sprinkle with cold water those smeared with viḍaṅga, ghee, and mud. / When fruit is lost, [watering] with horse-gram, black gram, mung bean, barley, and sesamum,

281.s:
ghṛtaśītapayaḥsekaḥ phalapuṣpāya sarvadā /
āvikājaśakṛccūrṇam yavacūrṇaṃ tilāni ca //
281.d:
घृतशीतपयःसेकः फलपुष्पाय सर्वदा /
आविकाजशकृच्चूर्णम् यवचूर्णं तिलानि च //
281.m: and sprinkling with ghee and cold milk always brings about fruit and flowers. / Powdered sheep and goat dung, barley powder, and sesamum seeds,

281.s:
gomāṃsamudakañcaiva saptarātraṃ nidhāpayet /
utsekaḥ sarvavṛkṣāṇāṃ phalapuṣpādivṛddhidaḥ //
281.d:
गोमांसमुदकञ्चैव सप्तरात्रं निधापयेत् /
उत्सेकः सर्ववृक्षाणां फलपुष्पादिवृद्धिदः //
281.m: beef, and water should be kept set aside for seven nights; / this effusion causes an increase of fruits, flowers, and the like in all trees.

281.s:
matsyāmbhasā tu sekena vṛddhirbhavati śākhinaḥ /
viḍaṅgataṇḍulopetaṃ matsyaṃ māṃsaṃ hi dohadaṃ /
sarveṣāmaviśeṣeṇa vṛkṣāṇāṃ rogamardanam //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe vṛkṣāyurvedo
nāmaikāśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:p 43
:ś atha dvyaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
nānārogaharāṇyauṣadhāni
281.d:
मत्स्याम्भसा तु सेकेन वृद्धिर्भवति शाखिनः /
विडङ्गतण्डुलोपेतं मत्स्यं मांसं हि दोहदं /
सर्वेषामविशेषेण वृक्षाणां रोगमर्दनम् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे वृक्षायुर्वेदो
नामैकाशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:प् 43
:श् अथ द्व्यशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
नानारोगहराण्यौषधानि
281.m:
By sprinkling with fish-water, growth of the tree occurs. / Fish and meat mixed with viḍaṅga and rice grains are a fertilizer (dohada) / that removes disease from all trees without exception.
Thus ends the two hundred and eighty-first chapter in the great Agni Purāṇa, named 'Arbori-horticulture'.
[page 43]
Now begins the two hundred and eighty-second chapter.
Medicines that cure various diseases.

282.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
siṃhī śaṭī(1) niśāyugmaṃ vatsakaṃ kvāthasevanaṃ /
śiśoḥ sarvātisāreṣu stanyadoṣeṣu śasyate //
282.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
सिंही शटी(1) निशायुग्मं वत्सकं क्वाथसेवनं /
शिशोः सर्वातिसारेषु स्तन्यदोषेषु शस्यते //
282.m:
Dhanvantari said:
Bṛhatī, śaṭī, the two kinds of turmeric, and kutaja—drinking a decoction of these / is commended for all kinds of diarrhea in a child, and for disorders caused by [vitiated] mother's milk.

282.s:
śṛṅgīṃ sakṛṣṇātiviṣāṃ cūrṇitāṃ madhunā lihet /
ekā cātiviśā kāśacchardijvaraharī śiśoḥ //
282.d:
शृङ्गीं सकृष्णातिविषां चूर्णितां मधुना लिहेत् /
एका चातिविशा काशच्छर्दिज्वरहरी शिशोः //
282.m: One should lick karkaṭaśṛṅgī combined with pippalī and ativiṣā, pulverized and mixed with honey; / and ativiṣā alone cures cough, vomiting, and fever in a child.

282.s:
bālaiḥ sevyā vacā sājyā sadugdhā vātha tailayuk /
yaṣṭikāṃ śaṅkhapuṣpīṃ vā bālaḥ kṣīrānvitāṃ pivet //
282.d:
बालैः सेव्या वचा साज्या सदुग्धा वाथ तैलयुक् /
यष्टिकां शङ्खपुष्पीं वा बालः क्षीरान्वितां पिवेत् //
282.m: Vacā mixed with ghee, or with milk, or accompanied by oil, should be taken by children. / Or a child should drink yaṣṭīmadhu or śaṅkhapuṣpī combined with milk.

282.s:
vāgrūpasampadyuktāyurmedhāśrīrvardhate śiśoḥ /
vacāhyagniśikhāvāsāśuṇṭhīkṛṣṇāniśāgadaṃ //
282.d:
वाग्रूपसम्पद्युक्तायुर्मेधाश्रीर्वर्धते शिशोः /
वचाह्यग्निशिखावासाशुण्ठीकृष्णानिशागदं //
282.m: The child's longevity, intellect, prosperity, and wealth of eloquence and beauty will increase. / Vacā, agniśikhā, vāsā, ginger, pippalī, turmeric, and kuṣṭha,

282.s:
sayaṣṭisaindhavaṃ bālaḥ prātarmedhākaraṃ pivet /
devadārumahāśigruphalatrayapayomucāṃ //
282.d:
सयष्टिसैन्धवं बालः प्रातर्मेधाकरं पिवेत् /
देवदारुमहाशिग्रुफलत्रयपयोमुचां //
282.m: along with yaṣṭīmadhu and rock salt, a child should drink in the morning to produce intellect. / A decoction of devadāru, mahāśigru, the three fruits (triphalā), and mustā,

282.s:
kvāthaḥ sakṛṣṇā mṛdvīkā kalkaḥ sarvān kṛmīnharet /
triphalābhṛṅgaviśvānāṃ raseṣu madhusarpiṣoḥ //
282.d:
क्वाथः सकृष्णा मृद्वीका कल्कः सर्वान् कृमीन्हरेत् /
त्रिफलाभृङ्गविश्वानां रसेषु मधुसर्पिषोः //
282.m: [or] a paste of them with pippalī and raisins, removes all worms. / [A preparation] processed in the juices of triphalā, bhṛṅgarāja, and ginger, along with honey and ghee,

282.s:
meṣīkṣīre ca gomūtre siktaṃ roge hitaṃ śiśoḥ /
nāsāraktaharo nasyāddurvārasa ihottamaḥ //
282.d:
मेषीक्षीरे च गोमूत्रे सिक्तं रोगे हितं शिशोः /
नासारक्तहरो नस्याद्दुर्वारस इहोत्तमः //
282.m: and mixed with ewe's milk and cow's urine, is beneficial in childhood diseases. / Juice of dūrvā grass administered as an errhine is the best here for stopping nasal hemorrhage.

282.s:
laśunārdrakaśigrūṇāṃ rasaḥ karṇasya pūraṇam /
tailamārdrakajātyaṃ vā śūlahā(2) cauṣṭharoganut(3) //
:n
1 siṃhī ṣaṣṭīti kha..
2 śūlahā ity atra puṃstvanirdeśa ārṣaḥ
3 mūtrahā śoṣaroganuditi ña..
:p 44
282.d:
लशुनार्द्रकशिग्रूणां रसः कर्णस्य पूरणम् /
तैलमार्द्रकजात्यं वा शूलहा(2) चौष्ठरोगनुत्(3) //
:न्
1 सिंही षष्टीति ख..
2 शूलहा इत्य् अत्र पुंस्त्वनिर्देश आर्षः
3 मूत्रहा शोषरोगनुदिति ञ..
:प् 44
282.m:
The juice of garlic, ginger, and śigru is used for filling the ear; / or an oil prepared with fresh ginger relieves earache and removes diseases of the lips.
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript kha, "siṃhī ṣaṣṭī".
2. Here, the masculine inflection in 'śūlahā' is an archaic (ārṣa) usage.
3. In manuscript ña, "mūtrahā śoṣaroganud". / [Page 44]

282.s:
jātīpatraṃ phalaṃ vyoṣaṃ kavalaṃ mūtrakaṃ niśā /
dugdhakvāthe 'bhayākalke siddhaṃ tailaṃ dvijārtinut //
282.d:
जातीपत्रं फलं व्योषं कवलं मूत्रकं निशा /
दुग्धक्वाथे ऽभयाकल्के सिद्धं तैलं द्विजार्तिनुत् //
282.m: Jasmine leaf, nut-meg, the three pungents, [used as] a mouth rinse with cow's urine and turmeric; / oil processed in a decoction of milk with a paste of harītakī removes toothache.

282.s:
dhānyāmbu nārikelaṃ gomūtraṃ kramūkaviśvayuk /
kvāthitaṃ kabalaṃ kāryamadhijihvādhiśāntaye //
282.d:
धान्याम्बु नारिकेलं गोमूत्रं क्रमूकविश्वयुक् /
क्वाथितं कबलं कार्यमधिजिह्वाधिशान्तये //
282.m: Coriander water, coconut water, and cow's urine with betel nut and dry ginger, / boiled and used as a gargle, should be applied to pacify ranula (adhijihvikā).

282.s:
sādhitaṃ lāṅgalīkalke tailaṃ nirguṇḍikārasaiḥ /
gaṇḍamālāgalagaṇḍau nāśayennasyakarmaṇā //
282.d:
साधितं लाङ्गलीकल्के तैलं निर्गुण्डिकारसैः /
गण्डमालागलगण्डौ नाशयेन्नस्यकर्मणा //
282.m: Oil prepared with a paste of lāṅgalī in the juice of nirguṇḍī / destroys cervical lymphadenitis and goiter by means of an errhine procedure.

282.s:
pallavair arkapūtīkasnuhīrugghātajātikaiḥ /
udvartayet sagomūtraḥ sarvatvagdoṣanāśanaiḥ //
282.d:
पल्लवैर् अर्कपूतीकस्नुहीरुग्घातजातिकैः /
उद्वर्तयेत् सगोमूत्रः सर्वत्वग्दोषनाशनैः //
282.m: With tender leaves of arka, pūtīka, snuhī, karañja, and jātī / together with cow's urine, one should perform anointment, which cures all skin diseases.

282.s:
vākucī satilā bhuktā vatsarāt kuṣṭhanāśanī /
pathyā bhallātakī tailaguḍapiṇḍī tu kuṣṭhajit //
282.d:
वाकुची सतिला भुक्ता वत्सरात् कुष्ठनाशनी /
पथ्या भल्लातकी तैलगुडपिण्डी तु कुष्ठजित् //
282.m: Bākučī eaten with sesame destroys leprosy after one year. / But a paste-ball of harītakī, bhallātaka, oil, and jaggery conquers leprosy.

282.s:
pūtīkavahnirajanī triphalāvyoṣacūrṇayuk /
takraṃ gudāṅkure peyaṃ bhakṣyā vā saguḍābhayā //
282.d:
पूतीकवह्निरजनी त्रिफलाव्योषचूर्णयुक् /
तक्रं गुदाङ्कुरे पेयं भक्ष्या वा सगुडाभया //
282.m: Buttermilk combined with powder of pūtīka, citraka, turmeric, triphalā, and the three pungents / should be drunk for piles, or harītakī eaten with jaggery.

282.s:
phaladārvīviṣāṇāntu kvātho dhātrīraso 'thavā /
pātavyo rajanīkalkaḥ kṣaudrākṣaudrapramehiṇā //
282.d:
फलदार्वीविषाणान्तु क्वाथो धात्रीरसो ऽथवा /
पातव्यो रजनीकल्कः क्षौद्राक्षौद्रप्रमेहिणा //
282.m: A decoction of the three fruits, dāruharidrā, and ativiṣā, or āmalakī juice, / or a paste of turmeric should be drunk with honey by one suffering from urinary disorder (prameha).

282.s:
vāsāgarbho vyādhighātakvātha eraṇḍatailayuk /
vātaśoṇitahṛt pānāt pippalī syāt plīhāharī //
282.d:
वासागर्भो व्याधिघातक्वाथ एरण्डतैलयुक् /
वातशोणितहृत् पानात् पिप्पली स्यात् प्लीहाहरी //
282.m: A decoction of vyādhighāta (āragvadha) containing a paste of vāsā, mixed with castor oil / and drunk, cures gout (vātarakta); pippalī removes splenic disease.

282.s:
sevyā jaṭhariṇā kṛṣṇā snukṣīravahubhāvitā /
payo vā racyadantyāgniviḍaṅgavyoṣakalkayuk //
282.d:
सेव्या जठरिणा कृष्णा स्नुक्षीरवहुभाविता /
पयो वा रच्यदन्त्याग्निविडङ्गव्योषकल्कयुक् //
282.m: Pippalī soaked many times in the milky latex of snuhī should be taken by one with abdominal enlargement, / or milk combined with the paste of pleasing dantī, citraka, viḍaṅga, and the three pungents.

282.s:
granthikogrābhayā kṛṣṇā viḍaṅgāktā ghṛte sthitā /
sāṃsantakraṃ grahaṇyarśaḥpāṇḍugulmakṛmīn haret //
282.d:
ग्रन्थिकोग्राभया कृष्णा विडङ्गाक्ता घृते स्थिता /
सांसन्तक्रं ग्रहण्यर्शःपाण्डुगुल्मकृमीन् हरेत् //
282.m: Pippalīmūla, vacā, harītakī, and pippalī smeared with viḍaṅga and kept in ghee, / [taken] with meat soup and buttermilk, cures sprue, piles, anemia, abdominal tumors, and worms.

282.s:
phalatrayāmṛtā vāsā tiktabhūnimbajas tathā /
kvāthaḥ samākṣiko hanyāt pāṇḍurogaṃ sakāmalaṃ //
282.d:
फलत्रयामृता वासा तिक्तभूनिम्बजस् तथा /
क्वाथः समाक्षिको हन्यात् पाण्डुरोगं सकामलं //
282.m: A decoction of the three fruits, guḍūcī, vāsā, and kirātatikta / mixed with honey destroys anemia along with jaundice.

282.s:
raktapittī pivedvāsāsurasaṃ sasitaṃ madhu /
:p 45
varīdrākṣābalāśuṇṭhīsādhitaṃ vā payaḥ pṛthak //
282.d:
रक्तपित्ती पिवेद्वासासुरसं ससितं मधु /
:प् 45
वरीद्राक्षाबलाशुण्ठीसाधितं वा पयः पृथक् //
282.m:
One suffering from internal hemorrhage should drink the juice of vāsā with sugar and honey,
[Page 45]
or milk separately prepared with śatāvarī, grapes, balā, and dry ginger.

282.s:
varī vidārī pathyā balātrayaṃ savāsakaṃ /
śvadaṃṣṭrāmadhusarpirbhyāmālihet kṣayarogavān //
282.d:
वरी विदारी पथ्या बलात्रयं सवासकं /
श्वदंष्ट्रामधुसर्पिर्भ्यामालिहेत् क्षयरोगवान् //
282.m: Śatāvarī, vidārī, harītakī, the three kinds of balā along with vāsā, / and gokṣura—one suffering from consumption should lick these with honey and ghee.

282.s:
pathyāśigrukarañjārkatvaksāraṃ madhusindhumat /
samūtraṃ vidradhiṃ hanti paripākāya tantrajit //
282.d:
पथ्याशिग्रुकरञ्जार्कत्वक्सारं मधुसिन्धुमत् /
समूत्रं विद्रधिं हन्ति परिपाकाय तन्त्रजित् //
282.m: The bark-pith of harītakī, śigru, karañja, and arka, with honey and rock salt, / along with cow's urine, cures abscess; expertly applied, it brings about suppuration.

282.s:
trivṛtā jīvatī dantī mañjiṣṭhā śarvarīdvayaṃ /
tārkṣajaṃ nimbapatrañca lepaḥ śasto bhagandare //
282.d:
त्रिवृता जीवती दन्ती मञ्जिष्ठा शर्वरीद्वयं /
तार्क्षजं निम्बपत्रञ्च लेपः शस्तो भगन्दरे //
282.m: Trivṛt, jīvantī, dantī, mañjiṣṭhā, the two kinds of turmeric, / rasāñjana, and neem leaves—a plaster [of these] is commended in fistula-in-ano.

282.s:
rugghātajanīlākṣācūrṇājakṣaudrasaṃyutā /
vāsovattirvraṇe yojyā śodhanī gatināśanī //
282.d:
रुग्घातजनीलाक्षाचूर्णाजक्षौद्रसंयुता /
वासोवत्तिर्व्रणे योज्या शोधनी गतिनाशनी //
282.m: A cloth wick smeared with goat's milk and honey, along with the powder of āragvadha, turmeric, and lac, / should be applied to a wound to purify it and destroy sinus tracts.

282.s:
śyāmāyaṣṭiniśālodhrapadmakotpalacandanaiḥ /
samarīcaiḥ śṛtaṃ tailaṃ kṣīre syādbraṇarohaṇaṃ //
282.d:
श्यामायष्टिनिशालोध्रपद्मकोत्पलचन्दनैः /
समरीचैः शृतं तैलं क्षीरे स्याद्ब्रणरोहणं //
282.m: Oil boiled with milk, along with priyaṅgu, yaṣṭīmadhu, turmeric, lodhra, padmaka, blue lotus, sandalwood, / and black pepper, brings about the healing of wounds.

282.s:
śrīkārpāsadalair bhasmaphalopalavaṇā niśā /
tatpiṇḍīsvedanaṃ tāmre satailaṃ syāt kṣatauṣadhaṃ //
282.d:
श्रीकार्पासदलैर् भस्मफलोपलवणा निशा /
तत्पिण्डीस्वेदनं ताम्रे सतैलं स्यात् क्षतौषधं //
282.m: Ash of sacred cotton leaves, bibhītaka, and rock salt, along with turmeric— / fomentation with that paste-ball in a copper vessel, with oil, is the medicine for cuts.

282.s:
kumbhīsāraṃ payoyuktaṃ vahnidagdhaṃ vraṇe lipet /
tadeva nāśayetsekānnārikelarajoghṛtam //
282.d:
कुम्भीसारं पयोयुक्तं वह्निदग्धं व्रणे लिपेत् /
तदेव नाशयेत्सेकान्नारिकेलरजोघृतम् //
282.m: One should apply to a wound the pith of kumbhī mixed with milk, charred in fire; / [or] coconut powder mixed with ghee destroys the same when applied as an irrigation.

282.s:
viṣvājamodasindhūtthaciñcātvagbhiḥ samābhayā /
takreṇoṣṇāmbunā vātha pītātīsāranāśanī //
282.d:
विष्वाजमोदसिन्धूत्थचिञ्चात्वग्भिः समाभया /
तक्रेणोष्णाम्बुना वाथ पीतातीसारनाशनी //
282.m: Harītakī combined equally with dry ginger, ajamodā, rock salt, and tamarind bark, / drunk with buttermilk or warm water, destroys diarrhea.

282.s:
vatsakātiviṣāviśvavillamustaśṛtaṃ jalaṃ /
sāme purāṇe 'tīsāre sāmṛkśūle ca pāyayet //
282.d:
वत्सकातिविषाविश्वविल्लमुस्तशृतं जलं /
सामे पुराणे ऽतीसारे सामृक्शूले च पाययेत् //
282.m: Water boiled with indrayava, ativiṣā, dry ginger, bael fruit, and mustā, / one should administer in acute or chronic diarrhea, and in colic accompanied by mucous and blood.

282.s:
aṅgāradagdhaṃ sugataṃ sindhumuṣṇāmbunā pivet /
śūlavānatha vā taddhi sindhuhiṃgukaṇābhayā //
282.d:
अङ्गारदग्धं सुगतं सिन्धुमुष्णाम्बुना पिवेत् /
शूलवानथ वा तद्धि सिन्धुहिंगुकणाभया //
282.m: Burned on embers and purified, one should drink rock salt with warm water / when suffering from colic; or likewise that rock salt, asafoetida, pippalī, and harītakī.

282.s:
kaṭurohotkaṇātaṅkalājacūrṇaṃ(1) madhuplutaṃ /
:n
1 kaṭurohotpalātaṅkalājacūrṇamiti ṭa..
:p 46
vastracchidragataṃ vaktre nyastaṃ tṛṣṇāṃ vināśayet //
282.d:
कटुरोहोत्कणातङ्कलाजचूर्णं(1) मधुप्लुतं /
:न्
1 कटुरोहोत्पलातङ्कलाजचूर्णमिति ट..
:प् 46
वस्त्रच्छिद्रगतं वक्त्रे न्यस्तं तृष्णां विनाशयेत् //
282.m:
Powder of kaṭukā, utpalikā, and puffed paddy steeped in honey,
[Footnote]
1. In manuscript ṭa, "kaṭurohotpalātaṅkalājacūrṇam". / [Page 46]
placed inside a cloth pouch and held in the mouth, destroys thirst.

282.s:
pāṭhādārvījātidalaṃ drākṣāmūlaphalatrayaiḥ(1) /
sādhitaṃ samadhu kvāthaṃ kavalaṃ mukhapāpahṛt //
282.d:
पाठादार्वीजातिदलं द्राक्षामूलफलत्रयैः(1) /
साधितं समधु क्वाथं कवलं मुखपापहृत् //
282.m: Pāṭhā, dāruharidrā, jasmine leaf, grapes, root of [eranda?], and the three fruits, / prepared as a decoction and held as a gargle with honey, cures diseases of the mouth.

282.s:
kṛṣṇātiviṣatiktendradārūpāṭhāpayomucāṃ /
kvātho mūtre śṛtaḥ kṣaudrī sarvakaṇṭhagadāpahaḥ //
282.d:
कृष्णातिविषतिक्तेन्द्रदारूपाठापयोमुचां /
क्वाथो मूत्रे शृतः क्षौद्री सर्वकण्ठगदापहः //
282.m: A decoction of pippalī, ativiṣā, tikta, indrayava, devadāru, pāṭhā, and mustā, / boiled in cow's urine and mixed with honey, removes all throat disorders.

282.s:
pathyāgokṣuradusparśarājavṛkṣaśilābhidāṃ /
kaṣāyaḥ samadhuḥ pīto mūtrakṛcchraṃ vyapohati //
282.d:
पथ्यागोक्षुरदुस्पर्शराजवृक्षशिलाभिदां /
कषायः समधुः पीतो मूत्रकृच्छ्रं व्यपोहति //
282.m: A decoction of harītakī, gokṣura, yavāsa, āragvadha, and pāsāṇabheda, / drunk with honey, dispels painful micturition.

282.s:
vaṃśatvagvaruṇakvāthaḥ śarkarāśmavighātanaḥ /
śākhoṭakvāthasakṣaudrakṣīrāśī ślīpadī bhavet //
282.d:
वंशत्वग्वरुणक्वाथः शर्कराश्मविघातनः /
शाखोटक्वाथसक्षौद्रक्षीराशी श्लीपदी भवेत् //
282.m: A decoction of bamboo bark and varuṇa destroys gravel and urinary calculi. / One drinking a decoction of śākhoṭaka with honey and living on milk will overcome elephantiasis.

282.s:
māsārkatvakpayastailaṃ madhusiktañca saindhavaṃ /
pādarogaṃ haretsarpirjālakukkuṭajaṃ tathā //
282.d:
मासार्कत्वक्पयस्तैलं मधुसिक्तञ्च सैन्धवं /
पादरोगं हरेत्सर्पिर्जालकुक्कुटजं तथा //
282.m: Milk of arka, black gram, bark, milk, and oil, with beeswax and rock salt, / destroys foot disease; likewise ghee [processed with] jālakukkuṭa.

282.s:
śuṇṭhīsīvarcalāhiṅgucūrṇaṃ śūṇṭhīrasair ghṛtam /
rujaṃ haredatha kvātho viddhi baddhāgnisādhane //
282.d:
शुण्ठीसीवर्चलाहिङ्गुचूर्णं शूण्ठीरसैर् घृतम् /
रुजं हरेदथ क्वाथो विद्धि बद्धाग्निसाधने //
282.m: Powder of dry ginger, sauvarcala salt, and asafoetida, [taken with] ghee and ginger juice, / relieves pain; and know this decoction to be effective for rekindling suppressed digestive fire.

282.s:
sauvarcalāgnihiṅgūnāṃ sadīpyānāṃ rasair yutaṃ /
viḍadīpyakayuktaṃ vā takraṃ gulmāturaḥ pivet //
282.d:
सौवर्चलाग्निहिङ्गूनां सदीप्यानां रसैर् युतं /
विडदीप्यकयुक्तं वा तक्रं गुल्मातुरः पिवेत् //
282.m: A patient suffering from abdominal tumor should drink buttermilk combined with the juices of / sauvarcala salt, citraka, asafoetida, and ajamodā, or mixed with viḍa salt and ajamodā.

282.s:
dhātrīpaṭolamudgānāṃ kvāthaḥ sājyo visarpahā /
śuṇṭhīdārunavākṣīrakvātho mūtrānvito 'paraḥ //
282.d:
धात्रीपटोलमुद्गानां क्वाथः साज्यो विसर्पहा /
शुण्ठीदारुनवाक्षीरक्वाथो मूत्रान्वितो ऽपरः //
282.m: A decoction of āmalakī, paṭola, and mudga beans, with ghee, cures erysipelas. / Another [remedy] is a decoction of ginger, devadāru, and fresh milk, combined with cow's urine.

282.s:
savyoṣāyorajaḥkṣāraḥ phalakvāthaś ca śothahṛt /
guḍaśigrutrivṛddhiś ca saindhavānāṃ rajoyutaḥ //
282.d:
सव्योषायोरजःक्षारः फलक्वाथश् च शोथहृत् /
गुडशिग्रुत्रिवृद्धिश् च सैन्धवानां रजोयुतः //
282.m: A decoction of the three fruits with the three pungents, iron powder, and alkali relieves dropsy; / as does jaggery, śigru, and trivṛt combined with the powder of rock salt.

282.s:
trivṛtāphalakakvāthaḥ saguḍaḥ syādvirecanaḥ /
vacāphalakaṣāyotthaṃ payo vamanakṛbhavet //
282.d:
त्रिवृताफलकक्वाथः सगुडः स्याद्विरेचनः /
वचाफलकषायोत्थं पयो वमनकृभवेत् //
282.m: A decoction of trivṛt and [harītakī] fruit with jaggery serves as a purgative. / Milk prepared from a decoction of vacā and madana fruit causes vomiting.

282.s:
triphalāyāḥ palaśataṃ pṛthagbhṛṅgajabhāvitam /
:n
1 drākṣāmṛtaphalatrayair iti ña.. , ṭa.. ca
:p 47
viḍaṅgaṃ lohacūrṇañca daśabhāgasamanvitam //
282.d:
त्रिफलायाः पलशतं पृथग्भृङ्गजभावितम् /
:न्
1 द्राक्षामृतफलत्रयैर् इति ञ.. , ट.. च
:प् 47
विडङ्गं लोहचूर्णञ्च दशभागसमन्वितम् //
282.m:
One hundred palas of triphalā, each separately macerated in bhṛṅgarāja juice,
[Footnote]
1. In manuscripts ña and ṭa, "drākṣāmṛtaphalatrayaiḥ". / [Page 47]
combined with a tenth part of viḍaṅga and iron powder,

282.s:
śatāvarīguḍucyagnipalānāṃ śataviṃśatiḥ(1) /
madhvājyatilajair lihyādbalīpalitavarjitaḥ //
282.d:
शतावरीगुडुच्यग्निपलानां शतविंशतिः(1) /
मध्वाज्यतिलजैर् लिह्याद्बलीपलितवर्जितः //
282.m: [and] one hundred and twenty palas each of śatāvarī, guḍūcī, and citraka, / one should lick with honey, ghee, and sesame oil: he is freed from wrinkles and gray hair,

282.s:
śatamabdaṃ hi jīveta sarvarogavivarjitaḥ /
triphalā sarvarogaghnī samadhuḥ śarkvarānvitā //
282.d:
शतमब्दं हि जीवेत सर्वरोगविवर्जितः /
त्रिफला सर्वरोगघ्नी समधुः शर्क्वरान्विता //
282.m: and lives for a hundred years, completely free from all diseases. / Triphalā cures all diseases when accompanied by honey and sugar.

282.s:
sitāmadhughṛtair yuktā sakṛṣṇā triphalā tathā /
pathyācitrakaśuṇṭhāś ca guḍucīmuṣalīrajaḥ //
282.d:
सितामधुघृतैर् युक्ता सकृष्णा त्रिफला तथा /
पथ्याचित्रकशुण्ठाश् च गुडुचीमुषलीरजः //
282.m: Likewise, triphalā mixed with sugar candy, honey, and ghee, along with pippalī. / Harītakī, citraka, dry ginger, guḍūcī, and powder of muśalī,

282.s:
saguḍaṃ bhakṣitaṃ rogaharaṃ triśatavarṣakṛt /
kiñciccūrṇaṃ javāpuṣpaṃ piṇḍitaṃ visṛjejjale //
282.d:
सगुडं भक्षितं रोगहरं त्रिशतवर्षकृत् /
किञ्चिच्चूर्णं जवापुष्पं पिण्डितं विसृजेज्जले //
282.m: eaten with jaggery, cures diseases and makes one live three hundred years. / A little powder of hibiscus flower made into a ball should be placed in water.

282.s:
tailaṃ bhaved ghṛtākāraṃ kiñciccūrṇaṃ jalānvitaṃ /
dhūpārthaṃ dṛśyate citraṃ vṛṣadaṃśajarāyunā //
282.d:
तैलं भवेद् घृताकारं किञ्चिच्चूर्णं जलान्वितं /
धूपार्थं दृश्यते चित्रं वृषदंशजरायुना //
282.m: The oil becomes like clarified butter; [and] a little powder mixed with water, / for the purpose of incense, appears wonderful together with the placenta of a cat.

282.s:
punarmākṣikadhūpena dṛśyate tadyathā purā /
karpūrajalakābhekatailaṃ(2) pāṭalimūlayuk //
282.d:
पुनर्माक्षिकधूपेन दृश्यते तद्यथा पुरा /
कर्पूरजलकाभेकतैलं(2) पाटलिमूलयुक् //
282.m: Again, with the fumes of honey, it appears as it was before. / Oil of camphor, leech, and frog mixed with the root of pāṭalī,

282.s:
piṣṭvā lipya pade dve ca caredaṅgārake naraḥ /
tṛṇautthānādikaṃ vyūhya darśayanvai kutūhalaṃ //
282.d:
पिष्ट्वा लिप्य पदे द्वे च चरेदङ्गारके नरः /
तृणौत्थानादिकं व्यूह्य दर्शयन्वै कुतूहलं //
282.m: having been ground and smeared on both feet, a man may walk upon burning coals, / tossing about grass, straw, and the like, showing indeed a wonder.

282.s:
viṣagraharujadhvaṃsakṣudranarma ca kāmikaṃ /
tatte ṣaṭkarmakaṃ proktaṃ siddhidvayasamāśrayaṃ //
282.d:
विषग्रहरुजध्वंसक्षुद्रनर्म च कामिकं /
तत्ते षट्कर्मकं प्रोक्तं सिद्धिद्वयसमाश्रयं //
282.m: Destruction of poison, planetary afflictions, and diseases, small entertainments, and rituals performed according to desire: / that is declared to you as the six acts, which rest upon the two kinds of supernatural power.

282.s:
mantradhyānauṣadhikathāmudrejyā yatra muṣṭayaḥ /
caturvargaphalaṃ proktaṃ yaḥ paṭhetsa divaṃ vrajet //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe nānārogaharāṇyauṣadhāni nāma
dvyaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
:n
1 pañcaviśatiriti ña.. , ṭa.. ca
2 karpūrajahukātailamiti kha.. / karpūrajānukātailamiti ja..
:p 48
:ś atha tryaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
mantrarūpauṣadhakathanaṃ
282.d:
मन्त्रध्यानौषधिकथामुद्रेज्या यत्र मुष्टयः /
चतुर्वर्गफलं प्रोक्तं यः पठेत्स दिवं व्रजेत् //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे नानारोगहराण्यौषधानि नाम
द्व्यशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः ||
:न्
1 पञ्चविशतिरिति ञ.. , ट.. च
2 कर्पूरजहुकातैलमिति ख.. / कर्पूरजानुकातैलमिति ज..
:प् 48
:श् अथ त्र्यशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
मन्त्ररूपौषधकथनं
282.m:
Where mantras, meditation, talk of herbs, ritual gestures, worship, and medicinal handfuls [are taught], / the fruit of the four goals of life is declared; whoever recites it goes to heaven.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and eighty-second chapter, called “Remedies That Remove Various Diseases.”
[Notes]
1. "pañcaviśatiḥ" in manuscripts ña and ṭa.
2. "karpūrajahukātailam" in manuscript kha; "karpūrajānukātailam" in manuscript ja. / [Page 48]
Now begins the two hundred and eighty-third chapter.
Account of Remedies in the Form of Mantras.

283.s:
dhanvantarir uvāca
āyurārogyakartara oṃkāradyāś ca nākadāḥ /
oṃkāraḥ paramo mantrastaṃ japtvā cāmaro bhavet //
283.d:
धन्वन्तरिर् उवाच
आयुरारोग्यकर्तर ओंकारद्याश् च नाकदाः /
ओंकारः परमो मन्त्रस्तं जप्त्वा चामरो भवेत् //
283.m: Dhanvantari said: / The bringers of longevity and health, beginning with Oṃkāra, also grant heaven. / Oṃkāra is the supreme mantra; having recited it, one becomes immortal.

283.s:
gāyatrī paramo mantrastaṃ japtvā bhuktimuktibhāk /
oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya mantraḥ sarvārthasādhakaḥ //
283.d:
गायत्री परमो मन्त्रस्तं जप्त्वा भुक्तिमुक्तिभाक् /
ओं नमो नारायणाय मन्त्रः सर्वार्थसाधकः //
283.m: The Gāyatrī is the supreme mantra; having recited it, one attains worldly enjoyment and liberation. / The mantra "oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya" accomplishes all aims.

283.s:
oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya sarvadaḥ /
oṃ hūṃ namo viṣṇave mantroyañcauṣadhaṃ paraṃ //
283.d:
ओं नमो भगवते वासुदेवाय सर्वदः /
ओं हूं नमो विष्णवे मन्त्रोयञ्चौषधं परं //
283.m: "oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya" bestows everything. / The mantra "oṃ hūṃ namo viṣṇave" is the supreme medicine.

283.s:
anena devā hy asurāḥ saśriyo nirujo 'bhavat /
bhūtānāmupakāraś ca tathā dharmo mahauṣadham //
283.d:
अनेन देवा ह्य् असुराः सश्रियो निरुजो ऽभवत् /
भूतानामुपकारश् च तथा धर्मो महौषधम् //
283.m: By this, the gods and asuras became endowed with prosperity and free from disease; / and helping living beings, as well as righteousness, is the great remedy.

283.s:
dharmaḥ saddharmakṛddharmī etair dharmaiś ca nirmalaḥ /
śrīdaḥ śrīṣaḥ śrīnivāsaḥ śrīdharaḥśrīniketanaḥ //
283.d:
धर्मः सद्धर्मकृद्धर्मी एतैर् धर्मैश् च निर्मलः /
श्रीदः श्रीषः श्रीनिवासः श्रीधरःश्रीनिकेतनः //
283.m: "Dharma," "Saddharmakṛt," "Dharmī": and through these righteous names, one becomes spotless. / "Śrīda," "Śrīśa," "Śrīnivāsa," "Śrīdhara," "Śrīniketana,"

283.s:
śriyaḥ patiḥ śrīparama etaiḥ śriyamavāpnuyāt /
kāmī kāmapradaḥ kāmaḥ kāmapālas tathā hariḥ //
283.d:
श्रियः पतिः श्रीपरम एतैः श्रियमवाप्नुयात् /
कामी कामप्रदः कामः कामपालस् तथा हरिः //
283.m: "Śriyaḥpati," "Śrīparama": through these [names] one attains prosperity. / "Kāmī," "Kāmaprada," "Kāma," "Kāmapāla," as well as "Hari,"

283.s:
ānando mādhavaś caiva nāma kāmāya vai hareḥ /
rāmaḥ paraśurāmaś ca nṛsiṃho viṣṇureva ca //
283.d:
आनन्दो माधवश् चैव नाम कामाय वै हरेः /
रामः परशुरामश् च नृसिंहो विष्णुरेव च //
283.m: "Ānanda," and "Mādhava": these indeed are the names of Hari for desire. / "Rāma," "Paraśurāma," "Nṛsiṃha," and "Viṣṇu,"

283.s:
trivikramaś ca nāmāni japtavyāni jigīṣubhiḥ /
vidyāmabhyasyatāṃ nityaṃ japtavyaḥ puruṣottamaḥ //
283.d:
त्रिविक्रमश् च नामानि जप्तव्यानि जिगीषुभिः /
विद्यामभ्यस्यतां नित्यं जप्तव्यः पुरुषोत्तमः //
283.m: and "Trivikrama": these names should be recited by those wishing for victory. / For those studying learning, "Puruṣottama" should be recited constantly.

283.s:
dāmodaro bandhaharaḥ puṣkarākṣo 'kṣiroganut /
hṛṣīkeśo bhayaharo japedauṣadhakarmaṇi //
:p 49
283.d:
दामोदरो बन्धहरः पुष्कराक्षो ऽक्षिरोगनुत् /
हृषीकेशो भयहरो जपेदौषधकर्मणि //
:प् 49
283.m:
"Dāmodara" removes bondage; "Puṣkarākṣa" removes eye disease; / "Hṛṣīkeśa" removes fear; one should recite [these] in medicinal treatments.
[Page 49]

283.s:
acyutañcāmṛtaṃ mantraṃ saṅgrāme cāparājitaḥ /
jalatāre nārasiṃhaṃ pūrvādau kṣemakāmavān //
283.d:
अच्युतञ्चामृतं मन्त्रं सङ्ग्रामे चापराजितः /
जलतारे नारसिंहं पूर्वादौ क्षेमकामवान् //
283.m: And "Acyuta" is the deathless mantra; and in battle one is undefeated [by reciting it]. / In crossing water, one desiring safety [should recite] "Nārasimha" at the beginning, toward the east, and so forth.

283.s:
cakriṇaṅgadinañcaiva śārṅgiṇaṃ khaḍginaṃ smaret /
nārāyaṇaṃ sarvakāle nṛsiṃho 'khilabhītinut //
283.d:
चक्रिणङ्गदिनञ्चैव शार्ङ्गिणं खड्गिनं स्मरेत् /
नारायणं सर्वकाले नृसिंहो ऽखिलभीतिनुत् //
283.m: One should remember the Holder of the Discus, the Mace-bearer, the Archer, and the Sword-bearer; / Nārāyaṇa at all times; Nṛsiṃha removes all fear.

283.s:
garuḍadhvajaś ca viṣahṛt vāsudevaṃ sadājapet /
dhānyādisthāpane svapne anantācyutamīrayet //
283.d:
गरुडध्वजश् च विषहृत् वासुदेवं सदाजपेत् /
धान्यादिस्थापने स्वप्ने अनन्ताच्युतमीरयेत् //
283.m: And "Garuḍadhvaja" removes poison; one should always recite "Vāsudeva." / When storing grains and the like, or in sleep, one should utter "Ananta" and "Acyuta."

283.s:
nārāyaṇañca duḥsvapne dāhādau jalaśāyinaṃ /
hayagrīvañca vidyārthī jagatsūtiṃ sutāptaye /
balabhadraṃ śaurakārye(1) ekaṃ nāmārthasādhakam(2) //
:e ity āgneye mahāpurāṇe mantrarūpauṣadhakathanaṃ nāma
tryaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
:ś atha caturaśītyadhikadviśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ
mṛtasañjīvanīkarasiddhayogaḥ
283.d:
नारायणञ्च दुःस्वप्ने दाहादौ जलशायिनं /
हयग्रीवञ्च विद्यार्थी जगत्सूतिं सुताप्तये /
बलभद्रं शौरकार्ये(1) एकं नामार्थसाधकम्(2) //
:ए इत्य् आग्नेये महापुराणे मन्त्ररूपौषधकथनं नाम
त्र्यशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
:श् अथ चतुरशीत्यधिकद्विशततमो ऽध्यायः
मृतसञ्जीवनीकरसिद्धयोगः
283.m:
And one should remember Nārāyaṇa in a bad dream; the One Who Sleeps on the Waters in burning and the like; / one desiring knowledge, Hayagrīva; the Origin of the World, for obtaining a son; / and Balabhadra in valiant deeds: each single name accomplishes its object.
Thus in the great Purāṇa of Agni, the two hundred and eighty-third chapter, called “Account of Remedies in the Form of Mantras.”
Now begins the two hundred and eighty-fourth chapter.
Proven Recipes That Revive the Dead.
